items.title: Hassan Sheikh Reaches Galmudug Side of Galkayo, but Somalia’s Political Divide Looms Large
items.description: Galkayo (WDN) —President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s arrival in Galkayo was presented as a celebration of peace, reconciliation and Somali unity. Yet the symbolism of his visit also exposed one of the most striking realities of Somalia’s political fragmentation: the country’s president can now visit only one half of a city that is physically united but politically divided. Hassan Sheikh and Galmudug President Ahmed Abdi Kariye “Qoorqoor” arrived in Galkayo from the southern, Galmudug-controlled side after traveling by road from Dhusamareb. They were welcomed at Abdullahi Issa Airport by thousands of residents, politicians, traditional elders, women and young people. The reception was reportedly warm, and the President used the occasion to praise Galkayo’s residents for overcoming the violence that once divided the city. But behind the celebrations lies a striking political reality. The President of Somalia did not cross into the Puntland side of Galkayo That is not simply a matter of geography. It is a reflection of the extraordinary political fragmentation that has developed during Hassan Sheikh’s presidency. Puntland severed political ties with the Federal Government amid deep disagreements over constitutional amendments, federal powers and the electoral process. Jubaland has likewise become embroiled in a bitter political confrontation with Mogadishu. President Farmajo, Abdiwali and Xaaf, Galkacyo As a result, Somalia’s president now faces a remarkable limitation: two of the country’s most important federal member states remain politically estranged from the government he leads. The contrast with Hassan Sheikh’s predecessor, former President Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed “Farmaajo,” could hardly be more striking. During Farmaajo’s presidency, the former president visited both sides of Galkayo, crossing the administrative divide between Puntland and Galmudug and presenting the city as a symbol of Somali unity despite its political differences. Today, Hassan Sheikh’s inability to visit the Puntland side of the same city has become a powerful symbol of how far Somalia’s political divisions have deepened. The physical boundary separating the two administrations may be little more than a line through a city. Politically, however, it increasingly resembles a national fault line. That symbolism has not escaped social media users. Some posts circulating online have mockingly portrayed Hassan Sheikh as a “Hawiye president,” suggesting that his inability to freely travel across federal territories has reinforced perceptions that his government is identified too closely with particular political or clan constituencies. Such claims are political opinions rather than established facts, but their circulation illustrates the depth of public frustration over Somalia’s worsening political divisions. A President Speaking About Unity from One Side of a Divided City During his address, Hassan Sheikh urged residents to protect the peace that has been achieved in Galkayo and prevent a return to the armed conflicts that once caused deaths, displacement and social fragmentation. He emphasized the importance of maintaining economic, cultural and social ties between the two sides of the city, arguing that Galkayo could serve as an example of how Somalis can overcome conflict and build lasting peace. The irony is difficult to ignore. The President was speaking about unity from the Galmudug side of a city whose other half remains under the authority of a federal state that has a deeply strained relationship with his government. The message was therefore both hopeful and revealing. Galkayo’s divisions mirror a much larger problem facing Somalia. The country has a federal system designed to distribute political authority between the central government and Federal Member States. Yet disagreements over the Constitution, elections, security structures and the balance of power have increasingly transformed that federal arrangement into a source of confrontation. Puntland’s political estrangement from Mogadishu has made presidential travel particularly sensitive. Jubaland’s confrontation with the Federal Government has created another major political divide. The result is a Somalia in which the president’s ability to move freely between regions can itself become a measure of national political cohesion. That is an extraordinary development for a country whose leaders routinely speak of national unity. Galkayo Still Offers a Different Possibility Yet there is another side to the story. Ordinary residents of Galkayo have continued to demonstrate that communities can maintain relationships even when politicians cannot. Families cross the divide. Businesses operate across it. Traders move between the two sides. Young people socialize together, and communities continue to share cultural and social ties. In that sense, Galkayo may still represent the Somalia that politicians have struggled to build: a country where borders are less important than relationships. Hassan Sheikh’s message that the people of Galkayo must protect their peace is therefore worth taking seriously. But national unity cannot ultimately be built through speeches alone. It requires political leaders who can sit together, negotiate constitutional disagreements and restore trust between Mogadishu and the Federal Member States. Until that happens, the image of Somalia’s president standing on one side of Galkayo while the other side remains politically out of reach will remain one of the most powerful symbols of the country’s unfinished political journey. Galkayo is one city. Its people increasingly behave like one community. The tragedy is that Somalia’s political leadership remains divided over who has the right to govern it. items.title: Guusha ugu weyn ee aan gaadhnay,waa in ay saqiirtay,wixii la odhan jiray Dowlada Fadaraalka Somaliya.
items.description: Guusha ugu weyn ee aan gaadhnay,waa in ay saqiirtay,wixii la oran jiray Dowlada Fadaraalka Somaliya. 1. Waxay lumisay aqoonsigii caalamiga ahaa. 2. Waxay lumisay aqoonsigii gudaha. Villa Somaliya,waxay noqotay Villa Muqdisho. Ninka fadhiya Villa-da,wuxuu noqday Oday Beeleed ama Gudoomiye Urur ama Madaxweyne Beeleed. Caawa,waxaa Galkacyo wada jooga Deni iyo Xasan oo midna maamulo Koonfurta,midna maamulo Puntland oo kala leh Laba Calan iyo Laba Dastuur. In DF burburto oo salka laga soo bilaabo,waa xalka kaliya ee maanta Somali uharsan,sababtoo ah si khaldan ayay ukabantay,waxayna ubaahan tahay in dib loo jabiyo oo si sax ah loo kabo. Waa ilaahay mahadii hadii Caawa Xasan oo Oday Qabiil ah oo aan lahayn maqaam kale uu Beeshiisa kula cawaynayo Baraxley. JQ.

items.title: DF: Sida Al-Shabaab loola diriro ayaa loola dagaalamaya maleeshiyaadka Lafta-gareen
items.description: Gaalkacyo (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya, Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo ka hadlay dagaalkii maanta ka dhacay magaalada Baydhabo ayaa sheegay inay dagaalkaas ka wada qeyb qaateen maleeshiyaad ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab iyo ciidanka taabacsan Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen oo isku milmay. Wasiirka ayaa si cad u sheegay in dowladda ay maleeshiyaadka taabacsan Lafta-gareen ay hadda kadib ula diriri doonto sida Al-Shabaab oo kale, maadaama ay ku biireen argagixisada, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Maleeshiyaadka argagixisada ku biiray ee Amniga iyo xasiloonida dadka Baydhabo carqadaynaya waxa ay la mid yihiin Al Shabaab waxaana loola dirirayaa sida Al Shabaab argagixisada ah loola diriro,” ayuu yiri Wasiir Fiqi. Sidoo kale, wasiirka ayaa ciidamada xoogga dalka ku amaanay in ay jabiyeen kooxaha weerarka soo qaaday maanta. “Dadka magaalada Baydhabo waa ku mahadsan yihiin in ay guryahooda u diideen kooxahaas argagixisada in ay ku dhuuntaan.” Waxa uu intaas kusii daray “Al Shabaab cid kasta oo shirko la noqota kama ab sokeeyaan, waxaan maantay caddayn loo doonayn in maleeshiyaadkii Lafta-gareen iyo kooxda Khawaarijta Al Shabaab ay isku milmeen. Saakay Labada gaari ee qaraxyada laga soo buuxiyay ee dagaalkii saakay lagu bilaabay waxay marag u tahay isku milankaas.” Wasaaradda Gaashaandhiga Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in howl-galka lagu dilay ugu yaraan illaa 30 ka tirsanaa ragga weerarka soo qaaday, isla markaana laga furtay hub iyo gaadiid dagaal. “Intii uu socday iska-horimaadka, ciidanka XDS ayaa nololsha ku qabtay qaar kamid ah maleeshiyaadkii weerarka soo qaadah. Ciidammada ayaa sidoo kale gacanta ku dhigay hub iyo gaadiid ay wateen kooxihii weerarka soo qaaday,” ayaa lagu yiri war-saxaafadeed kasoo baxay wasaaradda. Si kastaba, ma jiro wax hadal ah oo kasoo baxay dhanka kooxda Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen oo ku aadan eedeynta loo jeediyay kadib dagaalkii maanta ee Baydhabo, kaas oo dib loogu celiyay maleeshiyaadkii weerarka soo qaaday. items.title: Laftagareen oo bogaadiyay ciidamada weerarka ka gaystay Baydhabo
items.description: Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Laftagareen) oo weli ku adkeysanaya in uu yahay Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed ayaa bogaadiyay weerarka ay ciidamada taageersan maanta ku qaadeen Magaalada Baydhabo ee Xarunta Gobolka Baay. Waxa uu sheegay in Ciidanka Daraawiishta Koonfur Galbeed ay hawlgalo ka fuliyeen magaalada, si loo sugo amniga iyo xasilloonida. “Maanta oo ay taarikhdu tahay 17-ka Agosto 2026, Xafiiska Madaxweynaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya wuxuu bogaadinayaa hawlgalada ay Ciidanka Daraawiishta Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya ka fuliyeen Magaalada Baydhabo, kaas oo ujeedadoodu ahayd sugidda amniga, soo celinta xasilloonida iyo kala dambeynta magaalada.” Ayuu Cabdicasiis Laftagareen ku sheegay warqad qoraal ah oo caawa uu soo dhigay bartiisa Facebook. Laftagareen oo sheegay in hawlgalka lagu sifeynayay, waxa uu ku sheegay ciidamada sida gardarrada ah ugu soo duulay Magaalada Baydhabo ayaa dhanka kale beeniyay in taageereyaashiisa iyo maleeshiyada Al Shabaab ay si wadajir ah u weerareen magaaladaasi. “Hawlgalkan waxaa lagu sifeynayay ciidamada sida gardarrada ah ugu soo duulay deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed, gaar ahaan Magaalada Baydhabo. Dhammaan wararka sheegaya in Ciidanka Daraawiishta lagu tilmaamo koox xagjir ah waa warar marin habaabin ah oo been ah, kuwaas oo qiil loogu raadinayo in Madaxweynaha waqtigiisu dhamaaday Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu si sharci darro ah u isticmaalo qalabka Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed.” Ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka. Laftagareen ayaa qoraalka ku sheegay “Xafiiska Madaxweynaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya wuxuu bogaadinayaa Ciidanka Daraawiishta Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed guulaha ay ka soo hooyeen hawlgalka iyo sida ay uga go’an tahay difaaca shacabka, sugidda amniga iyo ilaalinta xasilloonida deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya. Madaxweynaha Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya wuxuu sidoo kale hambalyo u dirayaa shaacbka Koonfur Galbeed, sida diiran ee wanaagsan ee ay u soo dhaweeyeen Ciidanka Daraawiishta DKGS, u garab istaageen dib-u-xoreynta Magaalada Baydhabo.” Warka ayaa lagu soo geba-gabeeyay “Ugu dambayn, Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya waxay xaqiijineysaa inay ka go’an tahay ilaalinta nolosha iyo karaamada shacabka, difaaca dowladnimada iyo dhowrista hay’adaha dasuuriga ah ee Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed Somaliya.”

items.title: Madaxweynaha Somaliland  oo kulan la yeeshay gudiga Diwaangelinta ururada siyaasada
items.description: Madaxweynaha Somaliland oo kilan la yeeshay gudiga Diwaangelinta ururada siyaasada Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, Mudane Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), ayaa maanta kulan muhiim ah la yeeshay Guddida Diiwaangelinta Ururrada Siyaasadda iyo Ansixinta Axsaabta Qaranka JSL (GDUS&AAQ), kaas oo diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta hannaanka dimuqraadiyadda, ku-dhaqanka iyo kor-joogtaynta shuruucda iyo gudashada waajibaadka Qaran ee ay Guddidu u xil-saaran tahay. Guddidan oo ah Hay’ad Qaran oo madax-bannaan ayaa waxa ay u xil-saaran tahay diiwaangelinta, kormeerka, kobcinta, iyo xallinta khilaafaadka Axsaabta Qaranka iyo Ururrada Siyaasadda. Guddida Diiwaangelinta Ururada Siyaasadda iyo Ansixinta Axsaabta Qaranka ayaa Madaxweynaha ugu xog waramay halka ay marayso shaqada guddidu, qorshaha mustaqbalka dhow iyo kan fog, iyo caqabadaha jira. Intii uu kulanku socday, xubnaha Guddida ayaa Madaxweynaha warbixin faah-faahsan ka siiyey hawlaha uga qabsoomay dhinacyada kala duwan ee nidaamka diimoqraadiyadda iyo axsaabta badan ee dalka, waxa ayna Madaxweynaha gudoonsiiyeen Qorshahooda Istraatejiyadda (Strategic Plan) ee sannadaha 2025 – 2026. Sidoo kale, Guddidu waxa ay Madaxweynaha la wadaagtay qorshaha dhow ee ah Casriyeynta hawl-qabadka Guddida oo ay ka mid tahay in dhammaan xogta ay kaydiso Guddidu laga dhigi doono mid electronic ah (Digital Data Base), qorshaha samaynta ‘Democracy Academy’, Qorshaha Dib-u-habaynta Diimoqraadiyadda, Dhiirigelinta ka-qayb-galka loo dhanyahay ee Diimoqraadiyadda, kobcinta Axsaabta Siyaasadda, iyo islaxisaabtanka iyo daahfurnaanta. Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland ayaa Guddida Diiwaangelinta Ururrada Siyaasadda iyo Ansixinta Axsaabta Qaranka ku bogaadiyey dedaalka iyo masuuliyadda ay Qaranka u hayaan, isaga oo ku boorriyey in ay dardargeliyaan oo ay dhammaystiraan hawlaha muhiimka ah ee horyaalla. Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland waxa uu Guddida u xaqiijiyey in Xukuumaddu ay garab taagan tahay Hay’addan Qaran ee u xilsaaran ilaalinta iyo horumarinta dimuqraadiyadda, isaga oo ku adkeeyey in ay si daacadnimo iyo xilkasnimo leh u gutaan waajibaadkooda, si loo sii xoojiyo dhaqanka dimuqraadiyadeed ee Somaliland iyo kalsoonida shacabka ee hay’adaha Qaranka.

items.title: Faah-faahinta markab maanta lagu afduubtay biyaha Soomaaliya
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Markab xamuul ah ayaa lagu afduubtay meel ka baxsan xeebaha Soomaaliya, kadib markii koox hubeysan ay u suuragashay inay fuusho markabka oo ay la wareegto gacan-ku-hayntiisa. Hay’adda Hawl-gallada Ganacsiga Badda ee UK (UKMTO) ayaa sheegtay in dhacdadu ay dhacday Isniintii, iyadoo soo saartay digniin ku aaddan xaaladda amni ee markabka iyo nawaaxiga xeebaha Soomaaliya. Sida lagu sheegay warbixinta UKMTO, dhacdadu waxay ka dhacday qiyaastii afar mayl-badeed koonfur kaga beegan xeebaha Soomaaliya. Sarkaalka amniga ee shirkadda markabka ayaa hay’adda u sheegay in siddeed nin oo hubeysan oo aan fasax u haysan inay markabka fuulaan ay gudaha u galeen, kadibna ay gacanta ku dhigeen markabka. Ilaa hadda ma cadda cidda iska leh markabka la afduubtay iyo halka uu ku wajahnaa, iyadoo UKMTO aysan bixin faahfaahin dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan markabka ama kooxda qabsatay. Xeebaha Soomaaliya ayaa muddo dheer ahaa goob ay ka dhici jireen weerarro burcad-badeednimo, gaar ahaan intii u dhaxeysay 2008 iyo 2018, xilligaas oo maraakiib badan lagu afduubtay. Inkasta oo tallaabooyin amni iyo iskaashi caalami ah ay horseedeen hoos u dhac weyn oo ku yimid falalka burcad-badeednimada, haddana weerarro iyo afduubyo cusub ayaa dib uga soo muuqday xeebaha Soomaaliya dhammaadkii 2023. Dhacdadan cusub ayaa sare u qaadaysa walaaca laga qabo in burcad-badeednimadu ay mar kale ku soo xoogeysanayso xeebaha Soomaaliya, iyadoo hay’adaha amniga iyo kuwa maraakiibta ay si dhow ula socdaan xaaladda. items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Audit records and Documents reviewed by Daily Somalia raise serious questions over procurement, contracting and oversight at Somalia’s Civil Aviation Authority
items.description: MOGADISHU — Official audit records and supporting documents reviewed by Daily Somalia raise serious questions over procurement practices, private contracting and administrative controls within Somalia’s Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA), as the government continues to promote plans for rebuilding the country’s aviation sector. At the centre of the documents is a finding by the Office of the Auditor General that the Civil Aviation Authority entered into procurement agreements worth a combined $2,073,376.56 without registering them with the Auditor General’s office. The audit states that failure to register government contracts undermines transparency, accountability and the Auditor General’s ability to scrutinize public expenditure. The 2025 federal audit explains that the Auditor General is legally mandated to verify government contracts, monitor financial transactions and assess whether public institutions comply with Somalia’s financial-management and procurement laws. One company appearing in the aviation authority’s procurement records is One Complete Services Ltd, which is listed against a $12,532 contract. Documents reviewed by Daily Somalia show the company was registered on 10 October 2022. A commercial licence issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry identifies its business activity as “Facilities and Maintenance” and lists its address in Taleex, Hodan, Mogadishu. Daily Somalia has also received information alleging that the company, represented by Younis Mohamed Noor, became involved in additional services for the Civil Aviation Authority. The available audit record confirms the specific contract appearing in the document. It does not, on its own, establish the full value or extent of any wider business relationship between the company and SCAA. That distinction matters. What now requires scrutiny is whether additional contracts existed, how they were awarded, how much was paid, whether competitive procurement procedures were followed and whether any official connected to the Authority had a personal or financial interest in the arrangements. Questions for SCAA leadership The findings raise direct accountability questions for the management of the Civil Aviation Authority under Director General Ahmed Moallim Hassan. Somalia’s Auditor General states that directors-general and other senior officials of federal institutions are responsible for maintaining effective internal controls, managing financial risks and making sure government transactions comply with applicable laws. The central question is therefore not simply whether services were delivered. It is whether public contracts were awarded, registered, paid and supervised according to the law. Millions in airport revenue also questioned The latest federal audit identifies another major issue involving Somalia’s aviation sector. Under the concession agreement governing Aden Adde International Airport, the Federal Government is entitled to 25% of the gross revenue earned by Favori LLC, the private company operating the airport. According to the Auditor General, Favori reported approximately $29.71 million in revenue during 2025. That should have generated around $7.43 million for the Somali government. Government financial records, however, showed receipts of only about $4.15 million, leaving an audited difference of approximately $3.27 million. The Auditor General said the missing amount affected the completeness and accuracy of the government’s reported concession revenue. This finding concerns the government-Favori concession and should not be attributed to SCAA without further evidence. But it exposes another weakness in the financial controls surrounding one of Somalia’s most important public assets. Security questions at the airport Daily Somalia has separately received allegations involving the construction of an airport gate and an intervention by security authorities. Sources allege that the gate was constructed without the required prior coordination with relevant security agencies and was later closed following intervention by the National Intelligence and Security Agency, NISA. Further claims concern what happened following the closure, including an alleged dispute involving the private company representative and security services at the Authority. Daily Somalia has not independently verified these claims and is reporting them as allegations, not established facts. Given the security sensitivity of Aden Adde International Airport, the issue warrants an official investigation capable of determining who authorized the construction, which company performed the work, whether security approval existed and what actions followed NISA’s intervention. Allegations of exclusive access Daily Somalia has also received claims that foreign aviation companies operating in Somalia were directed to use services provided by a particular private company. No finding of wrongdoing can be made without examining the written instructions, contracts and relevant procurement records. If the allegation is substantiated, however, authorities would need to explain the legal basis for restricting companies to one provider and whether such an arrangement complied with procurement and competition rules. Ageing aviation systems There are also unresolved questions surrounding Somalia’s aviation infrastructure and the replacement of ageing technical systems. Information reviewed by Daily Somalia indicates that significant aviation equipment was inherited through earlier international aviation-management arrangements rather than purchased recently by the Federal Government. An accountable aviation authority should be able to publicly establish what safety-critical equipment is currently operating, when it was acquired, its expected operational lifespan, maintenance costs, replacement schedules and the procurement process for new systems. These are not minor administrative questions. They concern the systems responsible for managing aircraft moving through Somali airspace. What the evidence shows, and what it does not Daily Somalia’s review identifies two categories of information. Documented findings include: the Auditor General’s concerns over unregistered contracts, the listed $12,532 One Complete Services contract, and the approximately $3.27 million discrepancy in the government’s expected Favori concession revenue. The Auditor General’s broader 2025 review also examined compliance across 22 federal institutions, focusing specifically on procurement, personnel, assets and internal government controls. Other claims concerning additional contracts, the airport gate, security intervention and alleged exclusive service arrangements remain allegations requiring further evidence and official investigation. Daily Somalia will not present allegations as proven misconduct. But documented audit concerns cannot be dismissed simply because other parts of the case remain under investigation. The public deserves to know who received aviation contracts, how those contracts were awarded, what services were delivered, how much public money was paid, and who authorized the decisions. Questions have also emerged over the tenure and term limits of SCAA’s senior leadership, including Director General Ahmed Moallim Hassan. Greater clarity is needed on the legal duration of the Director General’s mandate, the date of his appointment, and whether any renewal or extension has been formally authorized. Publication of the relevant appointment decisions and legal provisions would help establish whether the current leadership remains within its prescribed mandate. Appointed acting head in 2018 and permanently confirmed on June 22, 2020, the Director General of the Somali Civil Aviation Authority has led the agency for eight years. Although Law No. 28 limits the term to four years renewable once, his mandate expired in June 2024. He remains in office despite changes in leadership and the expiration of his second term. This situation persists because Article 16(2) omits mandate expiration from the legal grounds for vacating office, attaching no consequences to a lapsed term. Without explicit provisions declaring the post vacant or requiring a succession process, enforcement relies entirely on executive discretion. Consequently, an aligned leadership can silently bypass term limits, leaving the regulator of sovereign airspace operating without a valid statutory mandate. Information reviewed by Daily Somalia indicates that significant aviation equipment was inherited through earlier international aviation-management arrangements rather than purchased recently by the Federal Government. An accountable aviation authority should be able to publicly establish what safety-critical equipment is currently operating, when it was acquired, its expected operational lifespan, maintenance costs, replacement schedules and the procurement process for new systems. These are not minor administrative questions. They concern the systems responsible for managing aircraft moving through Somali airspace. What the evidence shows, and what it does not Daily Somalia’s review identifies two categories of information. Documented findings include: the Auditor General’s concerns over unregistered contracts, the listed $12,532 One Complete Services contract, and the approximately $3.27 million discrepancy in the government’s expected Favori concession revenue. The Auditor General’s broader 2025 review also examined compliance across 22 federal institutions, focusing specifically on procurement, personnel, assets and internal government controls. Other claims concerning additional contracts, the airport gate, security intervention and alleged exclusive service arrangements remain allegations requiring further evidence and official investigation. Daily Somalia will not present allegations as proven misconduct. But documented audit concerns cannot be dismissed simply because other parts of the case remain under investigation. The public deserves to know who received aviation contracts, how those contracts were awarded, what services were delivered, how much public money was paid, and who authorized the decisions. Questions have also emerged over the tenure and term limits of SCAA’s senior leadership, including Director General Ahmed Moallim Hassan. Greater clarity is needed on the legal duration of the Director General’s mandate, the date of his appointment, and whether any renewal or extension has been formally authorized. Publication of the relevant appointment decisions and legal provisions would help establish whether the current leadership remains within its prescribed mandate. Appointed acting head in 2018 and permanently confirmed on June 22, 2020, the Director General of the Somali Civil Aviation Authority has led the agency for eight years. Although Law No. 28 limits the term to four years renewable once, his mandate expired in June 2024. He remains in office despite changes in leadership and the expiration of his second term. This situation persists because Article 16(2) omits mandate expiration from the legal grounds for vacating office, attaching no consequences to a lapsed term. Without explicit provisions declaring the post vacant or requiring a succession process, enforcement relies entirely on executive discretion. Consequently, an aligned leadership can silently bypass term limits, leaving the regulator of sovereign airspace operating without a valid statutory mandate. items.title: Somalia president calls for AU peacekeepers to leave
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud declared on Sunday that Somalia no longer needs foreign peacekeepers to guarantee its own security, telling African Union troops it was time to go home even as the continental mission they serve in faces the most serious funding crisis of its two-decade history. “We have reached a point where we can now take full charge of our security. Let’s give African peacekeepers a bunch of flowers and send them home,” Mohamud said, speaking in Somalia’s central Galmudug state. The president made the remarks at a graduation ceremony marking the passing-out of roughly 3,000 newly trained Somali National Army soldiers – the largest single graduating class the country has produced since the collapse of its central government in 1991. The recruits, drawn from across Somalia, completed a full year of training in basic soldiering, military discipline and combat tactics. The graduation was delivered under a defence cooperation agreement Somalia signed with Saudi Arabia in February, through which Riyadh committed to training approximately 5,000 Somali soldiers; Sunday’s cohort accounts for the bulk of that pledge delivered in a single intake. Training took place at Hanan Bure in the Galgaduud region, a site Saudi military officials visited repeatedly over the course of the year to monitor progress. Instruction was delivered by foreign military personnel from Romania, Ukraine, Sudan and other countries — a composition some regional reporting has separately described as also drawing on trainers from South Africa and Colombia. Mohamud cast the graduation as proof of Somalia’s broader recovery, describing it as testament to the reconstruction of the country’s national army. A drawdown already under way The president’s call comes only days after Ethiopian troops serving under the African Union handed over their forward operating base in the southern Somali town of Burhakaba to Somali government forces, part of a phased drawdown already reshaping the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia, AUSSOM, and its predecessor missions. AUSSOM, which succeeded the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS) on January 1, 2025, was itself designed around a gradual handover of security responsibility to Somali forces, continuing a process that began with the earlier AMISOM deployment in 2007. Somali authorities have said their forces assumed control of 23 former AU forward operating bases between January 2023 and April 2025. But the mission Mohamud is now urging out the door is also fighting for its own survival. AUSSOM’s current mandate expires on December 31, and the mission depends heavily on the UN Support Office in Somalia, UNSOS, for fuel, transport, medical care and other logistics. Washington has told the African Union it will not support renewing that UN logistical arrangement beyond the current mandate – while stopping short of blocking a renewal of AUSSOM’s mandate itself, provided an alternative source of logistical funding can be found. Somali officials are reported to be pressing Gulf states to help finance continued AU protection of key towns and infrastructure once the current arrangement lapses, though neither Mogadishu nor any Arab government has publicly confirmed such talks. A more crowded security picture, not a simpler one Mohamud’s invitation to African peacekeepers to leave does not mean Somalia is moving toward a purely national security posture. Turkey has built one of the most extensive bilateral military relationships in Mogadishu’s history, running training programmes through Camp TURKSOM since 2017 that have produced thousands of soldiers, including elite Gorgor commando units, and maintaining a troop presence its parliament has authorised to grow as large as 2,500. The United States continues to provide intelligence, training and air support. Egypt has joined the AU deployment itself, while Uganda and Ethiopia maintain forces in Somalia outside their formal AU commitments. The effect is a security architecture fragmenting from one dominant multinational African force into several parallel bilateral partnerships – with Saudi Arabia’s training programme now added to a list that already includes Turkey, the United States, Egypt, the UAE and others. A federal dispute in the background The president’s appearance in Galmudug carries political weight beyond the security announcement. His visit has sharpened tensions with neighbouring Puntland, which has placed its own security forces on alert and accused the federal government of stoking instability around Galkayo, a city split along the Puntland-Galmudug boundary. A stronger federal security presence in Galmudug would bolster Mogadishu’s hand in its wider standoff with more autonomous regional administrations, making Sunday’s graduation as much a marker in Somalia’s internal balance of power as in its relationship with foreign forces. items.title: Madaxweynaha Puntland oo la kulmay Saraakiisha Ciidamada ee Gobolka Mudug
items.description: Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Puntland, Siciid Cabdullaahi Maxamed (Deni) oo booqasho ku jooga Magaalada Gaalkacyo ayaa caawa waqooyiga magaaladaasi kula kulmay Saraakiisha Ciidamada Puntland ee Gobolka Mudug. Madaxweynaha ayaa waxaa kulanka ku wehlinayay xubno ka mid ah Goleyaasha Dowlad Goboleedka Puntland iyo Taliyaha Ciidanka Daraawiishta Puntland, General Aadan Cabdi Xaashi, sida lagu sheegay qoraal la soo dhigay bogga wararka ee Madaxtooyada Puntland. Qoraalka laguma sheegin waxa uu Madaxweynuhu kala hadlay Saraakiisha Ciidamada Qalabka Sida ee ka hawlgala Gobolka Mudug, balse waxa uu kulankan imanaya, wax yar uun ka dib, markii Madaxweye Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu gaaray koonfurta Gaalkacyo oo Galmudug ay maamusho. Dowlad Goboleedka Puntland ayaa horey uga digtay safarka Madaxweynaha Dowladda Federaalka ee Gaalkacyo, iyadoo ku andacooneysa in uu uga gol leeyahay in uu colaad cusub kaga huriyo deegaanada Puntland, gaar ahaan Gaalkacyo. Saraakiisha Ciidamada Puntland ayaa Axaddii sheegay in la xiray xuduudaha Puntland, si looga hortago waxa ay ku sheegeen sharta Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud. Puntland ayaa ciidamo fara-badan ku soo daadisay waddooyinka xaafadaha ku yaala waqooyiga Gaalkacyo, taas oo keentay in Galmudug ay dhinaceeda gasho xaalad feejignaan ah. Dhaqdhaqaaqyada ciidan ee ka soo cusboonaaday labada qaybood ee Gaalkacyo ayaa xaddiday isu socodka shacabka ee magaalada.

items.title: Toddobo Tahriibe oo ku Dhintay Badda Liibiya iyo 50 Soomaali iyo Masaari ah oo la Badbaadiyay
items.description: TRIPOLI, Goobjoog — Toddobo qof ayaa ku dhintay safar tahriib oo ay kaga gudbayeen Badda Dhexe, halka 50 kale oo u dhashay Soomaaliya iyo Masar laga badbaadiyay doon alwaax ah oo ku jirtay biyaha caalamiga ah ee ka baxsan xeebaha Liibiya, sida ay maanta sheegtay hay’adda samafalka caafimaadka ee EMERGENCY. Markabka samatabbixinta Life Support, oo ay maamusho EMERGENCY, ayaa subaxnimadii Isniinta helay doonta oo ku jirtay aagga baadigoobka iyo samatabbixinta ee Liibiya. Toddoba qof ayaa dhintay intii safarku socday, halka laba ka mid ah dadka la badbaadiyey ay xaaladdoodu aad u liidato, iyagoo la ildaran neefqabatin una baahan in si degdeg ah loo daadgureeyo si ay daryeel caafimaad u helaan. Dadka badbaaday ayaa sheegay inay waaberigii 16ka Agoosto ka soo shiraacdeen magaalada xeebeedka Zuwara ee galbeedka Liibiya. EMERGENCY waxay sheegtay in dadka doonta saarnaa ay asal ahaan ka soo jeedaan Soomaaliya iyo Masar, inkasta oo aan weli si gaar ah loo shaacin tirada Soomaalida iyo Masaarida mid kasta. Kontonka qof ee la badbaadiyey waxay ka kooban yihiin 45 rag ah iyo shan dumar ah. Waxa si gaar ah walaac u leh in 29 ka mid ahi yihiin carruur aan cid weyn oo masuul ka ahi la socon; 26 waa wiilal, saddexna waa gabdho, sida ay EMERGENCY sheegtay. Hay’addu waxay masuuliyiinta ka codsatay in markabka loo qoondeeyo deked ammaan ah oo dhow, hasayeeshee markii danbe waxaa loo asteeyey Bari, oo ku taalla koonfurta Talyaaniga, si dadka la soo badbaadiyay halkaas looga dejiyo. Ilaa hadda lama shaacin da’da iyo jinsiyadaha toddobada qof ee geeriyooday, mana cadda inta ay Soomaalidu ka yihiin dadka dhintay ama kuwa xaaladdoodu halista tahay. Reuters waxay sheegtay in EMERGENCY aanay faahfaahin dheeraad ah ka bixin xaaladda labada qof ee u baahan daadguraynta caafimaad ee degdegga ah. Dhacdadan ayaa, mar kale, muujinaysa khatarta sii kordhaysa ee marinbiyoodka bartamaha Badda Dhexe, oo ah jidka ay tahriibayaal badan uga gudbaan Liibiya iyagoo iskudayaya inay gaaraan Yurub. Hay’adda Caalamiga ah ee Socdaalka ee IOM ayaa dhowaan sheegtay in 821 qof ay ku dhinteen ama ku lumeen marinbiyoodka Bartamaha Badda Dhexe (Mediterranean Sea) sannadkan 2026, xilli tirada dadka jidkan ku gaaraya Yurub ay hoos u dhacday. IOM waxay marinbiyoodkan ku tilmaantaa jidka socdaalka ee dunida ugu dhimashada badan ee la diiwaangeliyay. Xogta IOM waxay, sidoo kale, muujinaysaa in tan iyo 2014 ugu yaraan 25,859 qof ay ku dhinteen ama ku lumeen marinbiyoodka Bartamaha Badda Dhexe (Mediterranean Sea), taas oo muujinaysa in dhimashada badda ay sii socoto inkasta oo isbeddello lagu arkayo tirada dadka tahriibka ku socda. Liibiya ayaa sannado badan ahayd marin weyn oo ay isticmaalaan dadka Afrika iyo meelo kale ka soo hayaamaya ee doonaya inay gaaraan Yurub. Zuwara, oo ah halka ay kooxdan cusub ka soo baxday, waxay ku taallaa xeebta galbeed ee Liibiya, waana mid ka mid ah meelaha laga bilaabo safarrada halista badan ee loo maro Badda Dhexe (Mediterranean Sea). Dhacdadan ayaa si gaar ah Soomaaliya u khusaysa, maadaama dadka la badbaadiyay ay ku jiraan muwaadiniin Soomaaliyeed, isla markaana ku dhowaad saddex-meelood laba meel carruurta kooxdan ka mid ahi ay safarka ku jireen iyagoo aan waalid ama qof weyn oo masuul ka ahi la socon. Ilaa fiidnimadii caawa, Dawladda Federaalka ah ee Soomaaliya kama aysan hadlin dhacdadan, mana jiro war rasmi ah oo sheegaya tirada saxda ah ee muwaadiniinta Soomaaliyeed ee ku jira dadka la badbaadiyay ama haddii Soomaali ay ka mid yihiin toddobada qof ee geeriyooday.

items.title: Markab Xamuul oo lagu Afduubtay Xeebaha Soomaaliya
items.description: MUQDISHO, Goobjoog — Markab xamuul ayaa galabnimadii maanta lagu afduubtay meel u dhow xeebaha Soomaaliya, kaddib markii siddeed nin oo hubaysan ay fuuleen markabka oo ay la wareegeen, sida ay sheegtay hay’adda UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). Dhacdada ayaa la soo sheegay abbaaraha 11:36 UTC, oo ku beegan 2:36 galabnimo waqtiga Soomaaliya, waxayna ka dhacday qiyaastii afar mayl-badeed meel koonfur ka xigta degaanka Mareeyo ee xeebaha Soomaaliya. UKMTO ayaa sheegtay in xogta dhacdada ay ka heshay sarkaalka amniga ee shirkadda markabka. Nimanka hubaysan ayaa markii ay markabka fuuleen kaddib la wareegay gacan-ku-hayntiisa. Hay’adaha amniga badda ayaa baaraya dhacdada, halka xaaladda shaqaalaha markabka aan ilaa hadda si rasmi ah loo xaqiijin. UKMTO ma aysan shaacin magaca markabka, hasayeeshee shirkadda amniga badda ee Vanguard Tech ayaa sheegtay in markabka la afduubtay uu yahay Lutuf, oo ah markab xamuul oo ka diiwaangashan Cameroon. Xogta Equasis ee ay soo xigatay Seatrade Maritime News ayaa muujinaysa in markabka la sameeyay 1995, awooddiisa culaysqaadka guudna ay tahay 1,401 tan. Dhacdadan cusub ayaa timid xilli walaac isa soo taraya laga muujinayo dibusookordhidda falalka burcadbadeednimada ee xeebaha Soomaaliya. Xarunta Iskuduwidda Macluumaadka Badaha ee JMIC waxay 16kii Agoosto qiimaynteeda halista maraakiibta ku sheegtay mid dhexdhexaad ah, iyadoo tilmaantay inay weli jiraan weerarro fursadraac ah oo ka dhacaya xeebaha Soomaaliya. JMIC waxay sheegtay in ilaa 16kii Agoosto afar markab oo ganacsi ay gacanta ugu jireen kooxo burcadbadeed Soomaali ah: Honour 25, oo la afduubtay 21kii Abriil; Sward, oo la qabsaday 26kii Abriil; Eureka, oo la afduubtay 2dii Maajo; iyo Asana, oo gacanta lagu dhigay 17kii Luulyo. Haddii xogta markabka Lutuf si buuxda loo xaqiijiyo, wuxuu noqonayaa markabkii shanaad ee taxanahan cusub lagu daro. Ilaa hadda lama shaacin tirada iyo jinsiyadaha hawlwadeennada saaran Lutuf, nooca xamuulka uu sido, halka ay afduubayaashu ula dhaqaaqeen iyo haddii uu jiro dalab madaxfurasho ah.

UKMTO ayaa sheegtay in xogta dhacdada ay ka heshay sarkaalka amniga ee shirkadda markabka. Nimanka hubaysan ayaa markii ay markabka fuuleen kaddib la wareegay gacan-ku-hayntiisa. Hay’adaha amniga badda ayaa baaraya dhacdada, halka xaaladda shaqaalaha markabka aan ilaa hadda si rasmi ah loo xaqiijin. UKMTO ma aysan shaacin magaca markabka, hasayeeshee shirkadda amniga badda ee Vanguard Tech ayaa sheegtay in markabka la afduubtay uu yahay Lutuf, oo ah markab xamuul oo ka diiwaangashan Cameroon. Xogta Equasis ee ay soo xigatay Seatrade Maritime News ayaa muujinaysa in markabka la sameeyay 1995, awooddiisa culaysqaadka guudna ay tahay 1,401 tan. Dhacdadan cusub ayaa timid xilli walaac isa soo taraya laga muujinayo dibusookordhidda falalka burcadbadeednimada ee xeebaha Soomaaliya. Xarunta Iskuduwidda Macluumaadka Badaha ee JMIC waxay 16kii Agoosto qiimaynteeda halista maraakiibta ku sheegtay mid dhexdhexaad ah, iyadoo tilmaantay inay weli jiraan weerarro fursadraac ah oo ka dhacaya xeebaha Soomaaliya. JMIC waxay sheegtay in ilaa 16kii Agoosto afar markab oo ganacsi ay gacanta ugu jireen kooxo burcadbadeed Soomaali ah: Honour 25, oo la afduubtay 21kii Abriil; Sward, oo la qabsaday 26kii Abriil; Eureka, oo la afduubtay 2dii Maajo; iyo Asana, oo gacanta lagu dhigay 17kii Luulyo. Haddii xogta markabka Lutuf si buuxda loo xaqiijiyo, wuxuu noqonayaa markabkii shanaad ee taxanahan cusub lagu daro. Ilaa hadda lama shaacin tirada iyo jinsiyadaha hawlwadeennada saaran Lutuf, nooca xamuulka uu sido, halka ay afduubayaashu ula dhaqaaqeen iyo haddii uu jiro dalab madaxfurasho ah.

items.title: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Baidoa as Rival Forces Battle for Control of Southwest Capital
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — Heavy fighting has erupted inside Baidoa, transforming the capital of South West State into the latest and most dramatic flashpoint in Somalia’s deepening political and security crisis. The clashes are reportedly pitting forces loyal to former South West State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed “Laftagareen” against forces aligned with the Federal Government of Somalia and supporting the administration led by Aden Mohamed Nur (Aden Madoobe). Fighting erupts, Baidoa, the interim capital of SW The intensity of the fighting has stunned residents, with reports of heavy gunfire and powerful explosions reverberating across different parts of the city. A spokesman for the Southwest administration aligned with Laftagareen claimed that his forces had captured parts of Baidoa, describing the operation as a “liberation struggle” and calling on residents to support the forces carrying out the offensive. A spokesman for Laftagareen’s forces also warned that troops deployed from Mogadishu would suffer defeat, referring to the expected confrontation as “Salbalaar.” The claims could not be independently verified. Meanwhile, residents reported sustained exchanges of heavy weapons and explosions in several areas of the city, underscoring the seriousness of the confrontation and the rapidly deteriorating security situation. Federal Government forces supporting the administration headed by Aden Madoobe are reportedly continuing to resist the assault. The battle has placed Baidoa at the center of an increasingly dangerous confrontation in which political disputes over leadership and legitimacy have spilled directly onto the streets. Neither the Federal Government nor the administration led by Aden Madoobe has issued a detailed official statement confirming the latest developments or providing verified information on casualties, territorial changes or the scale of the fighting. A City Caught in a Political Storm For now, Baidoa remains tense, with conflicting accounts emerging from the battlefield and independent verification proving difficult. The fighting represents more than another armed confrontation in Somalia. Baidoa is the political and administrative heart of South-west State, and any prolonged battle for control of the city could have consequences far beyond its streets. What is unfolding is therefore being watched with growing alarm: a political struggle that once played out through speeches, negotiations and competing claims of legitimacy has now erupted into open armed confrontation inside one of Somalia’s most important regional capitals. As gunfire continues to echo through Baidoa, the central question is no longer simply who controls the city—but whether Somalia’s political disputes can still be resolved through politics before the battlefield becomes the country’s principal negotiating table. items.title: Kumanaan qof oo isugu soo baxay Gaalkacyo kadib tegista Xasan Sheekh + Sawirro
items.description: Gaalkacyo (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud iyo wafdi uu hoggaaminayay ayaa si diiran loogu soo dhoweeyay isku soo bax ballaaran oo ka dhacay garoonka kubadda cagta Cabdullaahi Ciise ee magaalada Gaalkacyo. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa ku ammaanay shacabka reer Gaalkacyo sida ay xoogga u saareen ilaalinta midnimada iyo wadajirka dhexdooda ah, isagoo ugu baaqay in ay awooddooda isugu geeyaan adkeynta nabadda, dib u heshiisiinta bulshada iyo garab istaagga dowladnimada Soomaaliyeed. Madaxweynaha ayaa uga mahadceliyay shacabka reer Gaalkacyo soo dhaweynta heerkeedu sarreeyo ee ay u fidiyeen isaga iyo wafdigiisa, waxa uuna xusay in Gaalkacyo ay tahay magaalo mideysa shacabka Soomaaliyeed loona baahanyahay in laga gudbo wax weliba oo kala qaybsanaan ah. Booqashada Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ee magaalada Gaalkacyo ayaa qayb ka ah safarkiisa shaqo ee nabadda iyo u kuur-galka nolosha bulshada qaar ka mid ah deegaanada dowlad goboleedka Galmudug. Ka hor imaatinka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ee Gaalkacyo, Puntland ayaa si weyn u adkeysay ammaanka dhinaceeda magaalada Gaalkacyo, iyadoo la hakiyay isku-socodka labada dhinac ee magaalada. Maamulka ayaa socdaalka madaxweynaha ku tilmaantay mid abuuri kara qalalaase, waxayna heegan gelisay ciidamadeeda. Xasan Sheekh iyo madaxda Dowladda Federaalka ayaa xilligan ku guda jira abaabul siyaasadeed oo la xiriira doorashada Galmudug, gaar ahaan ololaha JSP, iyadoo dowladda ay sidoo kale waddo abaabul ciidan oo ay sheegtay in looga gol leeyahay la-dagaallanka kooxda Al-Shabaab. Magaalada Gaalkacyo waxaa sidoo kale ku sugan Madaxweynaha Puntland Saciid Cabdullaahi Deni, kaas oo halkaasi ka wada kulamo uu la yeelanayo bulshada iyo dhinacyada siyaasadda, xilli uu sii xoogeysanayo khilaafka siyaasadeed ee u dhexeeya Puntland iyo Dowladda Federaalka. items.title: Somaliland Signals Diplomatic Restraint Over UN Visit to Las Anod
items.description: Hargeisa (WDN) — Somaliland has adopted a notably measured diplomatic posture following a visit to Las Anod by a United Nations delegation, acknowledging the mission while strongly implying that the visit was undertaken with the knowledge and approval of Somaliland authorities. In a statement issued in English, Somaliland’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it remained committed to facilitating humanitarian assistance, but emphasized that visits of this nature should be conducted through established diplomatic channels and in coordination with Somaliland. “We remain committed to facilitating humanitarian assistance. However, visits of this nature must follow established diplomatic protocols and be coordinated with the Somaliland authorities,” the ministry said. The carefully worded statement appears to serve two purposes. On the one hand, Somaliland sought to avoid confrontation with the United Nations and reaffirm its willingness to facilitate humanitarian operations. On the other, its reference to established diplomatic procedures appears designed to signal that Hargeisa was aware of—and, by implication, had given the necessary clearance for—the UN delegation’s visit to Las Anod. Although the statement does not explicitly say that Somaliland formally authorized the visit, its wording strongly suggests that Hargeisa considers itself an authority whose consent or coordination is required for international missions operating in the disputed area. Diplomatic Message Behind the Statement The distinction is politically significant. Las Anod is currently administered by the Northeast State, which is aligned with Somalia’s Federal Government and rejects Somaliland’s claim to sovereignty over Sool and surrounding territories. Somaliland, however, continues to regard the region as part of its territory. By stressing coordination with Somaliland authorities, Hargeisa appears to be reinforcing its longstanding diplomatic position without directly challenging the UN delegation or obstructing humanitarian engagement. The approach represents a relatively restrained response to an issue that could easily have triggered a sharper political confrontation. Rather than accusing the United Nations of violating its territorial claims, Somaliland has chosen to emphasize diplomatic protocol and humanitarian cooperation. This allows Hargeisa to assert its position while maintaining working relations with international organizations. Las Anod at the Center of Competing Claims The UN visit comes amid an increasingly complicated political and humanitarian environment in Las Anod. Since Somaliland forces withdrew from the city following intense fighting in 2023, Las Anod has emerged as the political center of the North Eastern State, which has subsequently strengthened its relationship with Mogadishu. The competing claims have turned the city into one of the most politically sensitive locations in the Horn of Africa. For international organizations, the situation creates a delicate balancing act. Humanitarian agencies must maintain access to communities in need while navigating competing claims of authority from Somaliland, the Federal Government of Somalia and the North Eastern State administration. Somaliland’s latest statement appears to recognize that reality while making clear that it expects international actors to maintain formal diplomatic engagement with Hargeisa. Northeast State Yet to Respond The Northeast State administration has not yet publicly responded to Somaliland’s statement or clarified its position regarding the UN delegation’s visit. The absence of an immediate response leaves an important question unanswered: Was the UN mission coordinated solely with the authorities in Las Anod, or did Somaliland’s authorities formally provide the clearance they now appear to suggest? For now, Somaliland’s diplomatic language is significant precisely because it stops short of making an explicit claim of authorization while nevertheless conveying that the mission was not entirely outside Hargeisa’s diplomatic framework. The episode once again demonstrates the extraordinary complexity surrounding Las Anod, where humanitarian access, territorial claims and competing political authorities increasingly intersect. For Somaliland, the message appears clear: humanitarian assistance should not be politicized, but international engagement in the disputed territory should also recognize Hargeisa’s claimed authority and diplomatic standing. items.title: Shock and despair in Mogadishu as Hundreds of Poor Families Face Eviction in Waaberi
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Shock and despair are spreading through the Buulo Eelaay neighborhood of Waaberi district, where hundreds of mostly low-income families say they have been ordered to leave homes they have occupied for decades, amid fears that bulldozers could soon arrive to demolish the properties. Residents say they were given only a few days to vacate their homes. Many families have already begun moving their belongings, using small vehicles and donkey carts to transport what they can salvage. For families living on the margins, the order has created an immediate humanitarian crisis. Women, children and elderly residents are among those being forced to confront an agonizing question: Where will we go? Some families say they have neither the money to rent alternative accommodation nor the resources to cover the cost of moving. Others say they have received no clear information about whether the government has prepared relocation sites, compensation or any form of assistance. “We do not know where we are supposed to go,” residents told WDN, describing a growing sense of fear and uncertainty across the neighborhood. Buulo Eelaay, part of the Hantiwadaag area of Waaberi, is one of Mogadishu’s older neighborhoods. Its densely packed homes and narrow streets reflect decades of urban growth, with many residents saying their families have lived there for generations. Residents argue that successive governments, including previous civilian administrations and the former military government, refrained from forcibly removing long-established families because of the economic vulnerability of the communities and the particular circumstances surrounding the area. The latest developments have nevertheless reopened a much larger and increasingly bitter debate over land ownership in Mogadishu. Buulo Eelaay is reportedly not the only part of Mogadishu where residents have faced eviction or demolition in recent weeks. Similar complaints have emerged from parts of Tokyo neighborhood in Yaqshiid district, Karaan district and areas behind Juba Hotel. Opposition politicians have also accused the Federal Government of pursuing a broader campaign to reclaim or reorganize land occupied by civilians, warning that the approach could trigger a new wave of displacement among some of the capital’s poorest residents. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, now a prominent opposition figure, has sharply criticized the government’s handling of land disputes, accusing the administration of what he described as the “auctioning” and seizure of public and privately occupied land. “This is a major disaster that we condemn,” Sharif said, arguing that the government had moved from public land to settlements established during the collapse of the state and was now targeting properties that citizens claim to legally own. Development or Displacement? For families in Buulo Eelaay, the distinction is becoming increasingly difficult to see. Urban redevelopment may require roads to be widened, land to be reorganized and informal settlements to be regularized. But where families have lived for decades, any intervention raises difficult questions about property rights, due process, consultation and compensation. Without clear answers, the bulldozer becomes more than a construction machine. It becomes a symbol of state power confronting people with little political or economic influence. Residents are therefore calling on the government to suspend the eviction process, consult affected communities and establish a transparent mechanism for determining ownership and resolving disputes. They also want authorities to clarify what will happen to families who are removed: Will they receive alternative housing? Compensation? Relocation assistance? Or simply be left to fend for themselves? So far, residents say they have received few convincing answers. The controversy comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Somalia, when political tensions are already high and public confidence in state institutions remains fragile. For a government seeking to strengthen its legitimacy, the treatment of vulnerable citizens during urban redevelopment could prove politically consequential. Mogadishu needs roads, modern infrastructure and orderly land administration. But it also needs something equally fundamental: a government that protects its citizens while developing their city. For the families of Buulo Eelaay, that principle is no longer an abstract question of governance. It is a question of whether they will still have a home when the bulldozers arrive. Residents argue that successive governments, including previous civilian administrations and the former military government, refrained from forcibly removing long-established families because of the economic vulnerability of the communities and the particular circumstances surrounding the area. The latest developments have nevertheless reopened a much larger and increasingly bitter debate over land ownership in Mogadishu. Buulo Eelaay is reportedly not the only part of Mogadishu where residents have faced eviction or demolition in recent weeks. Similar complaints have emerged from parts of Tokyo neighborhood in Yaqshiid district, Karaan district and areas behind Juba Hotel. Opposition politicians have also accused the Federal Government of pursuing a broader campaign to reclaim or reorganize land occupied by civilians, warning that the approach could trigger a new wave of displacement among some of the capital’s poorest residents. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, now a prominent opposition figure, has sharply criticized the government’s handling of land disputes, accusing the administration of what he described as the “auctioning” and seizure of public and privately occupied land. “This is a major disaster that we condemn,” Sharif said, arguing that the government had moved from public land to settlements established during the collapse of the state and was now targeting properties that citizens claim to legally own. Development or Displacement? For families in Buulo Eelaay, the distinction is becoming increasingly difficult to see. Urban redevelopment may require roads to be widened, land to be reorganized and informal settlements to be regularized. But where families have lived for decades, any intervention raises difficult questions about property rights, due process, consultation and compensation. Without clear answers, the bulldozer becomes more than a construction machine. It becomes a symbol of state power confronting people with little political or economic influence. Residents are therefore calling on the government to suspend the eviction process, consult affected communities and establish a transparent mechanism for determining ownership and resolving disputes. They also want authorities to clarify what will happen to families who are removed: Will they receive alternative housing? Compensation? Relocation assistance? Or simply be left to fend for themselves? So far, residents say they have received few convincing answers. The controversy comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Somalia, when political tensions are already high and public confidence in state institutions remains fragile. For a government seeking to strengthen its legitimacy, the treatment of vulnerable citizens during urban redevelopment could prove politically consequential. Mogadishu needs roads, modern infrastructure and orderly land administration. But it also needs something equally fundamental: a government that protects its citizens while developing their city. For the families of Buulo Eelaay, that principle is no longer an abstract question of governance. It is a question of whether they will still have a home when the bulldozers arrive. items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo gaaray Magaalada Gaalkacyo (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud oo uu wehliyo Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug, Axmed Cabdi Kaariye (Qoorqoor) ayaa gelinkii dambe ee maanta gaaray Magaalada Gaalkacyo ee Xarunta Gobolka Mudug. Madaxda ayaa si diiran loogu soo dhaweeyay Garoonka Kubadda Cagta Cabdullaahi Ciise, halkaas oo ay kula hadleen dad fara-badan oo kuwa deegaanka ah. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa dadka reer Gaalkacyo uga mahadceliyay soo dhaweynta ballaaran ee ay ugu sameeyeen magaalada, isagoona ku amaanay, sida ay u ilaalinayaan midnimada iyo wadajirka dhexdooda. Madaxweynaha Dowladda Federaalka ayaa muddada uu ku sugan yahay magaalada kulamo kula qaadan doona bulshada qaybaheeda kala duwan. Magaalada ayaa waxaa la geeyay boqolaal ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, si ay kuwa Galmudug uga gacan siiyaan sugidda amniga ee wafdiga Madaxweynaha. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa gaaray Gaalkacyo, iyadoo Puntland ay digniin ka soo saartay imaanshiiisa magaalada, ka dib markii ay ku eedeysay in uu colaad cusub ka hurinayo gudaha Puntland. Galmudug ayaa Puntland ku gacan seyrtay in laga hortago safarka Madaxweynaha ee Gaalkacyo, iyadoona Galmudug ay sheegtay in Madaxweynuhu uu xaq u leeyahay in xilli kasta uu soo booqdo deegaanada Galmudug. Xaaladda Gaalkacyo ayaa ah mid xasaasi ah, iyadoo Puntland ay ku dhawaaqday in la hakiyay dhaqdhaqaaqyadii siyaasadeed ee magaalada, muddada uu Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ku sugan yahay magaaladaasi. Puntland ayaan ogoleyn in la tago koonfurta Gaalkacyo iyo in dad halkaasi ka socda ay soo galaan dhinaca waqooyi ee magaalada. Go’aankan ayaad mooddaa in si gaar ah loogu beegsanayo Odayaasha Dhaqanka ee reer Puntland ee la rabo inay koonfurta Gaalkacyo kula kulmaan Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh.

items.title: Booliska Bari iyo INTERPOL oo Ka Wada Hadlay Iskaashiga Amniga+SAWIRO
items.description: Boosaaso (Raxanreeb Online): Taliyaha Qaybta Booliska Gobolka Bari, G/Sare Saciid Aadan Saciid, ayaa xafiiskiisa ku qaabilay guddi ka socday INTERPOL, iyadoo kulanka looga hadlay xoojinta iskaashiga iyo wada-shaqeynta dhinacyada amniga. Kulanka ayaa si gaar ah diiradda loogu saaray is-dhaafsiga xogaha amni, ka hortagga dambiyada abaabulan, iyo sidii loo sii xoojin lahaa wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha amniga Gobolka Bari iyo INTERPOL. Taliyaha ayaa adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay wada-shaqeyn joogto ah oo dhex marta hay’adaha amniga gudaha iyo kuwa caalamiga ah, si loo xoojiyo amniga, loo yareeyo dambiyada, loona xaqiijiyo kala dambeyn waarta. Ugu dambeyn, Taliyaha ayaa guddiga INTERPOL uga mahadceliyay booqashadooda iyo dadaallada ay ku bixinayaan xoojinta iskaashiga dhinacyada amniga. items.title: Born From Collapse: The Real Story of How Somali Piracy Began
items.description: Somali piracy is often introduced as a story about criminals attacking ships from speedboats. That description captures the violence, but not the history. The phenomenon grew from state collapse, economic desperation, foreign exploitation of marine resources, weak maritime enforcement, and the opportunities created by a major shipping corridor that hosts roughly 20,000 vessels annually, carrying 12% of global seaborne trade. It was neither a simple popular uprising nor an inevitable product of Somali culture: it was a changing political economy that developed on land and at sea. Before the Pirate Boom Understanding Somali piracy requires distinguishing piracy from armed robbery, illegal fishing, maritime terrorism, and fishing-community conflicts under international law. While the Horn of Africa had a long maritime history, piracy was relatively uncommon before the modern Somali state was established. Coastal conflicts did exist, but they were not part of a continuous pirate tradition. The decisive break came with the collapse of the Somali state in 1991. This collapse created a profound institutional vacuum: when a state loses the capacity to police territory, enforce contracts, and punish violence, authority does not disappear, it fragments. In this vacuum, local elders, militias, businessmen, smugglers, and armed entrepreneurs began to compete over who can provide protection and collect revenue. The first recorded incidents of modern piracy occurred almost immediately after the collapse, specifically between 1991 and 1994 along the northeastern coast of Puntland and the central Mudug region. Early reports confirmed that in the absence of a navy, foreign trawlers began harvesting an estimated $300 million worth of seafood illegally each year. Somalia’s coastline became vulnerable not simply because the country was poor, but because no reliable institution could decide who had the right to fish, patrol, license vessels, or settle disputes. This vulnerability is best explained by political ecology, which connects environmental resources to power: fish stocks, coastal waters, and shipping lanes were not merely natural features, they were sources of wealth whose control changed after 1991. When foreign fishing fleets entered poorly regulated waters and local communities lost access to familiar livelihoods, environmental pressure became a political grievance. The end of centralized authority weakened policing, courts, coastguard functions, licensing systems, and the ability to regulate foreign access to Somali waters. Coastal communities were left with few legal economic opportunities while foreign vessels could operate with limited oversight. The early emergence and local tolerance of piracy are deeply connected to statelessness, poverty, illegal fishing, and toxic-waste dumping. Political ecology does not excuse piracy, rather, it explains how resource depletion and unequal control can create the resentment and insecurity in which armed markets grow. UNEP reports from 2005 documented the washing up of rusted containers following the 2004 Tsunami, providing physical evidence of the toxic waste dumping that occurred during the 1990s.  This history describes piracy’s origins as a political-ecological sequence in which governance collapse and resource exploitation disrupted coastal livelihoods and increased maritime insecurity. This does not mean that every pirate began as a fisherman defending Somali waters. The collapse of governance changed incentives for several groups at once, some saw armed protection or attacks on foreign vessels as income, while others entered a profitable criminal market once ransom became available. Claims of defending Somali waters and the commercial reality of hostage-taking could coexist. From Protection to Organized Crime Somali piracy developed as a cycle with distinct politically connected phases, tracing its path from the early 1990s through the dramatic rise after 2006. This framework rejects the idea that piracy appeared suddenly in 2008. While the international community noticed the crisis most clearly after attacks on World Food Programme vessels, the underlying conditions had been developing for years. This evolution is supported by the opportunity theory of crime: organized crime requires a suitable target, weak protection, expected profits, and a reasonable chance of escape. Somalia’s location beside one of the world’s busiest shipping routes supplied those conditions, offering targets ranging from small dhows to Ultra Large Crude Carriers. The transformation accelerated when hijacking ships for ransom became more profitable than opportunistic theft. Ransom transformed scattered maritime violence into a business, the target was valuable, the crew could be used as leverage, and the operation could be financed through networks onshore. World Bank data suggests that between 2005 and 2012, an estimated $339 million to $413 million was paid in total ransoms. As the business model matured, specific coastal towns evolved into specialized piracy hubs. Logistical nerve centers such as Eyl and Garacad in the north, alongside Hobyo and Harardhere in central Somalia, became the primary locations where hijacked vessels were anchored and negotiations were conducted. Between 2005 and 2011, attacks surged, peaking in 2011 with 176 reported attacks and 25 successful hijackings in a single year. Somali pirates became known for holding crews and cargoes hostage while negotiating their release. The operation required boats, weapons, fuel, intelligence, financiers, negotiators, safe houses, and intermediaries. Finally, the idea of social legitimacy helps explain why some coastal communities in these hubs tolerated pirates. A group can be criminal in international law while presenting itself locally as a protector, employer, or defender against foreign exploitation. That claim may be selective or fraudulent, but it can still create cooperation, silence, or access to supplies. Somali piracy therefore combined coercion with persuasion, its strength came not only from guns and boats, but also from the ability of pirate groups to embed themselves in local economies. In some hubs, the piracy economy was so integrated that local shops provided credit to pirate crews, to be repaid doubled (Dheef-Koror) only after a successful ransom was collected. Piracy economies are dynamic, actors, tactics, and incentives change, and a wide network of participants joined as the activities expanded following the collapse of the formal economy. Illegal fishing, piracy, counter-piracy, fraudulent negotiators, and foreign and local intermediaries all became deeply entangled. Why the Coast Mattered The relationship between piracy and fishing was never simple. Somali communities had legitimate grievances about foreign fishing and the loss of control over marine resources. Yet local actors also committed predation, competed over fishing rents, and sometimes cooperated with smugglers, officials, or pirate networks. Naval presence eventually contributed to a decline in piracy, but coastal engagement was deeper than many accounts assume. The maritime predatory trap cannot be broken without treating former pirate communities as partners in a legitimate blue economy. Regional evidence shows that illegal and foreign fishing, weak governance, restricted access to fishing grounds, and criminal activity were major drivers. Conflict was particularly concentrated in Kenyan and Somali waters and the southern Red Sea, meaning piracy belonged to a larger maritime-governance crisis that cost the global economy an estimated $7 billion to $12 billion annually at its height. Why Piracy Declined The dramatic decline in attacks after 2011 resulted from a combination of international naval patrols, improved coordination, ship protection, and, crucially, a shift in local political and social conditions. While effective naval measures reduced piracy in the Gulf of Aden, they often displaced activity further into the Indian Ocean. By 2012, over 30 nations had deployed more than 40 warships to the region, creating the most intensive naval cooperation since World War II. A decisive factor in this shift was the emergence of local Somali security actors, most notably the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF). Established in 2010 with support from the United Arab Emirates, the PMPF became the only local force capable of conducting sustained counter-piracy operations on land. With a force that eventually grew to over 500 trained personnel, the PMPF targeted pirate logistics and blocked access to traditional anchorages in hubs like Eyl and Garacad. The presence of the PMPF allowed the Puntland government to assert control over the coastline, preventing criminal networks from returning to the same bays to dock hijacked vessels. Equally important was a community-led social movement driven by traditional Somali leaders. Under the administration of Puntland President Abdirahman Farole, a community-centered approach was adopted to strip piracy of its social legitimacy. Religious sheikhs were mobilized to issue fatwas declaring piracy as forbidden (haram), while clan elders were encouraged to dissuade young men from joining pirate gangs. In Eyl and Garacad, once the world’s most notorious pirate capital, the local community eventually turned on the pirates, physically chasing them out of the town in 2011. However, the decline should not be confused with the resolution of piracy’s root causes. Counter-piracy measures addressed only the symptoms of the crisis, such as maritime insecurity and weak law enforcement, while leaving triggers like corruption and economic dislocation intact. Traditional income-sharing arrangements helped contain conflict in some regions, but Puntland remained more vulnerable due to its proximity to deep-water shipping lanes and the survival of underground criminal infrastructures. This regional evidence suggests that while the PMPF and community leaders successfully suppressed the era of high-seas piracy, they did so within a fragile land-sea political economy that remained susceptible to future collapse. The Unfinished Story The most recent sources argue that Somali piracy is dormant rather than extinguished. A 2026 perspective links renewed risk to unresolved governance failures, illegal fishing, environmental degradation, and the survival of criminal networks. The resurgence began showing early signs with the hijacking of the MV Ruen in late 2023, the first successful capture of a merchant vessel in over six years. A major catalyst for this renewed activity was the shifting security landscape on land, specifically the withdrawal of the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) from the strategic Mudug and Garacad shoreline to address insurgency in the Bari and Sanag mountains. This reallocation removed a primary arm of deterrence that had historically played a massive role in securing the Mudug coast. Furthermore, systemic unemployment among the coastal youth has reached critical levels. Despite the completion of the Garacad Port, the facility has yet to generate sustainable employment for local youth, leaving many with no viable economic future. This lack of opportunity is exacerbated by a severe economic crisis caused by the sharp cutting of international humanitarian funding in 2025 and 2026. Amidst this hardship, the successful hijacking of the MV Abdullah in April 2024, which yielded a $5 million ransom, has served as a powerful motivational trigger. For youth seeing their comrades make massive amounts of money in a matter of weeks, it has encouraged a new generation to venture far beyond Somali territorial waters. This resurgence after 2022 exposes the limits of deterrence when community grievances and pirate networks remain intact. Onshore governance gaps and criminal infrastructure remain blind spots in counter-piracy policy. The real story of Somali piracy begins with the collapse of institutions governing Somalia’s coast. It grew when resource insecurity met criminal opportunity, became organized through political and commercial networks centered in hubs like Garacad and Eyl, and declined when international force raised the cost of attacks. State collapse created the institutional space, resource conflict supplied grievances, shipping created opportunity, and local legitimacy helped convert individual attacks into a durable political economy. Its possible return shows that naval deterrence can suppress piracy without repairing the land-sea political economy that produced it. A lasting solution must protect shipping while restoring coastal livelihoods, regulating fisheries, strengthening legitimate authority, and addressing the networks that profit from insecurity. Counter-piracy measures addressed only the symptoms of the crisis, such as maritime insecurity and weak law enforcement, while leaving triggers like corruption and economic dislocation intact. Traditional income-sharing arrangements helped contain conflict in some regions, but Puntland remained more vulnerable due to its proximity to deep-water shipping lanes and the survival of underground criminal infrastructures. This regional evidence suggests that while the PMPF and community leaders successfully suppressed the era of high-seas piracy, they did so within a fragile land-sea political economy that remained susceptible to future collapse. The Unfinished Story The most recent sources argue that Somali piracy is dormant rather than extinguished. A 2026 perspective links renewed risk to unresolved governance failures, illegal fishing, environmental degradation, and the survival of criminal networks. The resurgence began showing early signs with the hijacking of the MV Ruen in late 2023, the first successful capture of a merchant vessel in over six years. A major catalyst for this renewed activity was the shifting security landscape on land, specifically the withdrawal of the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) from the strategic Mudug and Garacad shoreline to address insurgency in the Bari and Sanag mountains. This reallocation removed a primary arm of deterrence that had historically played a massive role in securing the Mudug coast. Furthermore, systemic unemployment among the coastal youth has reached critical levels. Despite the completion of the Garacad Port, the facility has yet to generate sustainable employment for local youth, leaving many with no viable economic future. This lack of opportunity is exacerbated by a severe economic crisis caused by the sharp cutting of international humanitarian funding in 2025 and 2026. Amidst this hardship, the successful hijacking of the MV Abdullah in April 2024, which yielded a $5 million ransom, has served as a powerful motivational trigger. For youth seeing their comrades make massive amounts of money in a matter of weeks, it has encouraged a new generation to venture far beyond Somali territorial waters. This resurgence after 2022 exposes the limits of deterrence when community grievances and pirate networks remain intact. Onshore governance gaps and criminal infrastructure remain blind spots in counter-piracy policy. The real story of Somali piracy begins with the collapse of institutions governing Somalia’s coast. It grew when resource insecurity met criminal opportunity, became organized through political and commercial networks centered in hubs like Garacad and Eyl, and declined when international force raised the cost of attacks. State collapse created the institutional space, resource conflict supplied grievances, shipping created opportunity, and local legitimacy helped convert individual attacks into a durable political economy. Its possible return shows that naval deterrence can suppress piracy without repairing the land-sea political economy that produced it. A lasting solution must protect shipping while restoring coastal livelihoods, regulating fisheries, strengthening legitimate authority, and addressing the networks that profit from insecurity.
