items.title: Xogta qaabkii ay DF uga hor-tagtay dal qarka u saarnaa in uu aqoonsado Somaliland?
items.description: Bissau (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa la sheegay inay fashilisay dadaal heer gabagabo marayay oo Somaliland ay ku dooneysay in Guinea-Bissau ay u aqoonsato dal madax-bannaan, kadib faragelin diblomaasiyadeed oo ay Muqdisho ku taageereen Turkiga, Masar iyo Sacuudi Carabiya. Warbixin ay daabacday Mada Masr , oo soo xiganeysa saraakiil sare oo ka tirsan Dowladda Federaalka iyo maamulka Somaliland ah oo arrinta si dhow ula socday, ayaa shaaca ka qaaday in wada-hadallo heer wasiir ah ay muddo u socdeen mas’uuliyiinta Hargeysa iyo Guinea-Bissau, isla markaana dhinaca Somaliland uu rumeysnaa in aqoonsiga lagu dhow yahay in si rasmi ah loogu dhawaaqo. Dabayaaqadii bishii July waxaa soo baxay warar sheegaya in Guinea-Bissau ay isku diyaarineyso inay Somaliland u aqoonsato dal madax-bannaan, taas oo ka dhigi lahayd dalkii ugu horreeyay ee Afrikaan ah ee tallaabadaas qaada. Arrintan ayaa timid kadib markii Israel ay dabayaaqadii December noqotay dalkii ugu horreeyay ee si rasmi ah u aqoonsada Somaliland, taas oo Hargeysa gelisay rajo ah in dowlado kale ay ku xigi karaan. Somaliland ayaa in ka badan 30 sano raadineysay aqoonsi caalami ah tan iyo markii ay 1991 ku dhawaaqday inay ka go’day Soomaaliya, xilli dowladdii dhexe burburtay, dalkuna galay dagaal sokeeye. Tan iyo waqtigaas waxay si joogto ah u wadday olole ay ku dooneyso inay hesho aqoonsi caalami ah, iyadoo isku dayeysa inay xaaladdeeda ka soocdo maamul-goboleedyada kale ee Soomaaliya. Wafdi gaar ah oo Bissau tegay Laba sarkaal oo sare oo Somaliland ah oo xog-ogaal u ahaa wada-hadallada ayaa Mada Masr u sheegay in xiriirrada Guinea-Bissau ay muddo socdeen, isla markaana ay gaareen heer wasiir. Mid ka mid ah saraakiisha ayaa sheegay in saddex mas’uul oo sare oo Somaliland ah, oo uu ku jiray wasiirka arrimaha dibadda, ay diyaarad gaar loo leeyahay ku tageen Guinea-Bissau, halkaas oo ay kula kulmeen madax sare oo dowladda ka tirsan. Sarkaalka ma uusan sheegin xilliga saxda ah ee wada-hadalladu bilowdeen, balse wuxuu kulamadii hore ku tilmaamay kuwo “guuleystay”. Wuxuu sheegay in wafdiga Somaliland uu kulamada ka soo baxay isagoo si weyn ugu kalsoon in aqoonsiga rasmiga ah uu soo dhow yahay. Madaxweynaha Somaliland Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdullaahi Cirro ayaa, sida laga soo xigtay sarkaalka, sugayay ku dhawaaqista rasmiga ah iyo wicitaan xaqiijin ah oo uga yimaada Bissau. Hase yeeshee, kahor inta aanu wicitaankaasi dhicin, dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa arrinta soo faragelisay. Sarkaalka Somaliland ayaa sheegay in Muqdisho ay taageero ka heshay Turkiga, Masar iyo Sacuudi Carabiya, kadibna wada-hadalladii aqoonsigu burbureen. Soomaaliya oo xogta heshay Sarkaal sare oo Soomaali ah oo qeyb ka ahaa jawaabtii diblomaasiyadeed ayaa isna Mada Masr u xaqiijiyay in dowladda Soomaaliya ay heshay xog sheegaysa in wafdi heer sare ah oo Somaliland ka socda uu joogo Guinea-Bissau. Sida uu sheegay sarkaalku, Muqdisho ayaa markaas si toos ah ula xiriirtay wasiirka arrimaha dibadda Guinea-Bissau. Dhinaca Guinea-Bissau ayaa, sida laga soo xigtay sarkaalka Soomaaliga ah, beeniyay in mas’uuliyiin Somaliland ah ay dalka joogeen, wuxuuna sheegay inaanay jirin wax qorshe ah oo lagu aqoonsanayo Somaliland. Maalmo kadib, 26-kii July, Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Guinea-Bissau ayaa soo saartay bayaan rasmi ah oo ay ku beenisay wararka. Wasaaraddu waxay sheegtay in Guinea-Bissau “aysan qaadan, isla markaana aysan ka fiirsaneyn wax go’aan ah” oo lagu aqoonsanayo Somaliland. Sarkaalka Soomaaliga ah ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in Hargeysa isla muddadaas dadaallo aqoonsi ka wadday Eswatini, South Sudan iyo dalal kale. Muqdisho ayaa uga jawaabtay olole diblomaasiyadeed ay la kaashatay dalal uu sarkaalku ku tilmaamay “dalal saaxiibbo ah”, waxaana uu sheegay in dadaalladaas ilaa hadda lagu xakameeyay qorshaha Somaliland. Sida uu sheegay isla sarkaalku, ololaha aqoonsi-raadinta Somaliland waxaa taageeraya, hormuudna ka ah Imaaraadka Carabta iyo Israel. Lix dal oo la hor istaagay Wasiiru-dowlaha Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya Cali Maxamed Cumar (Cali Balcad) ayaa 29-kii July wareysi uu siiyay Universal TV ku sheegay in dowladda Soomaaliya ay lix dal ka hor istaagtay inay raacaan tallaabadii Israel. Isagoo aan magacaabin dalalkaas, wuxuu sheegay in Muqdisho ay waraaqo u dirtay dowladahooda, kuna boorrisay inaysan Somaliland siin aqoonsi rasmi ah. Cali Maxamed Cumar ayaa sheegay inuu ku kalsoon yahay in dal Afrikaan ah ama quwad weyn oo caalami ah aysan qaadi doonin tallaabadaas, inkastoo uu sheegay in Israel ay dhowr dal oo yaryar ku cadaadineysay ama ku dhiirrigelineysay inay Somaliland aqoonsadaan. Inkasta oo Hargeysa markii hore filaysay in aqoonsigii Israel uu furo albaab ay dowlado kale ku soo raacaan, ilaa hadda taasi ma aysan dhicin. Cirro ayaa dhowr jeer sheegay in dalal dhowr ahi ay ka fiirsanayaan inay aqoonsadaan Somaliland, waxaana dadaallada diblomaasiyadeed ee maamulkiisa ay sii xoogaysteen wixii ka dambeeyay aqoonsigii Israel. Xiriirka cusub ee Israel iyo Somaliland, iyo dhaqdhaqaaqyada diblomaasiyadeed ee Hargeysa, ayaa sidoo kale sare u qaaday walaaca dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya. Muqdisho ayaa tan iyo December taageero ka raadinaysay dalalka Muslimka ah iyo xulafadeeda gobolka, iyadoo isku dayeysa inay go’doomiso aqoonsiga Israel oo ay ka hortagto in dowlado kale ay ku daydaan. Mowqifka dalalka Afrika Haddii Guinea-Bissau ay aqoonsan lahayd Somaliland, waxay arrintaasi calaamad u noqon lahayd isbeddel weyn oo ku yimaada mowqifka soo jireenka ah ee Midowga Afrika iyo dowladaha xubnaha ka ah. Dalalka Afrika ayaa guud ahaan ka fogaaday tallaabooyinka wax ka beddeli kara xuduudaha dowladaha xubnaha ka ah qaaradda, iyadoo laga cabsi qabo in arrintaasi dhiirrigeliso dhaqdhaqaaqyo kale oo gooni-u-goosad ah. Laba sarkaal oo Masri ah ayaa Mada Masr u sheegay in Qaahira ay arrintan kala shaqeyneyso Sacuudi Carabiya, iyagoo xiriir la sameynaya dalalka kale ee Afrika. Farriinta ay gudbinayaan ayaa ah in haddii la aqbalo gooni-u-goosashada Somaliland, aysan noqon doonin kiis keli ah oo qaaradda ka dhaca. “Si cad waa arrin saameyn ku yeelan doonta hoggaamiye kasta oo Afrikaan ah, gaar ahaan kuwa Bariga Afrika,” ayuu yiri mid ka mid ah saraakiisha Masar. Sarkaalka labaad ayaa yiri: “Aad ayay muhiim noogu tahay in dalalku aysan u dhaqaaqin aqoonsiga Somaliland, sababtoo ah inta ay xaaladdu sidaas tahay, su’aashan waxay ahaaneysaa mid aad u fudud in wax laga qabto — annaga oo keliya ma ahan, balse qof walba.” Itoobiya iyo rajadii hore Kahor Guinea-Bissau, Somaliland waxay rajadeeda ugu weyn ku qabtay Itoobiya. Horraantii 2024, maamulkii madaxweyne Muuse Biixi Cabdi ayaa Itoobiya la saxiixday is-afgarad siin lahaa Addis Ababa marin ay ka hesho xeebta Somaliland, iyadoo la sheegay in heshiisku ku saabsanaa dhul xeebeed dhererkiisu yahay 20 kiiloomitir oo lagu kireynayo muddo dheer. Muuse Biixi ayaa markaas sheegay in heshiiskaasi la filayo inuu Itoobiya u horseedo inay Somaliland aqoonsato. Hase yeeshee, qorshahaasi ma uusan gaarin natiijadii ay Hargeysa fileysay kadib markii Itoobiya iyo dowladda Soomaaliya ay wada-hadallo uu Turkigu dhexdhexaadinayay ku gaareen heshiis loo bixiyay Baaqa Ankara. Guinea-Bissau sidoo kale ma ahayn dalkii ugu horreeyay ee Galbeedka Afrika ee Somaliland ay la xiriirto. Sanadkii 2019, Muuse Biixi ayaa booqasho rasmi ah ku tagay Conakry, taas oo dowladda Soomaaliya ku kalliftay inay xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed u jarto Guinea. Falanqeeye si dhow ula socday dhacdadaas ayaa sheegay in isla xilligaas Hargeysa ay xiriir la sameysay Guinea-Bissau, inkastoo dadaalladaasi aysan horseedin aqoonsi. Fashilka wadahadalladii ugu dambeeyay ee Guinea-Bissau ayaa hadda muujinaya tartanka diblomaasiyadeed ee sii xoogeysanaya ee u dhexeeya Muqdisho iyo Hargeysa, iyadoo Somaliland ay raadineyso dalal kale oo aqoonsada, halka dowladda federaalka ay isku dayeyso inay ka hortagto in aqoonsigii Israel uu isu beddelo silsilad ay dowlado kale ku soo biiraan. items.title: Carruur nafaqo celin loogu sameeyay Muqdisho markii ay taageereen ganacsato Somali ah
items.description: (ERGO) – Laba boqol oo carruur ah ayaa ka soo kabanaya xaalado nafaqo-darro ah, markii hay’adda maxalliga ah ee Trevesom ay u bilowday nafaqeyn bilaash ah. Carruurtan ayaa inta badan ka soo jeeda qoysas danyar ah oo ku nool xeryaha lagu barakacay ee magaalada Muqdisho. Barnaamijkan oo magaciisu yahay (NUTHUP) waa mid lagu fulinayo dhaqaale laga soo aruuriyay ganacsato Soomaaliyeed. Cuntada nafaqada leh oo lagu farsameeyay dalka ayaa ka sameysan lows, sisinta oo laga helo dufanka caafimaadka leh, digir, galley iyo qamadi oo la isku daray, taas oo hay’addu sheegtay in carruurtu ka helayaan tamar badan, borotiin iyo nafaqooyin muhiimka u ah korriimada iyo caafimaadka carruurta. Tan iyo bishii Feberaayo oo barnaamijkan uu socdo waxaa ilmo kasta loo qoondeeyay bishii 3 illaa 6 kiilo garaam. Qoysaska la diiwaan-galiyay ayaa qoondadooda ay hay’addu ugu keentaa xerada ay deggan yihihiin. items.title: Iran oo mowqif lama filaan ah ka qaadatay heshiiska Turkey, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan
items.description: Tehran (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Iran ayaa hoos u dhigtay walaaca laga muujiyey heshiiska cusub ee amniga iyo difaaca ee ay magaalada barakeysan ee Makkah ku kala saxiixdeen Sacuudi Carabiya, Turkey iyo Pakistan, iyadoo sheegtay in Tehran aysan u arkin isbahaysigan mid si gaar ah iyada loogu wajahayo. Afhayeenka wasaaradda arrimaha dibadda Iran, Esmaeil Baghaei, ayaa Isniintii sheegay in dowladdiisu aysan arkin sabab ay uga walaacdo heshiiska cusub, xilli falanqeeyayaal badan ay ku doodayaan in iskaashiga Ankara, Riyadh iyo Islamabad uu qayb ahaan jawaab u yahay awoodda Iran ee gobolka. Baghaei ayaa taa beddelkeeda heshiiska ku tilmaamay calaamad muujineysa “isbeddel ku yimid aragtida” dalalka gobolka ay ka qabaan Mareykanka iyo qaabka loo wajahayo sugidda amniga Bariga Dhexe. Waxa uu sheegay in heshiisku muujinayo in dowladaha gobolka ay sii kordhinayaan ku tiirsanaanta awoodahooda gaarka ah, halkii ay ammaankooda ku tiirsanaan lahaayeen quwado dibadeed. “Qorshe kasta oo ku dhisan xaqiiqooyinka juqraafi-siyaasadeed iyo taariikheed ee gobolka, oo dhammeystiran, cid walbana loo dhan yahay, isla markaana si sax ah u aqoonsanaya cadowga iyo khatarta, wuxuu fursad u leeyahay inuu gacan ka geysto xoojinta amniga, kana hortago xasillooni-darrada iyo xadgudubyada cadowga Sahyuuniyadda iyo xulafadiisa,” ayuu yiri Baghaei. ‘ Iran ma qabto wax cabsi ah’ Hadalkan ayaa jawaab u ah dood sii xoogeysaneysa oo ku saabsan ujeeddada dhabta ah ee heshiiska difaaca ee saddexda dal. Falanqeeyayaal badan ayaa soo jeediyey in isu-soo-dhawaanshaha Turkey, Sacuudi Carabiya iyo Pakistan uu yahay isku-day lagu dhisayo miisaan cusub oo awoodda gobolka ah, gaar ahaan marka la eego Iran. Saddexda dal waxaa dadkooda u badan Muslimiin Sunni ah, hase yeeshee xiriirkooda Tehran isku heer ma aha. Sacuudi Carabiya iyo Iran muddo dheer waxaa ka dhexeeyey loollan siyaasadeed iyo mid istaraatiiji ah, inkastoo sannadihii dambe labada dhinac ay qaadeen tallaabooyin lagu yareynayo xiisadda. Turkey iyo Pakistan, dhankooda, waxay inta badan sii hayeen xiriir shaqeynaya oo ay la leeyihiin Tehran, xitaa xilliyada ay xiisadaha gobolka sare u kacaan. Pakistan ayaa sidoo kale door muhiim ah ka ciyaartay dadaallada lagu dhex-dhexaadinayo Mareykanka iyo Iran, iyadoo noqotay marin muhiim u ah wada-hadallada labada dhinac xilli uu sii jiitamayo khilaafka ka taagan Marinka Hormuz. Iran ayaa xiritaanka marinkaasi uga jawaabtay dagaalka ay Mareykanka iyo Israel kula jiraan dalkaas, kaas oo markii hore lagu sheegay inuu bartilmaameedsanayey in meesha laga saaro dowladda Tehran. ‘Cadaadis laba jiho ah’ Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa dhinaceeda si toos ah u dareenyay saameynta dagaalka, iyadoo Iran ay qaadday weerarro aargoosi ah oo inta badan lagu bartilmaameedsaday saldhigyada iyo hantida ciidamada Mareykanka ee ku sugan boqortooyada. Markii colaadda Iran iyo Mareykanka ay sii dheeraatay, waxaa mar kale soo cusboonaaday xiisadda u dhexeysa Sacuudiga iyo maamulka Xuutiyiinta ee magaalada Sanca, kaas oo gacanta ku haya inta badan waqooyiga Yemen. Xuutiyiinta ayaa weerarro ku qaaday xarumo tamareed oo ku yaalla Sacuudiga, iyagoo sheegay inay uga jawaabayaan duqeymaha Riyadh iyo weerarrada ay qaadaan xulafadeeda ka tirsan dowladda Yemen ee caalamku aqoonsan yahay. Dhacdadii ugu dambeysay, dab ballaaran ayaa ka kacay warshad sifeysa shidaalka oo ay leedahay shirkadda Saudi Aramco, kadib markii diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn ay ku dhacday xaruntaas oo ku taalla gobolka Jizan subaxnimadii Axadda. Xuutiyiinta ayaa sheegtay mas’uuliyadda weerarka, taas oo mar kale muujisay sida dagaallada isbiirsaday ee gobolka ay cadaadis ugu saarayaan Sacuudiga dhinacyo kala duwan. Xiriirka Ankara iyo Riyadh Heshiiska Makkah ayaa sidoo kale imanaya xilli xiriirka Turkey iyo Sacuudi Carabiya uu si weyn uga soo kabanayo khilaafkii labada dal kala fogeeyey sannado ka hor. Xiriirka Ankara iyo Riyadh ayaa aad u xumaaday kadib dilkii wariye Jamal Khashoggi ee qunsuliyadda Sacuudiga ee Istanbul, iyo sidoo kale taageeradii labada dal ay siiyeen dhinacyo iska soo horjeeda oo ka dagaallamayey Libya. Hase yeeshee, sannadihii dambe labada dowladood ayaa bilaabay dib-u-heshiisiin siyaasadeed iyo mid dhaqaale, taas oo hadda u muuqata inay gaartay heer iskaashi difaac iyo amni. Pakistan, dhankeeda, waxay muddo dheer ahayd saaxiib militari oo muhiim u ah Sacuudi Carabiya, iyadoo ciidamadeeda iyo khubaradeeda difaaca ay xiriir dhow la lahaayeen Riyadh. Islamabad ayaa haddana isku dayda inay xiriir wanaagsan la sii yeelato dowladaha kale ee Muslimka ah, gaar ahaan Iran, taas oo ka dhigaysa doorkeeda heshiiskan mid si dhow isha loogu hayo. Hadallada Iran waxay muujinayaan in Tehran ay hadda dooratay inay heshiiska cusub u fasirto isbeddel ka dhan ah ku tiirsanaanta Mareykanka, halkii ay u arki lahayd isbahaysi cusub oo lagu hareereynayo ama lagu cadaadinayo Iran. Waxa uu sheegay in heshiisku muujinayo in dowladaha gobolka ay sii kordhinayaan ku tiirsanaanta awoodahooda gaarka ah, halkii ay ammaankooda ku tiirsanaan lahaayeen quwado dibadeed. “Qorshe kasta oo ku dhisan xaqiiqooyinka juqraafi-siyaasadeed iyo taariikheed ee gobolka, oo dhammeystiran, cid walbana loo dhan yahay, isla markaana si sax ah u aqoonsanaya cadowga iyo khatarta, wuxuu fursad u leeyahay inuu gacan ka geysto xoojinta amniga, kana hortago xasillooni-darrada iyo xadgudubyada cadowga Sahyuuniyadda iyo xulafadiisa,” ayuu yiri Baghaei. ‘ Iran ma qabto wax cabsi ah’ Hadalkan ayaa jawaab u ah dood sii xoogeysaneysa oo ku saabsan ujeeddada dhabta ah ee heshiiska difaaca ee saddexda dal. Falanqeeyayaal badan ayaa soo jeediyey in isu-soo-dhawaanshaha Turkey, Sacuudi Carabiya iyo Pakistan uu yahay isku-day lagu dhisayo miisaan cusub oo awoodda gobolka ah, gaar ahaan marka la eego Iran. Saddexda dal waxaa dadkooda u badan Muslimiin Sunni ah, hase yeeshee xiriirkooda Tehran isku heer ma aha. Sacuudi Carabiya iyo Iran muddo dheer waxaa ka dhexeeyey loollan siyaasadeed iyo mid istaraatiiji ah, inkastoo sannadihii dambe labada dhinac ay qaadeen tallaabooyin lagu yareynayo xiisadda. Turkey iyo Pakistan, dhankooda, waxay inta badan sii hayeen xiriir shaqeynaya oo ay la leeyihiin Tehran, xitaa xilliyada ay xiisadaha gobolka sare u kacaan. Pakistan ayaa sidoo kale door muhiim ah ka ciyaartay dadaallada lagu dhex-dhexaadinayo Mareykanka iyo Iran, iyadoo noqotay marin muhiim u ah wada-hadallada labada dhinac xilli uu sii jiitamayo khilaafka ka taagan Marinka Hormuz. Iran ayaa xiritaanka marinkaasi uga jawaabtay dagaalka ay Mareykanka iyo Israel kula jiraan dalkaas, kaas oo markii hore lagu sheegay inuu bartilmaameedsanayey in meesha laga saaro dowladda Tehran. ‘Cadaadis laba jiho ah’ Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa dhinaceeda si toos ah u dareenyay saameynta dagaalka, iyadoo Iran ay qaadday weerarro aargoosi ah oo inta badan lagu bartilmaameedsaday saldhigyada iyo hantida ciidamada Mareykanka ee ku sugan boqortooyada. Markii colaadda Iran iyo Mareykanka ay sii dheeraatay, waxaa mar kale soo cusboonaaday xiisadda u dhexeysa Sacuudiga iyo maamulka Xuutiyiinta ee magaalada Sanca, kaas oo gacanta ku haya inta badan waqooyiga Yemen. Xuutiyiinta ayaa weerarro ku qaaday xarumo tamareed oo ku yaalla Sacuudiga, iyagoo sheegay inay uga jawaabayaan duqeymaha Riyadh iyo weerarrada ay qaadaan xulafadeeda ka tirsan dowladda Yemen ee caalamku aqoonsan yahay. Dhacdadii ugu dambeysay, dab ballaaran ayaa ka kacay warshad sifeysa shidaalka oo ay leedahay shirkadda Saudi Aramco, kadib markii diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn ay ku dhacday xaruntaas oo ku taalla gobolka Jizan subaxnimadii Axadda. Xuutiyiinta ayaa sheegtay mas’uuliyadda weerarka, taas oo mar kale muujisay sida dagaallada isbiirsaday ee gobolka ay cadaadis ugu saarayaan Sacuudiga dhinacyo kala duwan. Xiriirka Ankara iyo Riyadh Heshiiska Makkah ayaa sidoo kale imanaya xilli xiriirka Turkey iyo Sacuudi Carabiya uu si weyn uga soo kabanayo khilaafkii labada dal kala fogeeyey sannado ka hor. Xiriirka Ankara iyo Riyadh ayaa aad u xumaaday kadib dilkii wariye Jamal Khashoggi ee qunsuliyadda Sacuudiga ee Istanbul, iyo sidoo kale taageeradii labada dal ay siiyeen dhinacyo iska soo horjeeda oo ka dagaallamayey Libya. Hase yeeshee, sannadihii dambe labada dowladood ayaa bilaabay dib-u-heshiisiin siyaasadeed iyo mid dhaqaale, taas oo hadda u muuqata inay gaartay heer iskaashi difaac iyo amni. Pakistan, dhankeeda, waxay muddo dheer ahayd saaxiib militari oo muhiim u ah Sacuudi Carabiya, iyadoo ciidamadeeda iyo khubaradeeda difaaca ay xiriir dhow la lahaayeen Riyadh. Islamabad ayaa haddana isku dayda inay xiriir wanaagsan la sii yeelato dowladaha kale ee Muslimka ah, gaar ahaan Iran, taas oo ka dhigaysa doorkeeda heshiiskan mid si dhow isha loogu hayo. Hadallada Iran waxay muujinayaan in Tehran ay hadda dooratay inay heshiiska cusub u fasirto isbeddel ka dhan ah ku tiirsanaanta Mareykanka, halkii ay u arki lahayd isbahaysi cusub oo lagu hareereynayo ama lagu cadaadinayo Iran. Soomaaliya oo doonaysa inay kheyraadkeeda badda u badelo awood dhaqaale iyo fursado ganacsi oo caalami ah
items.description: Soomaaliya ayaa dedaal ugu jirta sidii ay kheyraadkeeda badda u badeli lahayd awood dhaqaale iyo fursado ganacsi oo caalami ah, ayadoo Maamulka Dekedda Muqdisho uu sheegay in la doonayo inay dekeddu fududeyso maalgashiga gaarka loo leeyahay ee dhinaca kalluumeysiga iyo dhoofinta wax-soo-saarka badda. Agaasimaha Guud ee Dekedda Muqdisho, Danjire Maxamed Cali Nuur (Ameriko), ayaa gudaha dekedda ku qaabilay shirkadda Marina Seafood iyo markabkeeda Maanya Mooya, oo ku howlan gaadiidka kalluunka Soomaaliya ee loo dhoofinayo suuqyada dibadda. Agaasimuhu wuxuu soo dhoweeyay shaqada shirkadda iyo ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed ee maalgashanaya kalluumeysiga, isagoo sheegay in maamulka dekeddu ay ka go’an tahay fududeynta ganacsiga iyo taageeridda shirkadaha wax dhoofiya. Wuxuu tilmaamay in dhiirrigelinta dhoofiyeyaasha ay gacan ka geysan karto kordhinta wax-soo-saarka gudaha iyo in badeecooyinka Soomaaliya ay helaan suuqyo caalami ah. Arrintan ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli dowladda Soomaaliya ay xoogga saarayso horumarinta kalluumeysiga, ganacsiga badda iyo dhaqaalaha buluugga ah (Blue Economy), iyadoo dalka uu leeyahay xeeb aad u dheer iyo khayraad badeed oo ballaaran. Inkasta oo Soomaaliya ay leedahay mid ka mid ah xeebaha ugu dheer qaaradda Afrika, haddana khayraadka badda ayaa weli ah kuwo aan si buuxda looga faa’iideysan.

items.title: Dagaalka Iran oo banaanka soo dhigay yaraanta kaydka hubka Mareykanka
items.description: Dagaalka u dhexeeya Mareykanka iyo Iiraan ayaa soo bandhigay caqabado waaweyn oo ku saabsan kaydka hubka iyo awoodda warshadaha difaaca Mareykanka, iyadoo saraakiil iyo khubaro dhinaca ammaanka ah ay ka digayaan in isticmaalka joogtada ah ee gantaallada iyo hubka casriga ah uu hoos u dhigay kaydkii Pentagon-ka. Dagaalka oo galay ku dhowaad shan bilood ayaa si gaar ah u saameeyay gantaallada riddada dheer iyo kuwa difaaca cirka. Warbixinno cusub ayaa sheegaya in Ciidanka Mareykanka uu isticmaalay inta badan kaydkiisa qaar ka mid ah gantaallada saxda ah ee riddada dheer, gaar ahaan ATACMS iyo Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). Hubkan ayaa door muhiim ah ka ciyaara weerarrada fog, balse soo saaristooda cusub waxay qaadan kartaa sannado, taas oo walaac ka dhalisay awoodda Mareykanka ee uu si degdeg ah uga jawaabi karo dagaal kale oo weyn. Dhibaatadu kuma koobna gantaallada weerarka oo keliya, balse difaaca cirka ayaa sidoo kale si weyn loo isticmaalay, waxaana ka mid ah Patriot, THAAD, SM-3 iyo SM-6. Daraasad ay samaysay CSIS ayaa muujisay in dagaalku isticmaalay heerar aad u sarreeya oo hubkan ah, iyadoo qaar ka mid ah kaydadka ay gaareen heerar keeni kara in mustaqbalka ay adkaato in si degdeg ah loo daboolo baahida dagaal kale. Arrintan ayaa dhalisay su’aal weyn: haddii Mareykanku sannado badan ku bixiyay boqolaal bilyan oo doolar miisaaniyadda difaaca, sidee ayuu kaydka hubku ugu yaraaday muddo dhowr bilood ah? Khubaradu waxay tilmaamayaan in dhibaatadu aysan ahayn lacag la’aan oo keliya, balse ay sidoo kale tahay awoodda wax-soo-saarka warshadaha hubka. Gantaallada casriga ah waxay leeyihiin qaybo badan oo farsamo iyo silsilado sahay oo caalami ah, sidaas darteed kordhinta wax-soo-saarkooda ma dhici karto habeen keliya. Qaar ka mid ah hubka muhiimka ah waxaa lagu qiyaasay inay qaadan karaan in ka badan saddex sano in si buuxda dib loogu soo celiyo kaydkii hore. Pentagon-ka ayaa hadda cadaadis saaraya shirkadaha waaweyn ee warshadaha difaaca si ay u kordhiyaan wax-soo-saarka hubka. Wasaaradda Difaaca ayaa shirkadaha ka dalbatay qorshayaal lagu dardargelinayo soo saarista hubka muhiimka ah, iyadoo ujeeddadu tahay in dib loo buuxiyo kaydadka hoos u dhacay intii uu dagaalku socday. Si kastaba, saraakiisha Mareykanka ayaa hore u diiday in xaaladda lagu tilmaamo in ciidamadu ay gebi ahaanba hub la’aan yihiin, ayadoo Pentagon-ku uu ku adkeysanayo in weli uu haysto awood milatari oo weyn, balse xogta soo baxaysa waxay muujinaysaa in dagaal muddo dheer socda uu si weyn u cadaadin karo kaydka hubka, gaar ahaan kuwa ay adag tahay in si degdeg ah loo soo saaro.

items.title: The Recurrent Injustice Against the SSC People in Somali Politics Preamble
items.description: By Osman Hassan Dr Ali Khalif Galaydh was steeped in the Darwish heritage of freedom loving. He was a paragon of “Somalinimo”, nationalism and staunch unionist and for all that earned the highest posts of government – above all becoming the Prime Minister of Somalia. He is the last person one would expect to renounce all that dear to him and one day embrace the secession that was hitherto an anathema to him. Similarly, Miss Fahiima Quuje was the heroine of the liberation of Sool from the occupying separatists and later became an MP in the parliament of her NE State of Somalia. Who would have thought she would one day repudiate all that legacy and defect to the very enemy she fought. Yet both found themselves on the horns of a dilemma and in the end they choose the unthinkable Most people’s kneejerk reaction is to brand and shame her as another “Horgal”, another infamous defector , another fortune hunters. She is none of that just as Dr Galaydh was not. Their backgrounds simply belie all that. It is therefore appropriate to reflect on at what point each could no longer solder on and threw in the towel, give up on their once cherished union and in favour of the secession that was hitherto their anathema. This paper traces that history and the lessons for their people. Mogadishu is the bane of the unity of Somalia & not Hargeisa The 1991 collapse of the Somali state marked a critical turning point in the history of Somali unity. The subsequent unilateral declaration of independence in the north (former British Somaliland) served as a definitive test of the support for the union. While one specific clan spearheaded the secessionist movement, all other northern clans actively resisted the split, maintaining a steadfast commitment to a unified Somalia in both in word and in deed to this day. In contrast, Somalia’s presidents and Prime Ministers (invariably all southerners) have without exception abdicated their constitutional obligations to oppose the secession and defend the union, Hassan Sheikh Mohamoud (hereafter HSM) being the most manifestly indifferent to it. Far from taking concrete actions to end the secession, HSM is aiding and abetting it to the present day while on the on the other hand openly undermining the struggle of northern unionists to defend the union. Villa Somalia’s actions amount to puling the rug from underneath the union and sending a message to northern unionists to fend for themselves- or worse surrender to their secessionist occupier. Dr Galaydh and Fihiime Quuje eventually yielded to these immense pressures at critical junctures of the struggle. Revisiting these historical turning points is essential to understanding their profound implications for the present-day Northeast (NE) State. Shutting the door on Khatumo For Dr. Galaydh, the then-president of the self-proclaimed Khatumo State, the turning point for the union occurred in July 2015. At that time, President HSM announced that the Galmudug regions would be the final state admitted into the federal system. This declaration sent an unmistakable message to Dr. Galaydh, who had been actively lobbying for Khatumo’s federal inclusion: the northern regions were being excluded from federal Somalia. To him, and to northerners, this decision was tantamount to Mogadishu’s unilateral termination of the union and the ultimate breakup of the country. Dr Ali Khalif Galaydh HSM’s action received the silent endorsement of the entire southern political establishment, as no major political figure dissented at the time or in the years that followed. Ironically, President HSM’s stance closely echoed Hargeisa’s 1991 unilateral declaration of secession. For a brief moment, Mogadishu and Hargeisa aligned, sharing a parallel perspective on the dissolution of the union. It was then that Dr Galaydh made his memorable statement that they thought until then that the unity of Somalia was being undone in Hargeisa but realised then that it was in Mogadishu. With the door to unity closed, Dr Galaydh then made overtures to “Somaliland”, then headed by Ahmed Mohamed Mohamoud (Siilaanyo). The two leaders successfully brokered an agreement to amend the constitution, aiming to ensure equitable power-sharing among the northern clans. However, this hard-won compromise was ultimately vetoed by Siilaanyo’s successor Dr. Galaydh faced significant backlash for crossing a red line by embarking on a unilateral and controversial negotiations with Hargeisa. Nevertheless, he has succeeded to expose the true colours of his counterparts without compromising his position. His demand for a Somaliland grounded in equity among all its clans, and his mission for an inclusive federal Somalia, were ultimately rebuffed by both Colonel Muse Bihi and HSM, a revelation that as a minimum served as an eye-opener for his people as to the malevolent realities in Mogadishu and Hargeisa which persist to the present day. The war on Sool and the support for the aggressor Fahiima, a Northeastern lawmaker, to defect to Somaliland is something no one who has stood firmly for the cause of SSC-Khaatumo could accept. It is deeply troubling that she would abandon the cause she fought for and defect to an administration accused of subjecting the people of SSC-Khaatumo to killings, displacement, and repression. Such a decision is not only a serious political misjudgment but, in the eyes of those who have fought for the cause, a deeply wrong and unacceptable act. For Fahiima Quuje and her people, another defining test of their place within Somalia emerged during “Somaliland’s” eight-month war of attrition against the city of LasAnod. The conflict was purely one between two Somali clans, one of them a clear aggressor. Under the circumstances, the Federal Government of Somalia was constitutionally and morally obligated to intervene and halt the violence. At the very least, it should have sided with the victims—particularly since they were defending the unity of Somalia against a separatist entity. Barring direct intervention, it should have, at a minimum, offered public moral support to the wronged party. None of that narrative however has resonated with HSM who, as he stated, saw the fighting purely as an internal matter for “Somaliland”, implying that it was another country and therefore outside his jurisdiction. Additionally, his diabolical downplaying of the scale of the atrocities committed by the secessionists, and his equally reprehensible blocking urgently needed humanitarian aid to the victims, are clearly politically motivated and show whose side he was on. When this is taken together with the lack of dissent from other southern political figures with his partisan actions, it all adds to a collective ambivalence towards the union among the southern political establishment, across regions and clans Liberation Without Reward: The Betrayal of SSC-Khatumo By liberating their territory, the people of the SSC region single-handedly kept the dream of a unified Somalia alive. Yet, their rightful expectation to exist as a fully recognized federal member state has been treated as a pipe dream. Following months of pleading, the region finally received only a hollow, symbolic federal status on paper. This token gesture merely serves President HSM’s political shenanigans to retain power, while the region continues to face systemic marginalization and a denial of its constitutional rights. Compounding and legitimising this injustice is the absolute silence from the wider southern Somali political establishment. No former president, former prime minister, regional leader, or prominent politician has questioned HSM’s discriminatory, punitive, and unconstitutional actions against this nascent northeastern state. This continuing collective stand sends once again a clear, troubling message: the effective borders of the Somali federal project remain confined to the south. History Repeating Itself We are witnessing history repeating itself. The same president who slammed the door on Dr. Ali Khalif Galaydh and his Khatumo movement in 2015 is more or less doing the same containment strategy against its successor in 2026. For Fahiima Quuje, the relentless endless and humiliating denials of her peoples’ constitutional rights under the current administration have surpassed what Galaydh ever faced, and in the end shattered her resolve and forced her to defect to Hargeisa. Yet, this defection is akin to jumping from the frying pan into the fire. Nevertheless, Fahiima’s defection to Somaliland is something no one who has stood firmly for the cause of SSC-Khaatumo could accept. It is deeply troubling that she would abandon the cause she fought for and defect to an administration that subjected the people of SSC-Khaatumo to killings, displacement, and repression. Such a decision is not only a serious political misjudgment but, in the eyes of those who have fought for the cause, a deeply wrong and unacceptable act. It begs the critical questions: What viable choices are left for her people? Where do they go from here? The demise of the union of Somalia is the main casualty of the overthrow of the military government in 1991. It does not count for the federal government which is supposed to be its custodian. It matters even less for the fragmented decentralized autonomous clan-based enclaves. All have shelved it, pay lip service to it, and prioritise their own interests. The exception are the NE people who are dogmatically beholden to an unwanted nominal union as if they are God’s mandated people to defend it when the rest of Somalia have ditched it. That is mission impossible and self-defeating. Getting your priorities right The historic 6 February 2023 Las Anod Declaration promised true regional self-determination and representative governance. Those aspirations came closer to being realised when SSC-Khatumo liberated its occupied regions, setting the stage to fulfil the declaration. Unfortunately, those hopes were compromised when President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud (HSM), in collusion with the then SSC-Khatumo leadership, was allowed to hijack the   August 2025 state formation elections. By securing the selection of handpicked loyalist candidates, the federal government effectively integrated the region into its own political agenda to retain power. Rather than focusing on the urgent task of nation-building for the new Northeast state -cementing the cohesion of its clan partners and strengthening nascent institutions-the current leadership has prioritised alignment with Villa Somalia. This blind loyalty has yielded little to no tangible benefits for the local population. While unwavering loyalty to  the Sayid was a trait of the Darwish, such devotion is not meant for the enemies of their people. The consequences of these compromised elections and the perceived betrayal of the Las Anod Declaration are now becoming clear. The initial unity born of the uprising is fracturing, political cohesion between the two principal clan partners is wearing thin, and the State is drifting without strong, independent leadership. Recent high-profile defections to Hargeisa reflect growing disillusionment with the administration under Abdirisak Firdhiye. While these defections currently represent a small fraction, they could trigger a larger exodus if the administration fails to address the consequences of their neglect and failures. items.fullContent: By Osman Hassan Dr Ali Khalif Galaydh was steeped in the Darwish heritage of freedom loving. He was a paragon of “Somalinimo”, nationalism and staunch unionist and for all that earned the highest posts of government – above all becoming the Prime Minister of Somalia. He is the last person one would expect to renounce all that dear to him and one day embrace the secession that was hitherto an anathema to him. Similarly, Miss Fahiima Quuje was the heroine of the liberation of Sool from the occupying separatists and later became an MP in the parliament of her NE State of Somalia. Who would have thought she would one day repudiate all that legacy and defect to the very enemy she fought. Yet both found themselves on the horns of a dilemma and in the end they choose the unthinkable Most people’s kneejerk reaction is to brand and shame her as another “Horgal”, another infamous defector , another fortune hunters. She is none of that just as Dr Galaydh was not. Their backgrounds simply belie all that. It is therefore appropriate to reflect on at what point each could no longer solder on and threw in the towel, give up on their once cherished union and in favour of the secession that was hitherto their anathema. This paper traces that history and the lessons for their people. Mogadishu is the bane of the unity of Somalia & not Hargeisa The 1991 collapse of the Somali state marked a critical turning point in the history of Somali unity. The subsequent unilateral declaration of independence in the north (former British Somaliland) served as a definitive test of the support for the union. While one specific clan spearheaded the secessionist movement, all other northern clans actively resisted the split, maintaining a steadfast commitment to a unified Somalia in both in word and in deed to this day. In contrast, Somalia’s presidents and Prime Ministers (invariably all southerners) have without exception abdicated their constitutional obligations to oppose the secession and defend the union, Hassan Sheikh Mohamoud (hereafter HSM) being the most manifestly indifferent to it. Far from taking concrete actions to end the secession, HSM is aiding and abetting it to the present day while on the on the other hand openly undermining the struggle of northern unionists to defend the union. Villa Somalia’s actions amount to puling the rug from underneath the union and sending a message to northern unionists to fend for themselves- or worse surrender to their secessionist occupier. Dr Galaydh and Fihiime Quuje eventually yielded to these immense pressures at critical junctures of the struggle. Revisiting these historical turning points is essential to understanding their profound implications for the present-day Northeast (NE) State. Shutting the door on Khatumo For Dr. Galaydh, the then-president of the self-proclaimed Khatumo State, the turning point for the union occurred in July 2015. At that time, President HSM announced that the Galmudug regions would be the final state admitted into the federal system. This declaration sent an unmistakable message to Dr. Galaydh, who had been actively lobbying for Khatumo’s federal inclusion: the northern regions were being excluded from federal Somalia. To him, and to northerners, this decision was tantamount to Mogadishu’s unilateral termination of the union and the ultimate breakup of the country. Dr Ali Khalif Galaydh HSM’s action received the silent endorsement of the entire southern political establishment, as no major political figure dissented at the time or in the years that followed. Ironically, President HSM’s stance closely echoed Hargeisa’s 1991 unilateral declaration of secession. For a brief moment, Mogadishu and Hargeisa aligned, sharing a parallel perspective on the dissolution of the union. It was then that Dr Galaydh made his memorable statement that they thought until then that the unity of Somalia was being undone in Hargeisa but realised then that it was in Mogadishu. With the door to unity closed, Dr Galaydh then made overtures to “Somaliland”, then headed by Ahmed Mohamed Mohamoud (Siilaanyo). The two leaders successfully brokered an agreement to amend the constitution, aiming to ensure equitable power-sharing among the northern clans. However, this hard-won compromise was ultimately vetoed by Siilaanyo’s successor Dr. Galaydh faced significant backlash for crossing a red line by embarking on a unilateral and controversial negotiations with Hargeisa. Nevertheless, he has succeeded to expose the true colours of his counterparts without compromising his position. His demand for a Somaliland grounded in equity among all its clans, and his mission for an inclusive federal Somalia, were ultimately rebuffed by both Colonel Muse Bihi and HSM, a revelation that as a minimum served as an eye-opener for his people as to the malevolent realities in Mogadishu and Hargeisa which persist to the present day. The war on Sool and the support for the aggressor Fahiima, a Northeastern lawmaker, to defect to Somaliland is something no one who has stood firmly for the cause of SSC-Khaatumo could accept. It is deeply troubling that she would abandon the cause she fought for and defect to an administration accused of subjecting the people of SSC-Khaatumo to killings, displacement, and repression. Such a decision is not only a serious political misjudgment but, in the eyes of those who have fought for the cause, a deeply wrong and unacceptable act. For Fahiima Quuje and her people, another defining test of their place within Somalia emerged during “Somaliland’s” eight-month war of attrition against the city of LasAnod. The conflict was purely one between two Somali clans, one of them a clear aggressor. Under the circumstances, the Federal Government of Somalia was constitutionally and morally obligated to intervene and halt the violence. At the very least, it should have sided with the victims—particularly since they were defending the unity of Somalia against a separatist entity. Barring direct intervention, it should have, at a minimum, offered public moral support to the wronged party. None of that narrative however has resonated with HSM who, as he stated, saw the fighting purely as an internal matter for “Somaliland”, implying that it was another country and therefore outside his jurisdiction. Additionally, his diabolical downplaying of the scale of the atrocities committed by the secessionists, and his equally reprehensible blocking urgently needed humanitarian aid to the victims, are clearly politically motivated and show whose side he was on. When this is taken together with the lack of dissent from other southern political figures with his partisan actions, it all adds to a collective ambivalence towards the union among the southern political establishment, across regions and clans Liberation Without Reward: The Betrayal of SSC-Khatumo By liberating their territory, the people of the SSC region single-handedly kept the dream of a unified Somalia alive. Yet, their rightful expectation to exist as a fully recognized federal member state has been treated as a pipe dream. Following months of pleading, the region finally received only a hollow, symbolic federal status on paper. This token gesture merely serves President HSM’s political shenanigans to retain power, while the region continues to face systemic marginalization and a denial of its constitutional rights. Compounding and legitimising this injustice is the absolute silence from the wider southern Somali political establishment. No former president, former prime minister, regional leader, or prominent politician has questioned HSM’s discriminatory, punitive, and unconstitutional actions against this nascent northeastern state. This continuing collective stand sends once again a clear, troubling message: the effective borders of the Somali federal project remain confined to the south. History Repeating Itself We are witnessing history repeating itself. The same president who slammed the door on Dr. Ali Khalif Galaydh and his Khatumo movement in 2015 is more or less doing the same containment strategy against its successor in 2026. For Fahiima Quuje, the relentless endless and humiliating denials of her peoples’ constitutional rights under the current administration have surpassed what Galaydh ever faced, and in the end shattered her resolve and forced her to defect to Hargeisa. Yet, this defection is akin to jumping from the frying pan into the fire. Nevertheless, Fahiima’s defection to Somaliland is something no one who has stood firmly for the cause of SSC-Khaatumo could accept. It is deeply troubling that she would abandon the cause she fought for and defect to an administration that subjected the people of SSC-Khaatumo to killings, displacement, and repression. Such a decision is not only a serious political misjudgment but, in the eyes of those who have fought for the cause, a deeply wrong and unacceptable act. It begs the critical questions: What viable choices are left for her people? Where do they go from here? The demise of the union of Somalia is the main casualty of the overthrow of the military government in 1991. It does not count for the federal government which is supposed to be its custodian. It matters even less for the fragmented decentralized autonomous clan-based enclaves. All have shelved it, pay lip service to it, and prioritise their own interests. The exception are the NE people who are dogmatically beholden to an unwanted nominal union as if they are God’s mandated people to defend it when the rest of Somalia have ditched it. That is mission impossible and self-defeating. Getting your priorities right The historic 6 February 2023 Las Anod Declaration promised true regional self-determination and representative governance. Those aspirations came closer to being realised when SSC-Khatumo liberated its occupied regions, setting the stage to fulfil the declaration. Unfortunately, those hopes were compromised when President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud (HSM), in collusion with the then SSC-Khatumo leadership, was allowed to hijack the   August 2025 state formation elections. items.title: Sababta Masar uga baaqatay heshiiska difaac ee Turkiga, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan
items.description: Qaahira (Caasimada Online) – Markii hoggaamiyeyaasha Sacuudiga, Turkiga iyo Pakistan ay Jimcihii magaalada Makka ku soo bandhigeen heshiis cusub oo difaac wadajir ah, hal dal oo si weyn uga dhex muuqday dadaalladii diblomaasiyadeed ee ka horreeyay heshiiska ayaa ka maqnaa munaasabadda: Masar. Heshiiska oo loogu magac daray Mecca Joint Defense Agreement , ayaa dhigaya in weerar hubeysan oo dibadda kaga yimaada mid ka mid ah saddexda dal loo aqoonsan doono weerar lagu qaaday dhammaantood. Rayed Krimly, wasiir ku-xigeenka Sacuudiga ee diblomaasiyadda dadweynaha, ayaa sheegay in heshiisku u oggolaanayo saddexda dal inay “horumariyaan awoodaha difaac ee wadajirka ah, xoojiyaan awoodda ka-hortagga, sare u qaadaan diyaargarowga, isla markaana sii mideeyaan awoodahooda difaac si wadajir ah looga hortago khatar kasta oo amnigooda ku soo wajahan.” Heshiiska ayaa yimid kadib bilo ay Sacuudiga, Turkiga, Pakistan iyo Masar si dhow uga wada shaqeynayeen dadaallo lagu dejinayo xiisadaha gobolka, gaar ahaan dagaalkii Iran iyo Mareykanka oo saameyn xooggan ku yeeshay dalalka Khaliijka iyo isu-socodka maraakiibta tamarta. Afarta dal waxay lixdii bilood ee lasoo dhaafay yeesheen kulamo xiriir ah, wada-hadallo hoose, xiriirro taleefan oo heer sare ah iyo dadaallo ay dhinacyada isku hayay ugu gudbinayeen farriimo diblomaasiyadeed. Hase yeeshee markii iskaashigaas loo beddelay heshiis rasmi ah oo difaac, Masar waxay dooratay inay bannaanka ka joogto. Ilo ku dhow wada-hadallada Pakistan ayaa Mada Masr u sheegay in Qaahira lagu casuumay inay heshiiska qeyb ka noqoto, balse ay diidday. Wasiirka arrimaha dibadda Turkiga Hakan Fidan ayaa Sabtidii xaqiijiyay in madaxweyne Recep Tayyip Erdogan uu doonayo in isbahaysiga la ballaariyo, Masarna ay ka mid tahay dalalka uu jeclaan lahaa inay ku soo biiraan. “Masar mar horeba waa saaxiibkeen dabiiciga ah dhammaan arrimaha,” ayuu yiri Fidan. “Waxaan aaminsanahay in marxaladda xigta Masar ay sidoo kale naga mid noqon doonto. Durba waxaan ula dhaqannaa sidii dalal xulufo ah. Waxaa jira arrimo farsamo oo yar, marka kuwaas la dhammeeyana ma jirto sabab Masar aysan qeyb uga noqon.” Laakiin dhinaca Qaahira, arrintu sidaas uma fududa. Maxay Masar ka baqeysaa? Saraakiil iyo diblomaasiyiin Masri ah ayaa sheegaya in sababta ugu weyn ee Qaahira uga baaqatay aysan ahayn khilaaf ay kala dhexeyso Turkiga, Pakistan ama Sacuudiga, balse ay tahay nooca siyaasadeed ee heshiiska cusub. Masar waxay heshiiska u aragtaa mid ka baxsan difaac wadajir ah oo keliya, una dhow dhismaha xero siyaasadeed oo uu Sacuudigu hoggaaminayo. Qaahira waxay xiriir wanaagsan la leedahay dalalka heshiiska saxiixay, laakiin ma rabto inay gasho isbahaysi xaddidi kara awooddeeda ay si madax-bannaan ugu maareyso xiriirrada gobolka. Fidan wuxuu heshiiska Makka ku tilmaamay mid la mid ah qodobka shanaad ee heshiiska NATO, kaas oo dhigaya in weerar lagu qaado hal xubin loo arko weerar ka dhan ah dhammaan xubnaha. “Taasi waa sababta loo sameeyo heshiis amni,” ayuu yiri. “Taasi ayaana ah sababta dalal kale ugu dambeyn ugu biiraan isbahaysi — si ay uga faa’iideystaan ilaalinta midba midka kale.” Muddo sanado ah gobolka waxaa laga hadlaayay fikradda dhismaha waxa mararka qaar loogu yeero “NATO Carbeed”, iyadoo Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka Carabta ay labaduba isku dayeen inay door hoggaamineed ku yeeshaan nidaam amni oo cusub oo Bariga Dhexe laga hirgeliyo. Si kastaba, ilo Turki ah ayaa hoos u dhigay fikradda ah in qodobka difaaca wadajirka ahi si toos ah waddamada ugu khasbayo inay dagaal galaan. Sarkaal Turki ah ayaa sheegay in haddii mid ka mid ah dalalka la weeraro ay u badan tahay in marka hore guddiyo saddex geesood ah ay qiimeeyaan xaaladda, kadibna go’aan laga gaaro tallaabada la qaadayo. “Qodobka sheegaya in weerar lagu qaado hal waddan uu yahay weerar lagu qaaday saddexdaba waa arrin aad u culus, waana mid u eg qodobka shanaad ee NATO,” ayuu yiri. Laakiin wuxuu intaas ku daray in fulinta heshiiska ay u badan tahay inay ku xirnaato hannaan wada-tashi iyo codbixin. Sarkaalku wuxuu sheegay in iskaashiga ugu horreeya uusan qasab ahaan noqon doonin ciidamo si wadajir ah u dagaallama, balse uu xoogga saari karo isdhaafsiga xogta sirdoonka iyo xogta radar-ka. “Waxaan u arkaa isbahaysigan inuu yahay xudunta dallad ka-hortag oo ka bilaaban karta bariga Mediterranean-ka kuna fidi karta Badda Carabta,” ayuu yiri. Heshiis difaaca Sacuudiga? Diblomaasi Carbeed oo hore uga soo shaqeeyay Turkiga ayaa qaba in heshiiska, marka dhinaca awoodda militariga laga eego, uu dhab ahaan aad uga faa’iido badan yahay Sacuudiga marka loo eego labada dal ee kale. “Ma filayo in qof uu aaminsan yahay in haddii Turkiga la weeraro uu u baahan doono ciidamada Sacuudiga ama xitaa Pakistan,” ayuu yiri. Sidoo kale wuxuu shaki geliyay in Turkey ama Pakistan ay dagaal toos ah ula geli doonaan Iran ama dal kale si ay Sacuudiga u difaacaan. “Haddii Sacuudigu wajaho khatar militari oo la mid ah tii dalalka Khaliijka ka dhalatay duullaankii Ciraaq ee Kuwait, ma Turkiga iyo Pakistan oo keliya ayuu u carari lahaa?” ayuu weydiiyay. “Jawaabtu waa maya. Wuxuu u baahnaan lahaa isbahaysi dalal diyaar u ah dagaal oo Mareykanku hoggaaminayo, sida kii xoreeyay Kuwait.” Aragtidaas waxaa la wadaaga qaar ka mid ah saraakiisha Masar. Sarkaal sare oo Masri ah ayaa sheegay in inkastoo dalalka Khaliijka ay mararka qaar ka caroodaan siyaasadaha Washington, haddana aysan jirin beddel dhab ah oo ay u haystaan Mareykanka marka laga hadlayo ammaankooda istiraatiijiga ah. “Ma noolaan karaan Mareykanka la’aantiis,” ayuu yiri sarkaalku. Wuxuu sheegay in iskaashiga ay la sameeyaan Turkey, Pakistan, Masar ama dalal kale uu noqon karo mid kaabaya nidaamka jira, balse uusan beddeli karin kaalinta Mareykanka ee difaaca Khaliijka. Taasi waxay qeyb ka tahay sababta Qaahira aysan ugu qanacsaneyn inay gasho heshiis sharci ahaan ama siyaasad ahaan ku qasbi kara inay qeyb ka noqoto difaaca Sacuudiga. Sarkaal hore oo Masri ah ayaa si cad u yiri: “Masar kuma biiri doonto isbahaysi militari oo Sacuudigu hoggaaminayo.” Maxay Qaahira rabtaa? Taas macnaheedu ma aha in Masar ay diidan tahay dhammaan iskaashiga amni ee Sacuudiga. Qaahira waxay hore ugu biirtay qaab-dhismeedka iskaashiga dalalka ku teedsan Badda Cas ee uu Sacuudigu hoggaamiyo, maadaama ay u aragto Badda Cas meel si toos ah ugu xiran amniga qaranka Masar. “Farqigu wuxuu yahay in iskaashiga Badda Cas uu ku saabsan yahay xog-wadaag, wada-tashi iyo difaaca Badda Cas, ee uusan ahayn difaaca Sacuudiga,” ayuu yiri sarkaalka hore ee Masar. Sarkaal kale ayaa sheegay in wasiirrada arrimaha dibadda Masar iyo Qatar ay hore uga wada hadleen sida Qaahira uga qeyb qaadan karto nidaam cusub oo amni oo gobolka laga hirgeliyo. Laakiin wuxuu sheegay in Masar aysan taageersaneyn nidaam ballaaran oo amni oo aan Carab ku koobneyn, gaar ahaan mid ay Turkiga iyo Pakistan door weyn ku leeyihiin. “Masar ma taageersana inay qeyb ka noqoto nidaam amni oo aan Carbeed ahayn,” ayuu yiri. Masar sidoo kale waxay qabtaa in haddii Sacuudigu u baahan yahay taageero militari oo dalalka Carabta ah, ay hore u jirto Heshiiska Difaaca Wadajirka Carabta , kaas oo labada dalba xubno ka yihiin. Sidaas darteed, ilo diblomaasiyadeed ayaa ku doodaya in heshiiska Makka uu leeyahay muhiimad siyaasadeed oo ka weyn tan militari. Diblomaasiga Carbeed ayaa sheegay in fariinta Riyadh ay tahay: “Waxaan awoodnaa, waxaana dhiseynaa istiraatiijiyad difaac oo cusub oo ka gudbaysa nidaamkii hore ee jiray.” Danaha Turkiga iyo Pakistan Turkiga iyo Pakistan-na waxay heshiiska ka leeyihiin xisaab siyaasadeed iyo mid istiraatiiji ah. Il Turki ah ayaa tilmaamay xiriirka sii xoogeysanaya ee India la leedahay Israel iyo Greece, isagoo sheegay in Ankara iyo Islamabad ay arkaan isbeddel juqraafi-siyaasadeed oo labada dhinacba saameynaya. “India oo deris la ah Pakistan waxay xiriir buuxa la leedahay Israel, oo ku dhow Turkiga. India iyo Israel labaduba waxay sidoo kale xiriir la leeyihiin Greece,” ayuu yiri. Sida uu sheegay isha, arrimahaas waxay Ankara iyo Islamabad ku riixayaan inay iyaguna dhistaan shabakad iskaashi oo ka tarjumeysa isbeddelada cusub ee gobolka. Ka hor dagaalkii Gaza ee billowday 2023, India waxay ku dhawaaqday mashruuca India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor , oo qorshihiisu ahaa in India iyo Yurub lagu xiro dekedo iyo tareenno mara Imaaraadka, Sacuudiga, Jordan, Israel iyo Greece. Laakiin dagaalladii iyo khilaafaadkii gobolka ka dhacay ayaa beddelay xisaabihii siyaasadeed iyo dhaqaale, iyadoo dalal badan ay bilaabeen inay raadiyaan waddooyin kale oo ay ku xaqiijinayaan danahooda. Masar ayaa iyaduna ku dhex jirta isla shabakaddaas xiriirrada isdiidan. Diblomaasi hore oo Carbeed ayaa sheegay in Qaahira aysan dooneyn heshiis difaac oo Turkey ay qeyb ka tahay xilli ay xiriir istiraatiiji ah la leedahay Greece iyo Cyprus. Sidoo kale waxay dooneysaa inay sii ballaariso xiriirkeeda dhaqaale ee India, taas oo ka dhigeysa mid aan jeclayn inay si cad ugu soo biirto xero uu Pakistan door muuqda ku leeyahay. Waxaa arrinta sii adkeynaya loollanka sii muuqda ee Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka Carabta ee hoggaanka iyo saameynta gobolka. Qaahira waxay ilaa hadda isku dayday inay ka fogaato inay si cad dhinac uga raacdo Riyadh ama Abu Dhabi. Sarkaal hore oo Masri ah ayaa sheegay in Masar ay Sacuudiga ugu baahan tahay arrimo badan oo siyaasadda dibadda ah, gaar ahaan marka laga hadlayo Sudan iyo Soomaaliya, halka Imaaraadku dhinaca kale yahay maal-galiye aad muhiim ugu ah dhaqaalaha Masar. Sidaas darteed Qaahira waxay dooneysaa inay xiriirka labada dhinacba ilaashato. Aragtidaas ayaa sharxaysa sababta Masar, inkastoo ay qeyb muhiim ah ka ahayd dadaalladii diblomaasiyadeed ee gogosha u xaadhay iskaashiga cusub, ay uga maqneyd sawirkii Jimcihii laga qaaday Makka. Marka laga eego dhinaca Qaahira, ku biirista heshiiska cusub ma aha oo keliya go’aan ku saabsan difaac wadajir ah. Waxay sidoo kale ka dhigan tahay doorasho xero siyaasadeed oo gobolka ah — doorasho aysan Masar xilligan diyaar u ahayn inay sameyso. Rayed Krimly, wasiir ku-xigeenka Sacuudiga ee diblomaasiyadda dadweynaha, ayaa sheegay in heshiisku u oggolaanayo saddexda dal inay “horumariyaan awoodaha difaac ee wadajirka ah, xoojiyaan awoodda ka-hortagga, sare u qaadaan diyaargarowga, isla markaana sii mideeyaan awoodahooda difaac si wadajir ah looga hortago khatar kasta oo amnigooda ku soo wajahan.” Heshiiska ayaa yimid kadib bilo ay Sacuudiga, Turkiga, Pakistan iyo Masar si dhow uga wada shaqeynayeen dadaallo lagu dejinayo xiisadaha gobolka, gaar ahaan dagaalkii Iran iyo Mareykanka oo saameyn xooggan ku yeeshay dalalka Khaliijka iyo isu-socodka maraakiibta tamarta. Afarta dal waxay lixdii bilood ee lasoo dhaafay yeesheen kulamo xiriir ah, wada-hadallo hoose, xiriirro taleefan oo heer sare ah iyo dadaallo ay dhinacyada isku hayay ugu gudbinayeen farriimo diblomaasiyadeed. Hase yeeshee markii iskaashigaas loo beddelay heshiis rasmi ah oo difaac, Masar waxay dooratay inay bannaanka ka joogto. Ilo ku dhow wada-hadallada Pakistan ayaa Mada Masr u sheegay in Qaahira lagu casuumay inay heshiiska qeyb ka noqoto, balse ay diidday. Wasiirka arrimaha dibadda Turkiga Hakan Fidan ayaa Sabtidii xaqiijiyay in madaxweyne Recep Tayyip Erdogan uu doonayo in isbahaysiga la ballaariyo, Masarna ay ka mid tahay dalalka uu jeclaan lahaa inay ku soo biiraan. “Masar mar horeba waa saaxiibkeen dabiiciga ah dhammaan arrimaha,” ayuu yiri Fidan. “Waxaan aaminsanahay in marxaladda xigta Masar ay sidoo kale naga mid noqon doonto. Durba waxaan ula dhaqannaa sidii dalal xulufo ah. Waxaa jira arrimo farsamo oo yar, marka kuwaas la dhammeeyana ma jirto sabab Masar aysan qeyb uga noqon.” Laakiin dhinaca Qaahira, arrintu sidaas uma fududa. Maxay Masar ka baqeysaa? Saraakiil iyo diblomaasiyiin Masri ah ayaa sheegaya in sababta ugu weyn ee Qaahira uga baaqatay aysan ahayn khilaaf ay kala dhexeyso Turkiga, Pakistan ama Sacuudiga, balse ay tahay nooca siyaasadeed ee heshiiska cusub. Masar waxay heshiiska u aragtaa mid ka baxsan difaac wadajir ah oo keliya, una dhow dhismaha xero siyaasadeed oo uu Sacuudigu hoggaaminayo. Qaahira waxay xiriir wanaagsan la leedahay dalalka heshiiska saxiixay, laakiin ma rabto inay gasho isbahaysi xaddidi kara awooddeeda ay si madax-bannaan ugu maareyso xiriirrada gobolka. Fidan wuxuu heshiiska Makka ku tilmaamay mid la mid ah qodobka shanaad ee heshiiska NATO, kaas oo dhigaya in weerar lagu qaado hal xubin loo arko weerar ka dhan ah dhammaan xubnaha. “Taasi waa sababta loo sameeyo heshiis amni,” ayuu yiri. “Taasi ayaana ah sababta dalal kale ugu dambeyn ugu biiraan isbahaysi — si ay uga faa’iideystaan ilaalinta midba midka kale.” Muddo sanado ah gobolka waxaa laga hadlaayay fikradda dhismaha waxa mararka qaar loogu yeero “NATO Carbeed”, iyadoo Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka Carabta ay labaduba isku dayeen inay door hoggaamineed ku yeeshaan nidaam amni oo cusub oo Bariga Dhexe laga hirgeliyo. Si kastaba, ilo Turki ah ayaa hoos u dhigay fikradda ah in qodobka difaaca wadajirka ahi si toos ah waddamada ugu khasbayo inay dagaal galaan. Sarkaal Turki ah ayaa sheegay in haddii mid ka mid ah dalalka la weeraro ay u badan tahay in marka hore guddiyo saddex geesood ah ay qiimeeyaan xaaladda, kadibna go’aan laga gaaro tallaabada la qaadayo. “Qodobka sheegaya in weerar lagu qaado hal waddan uu yahay weerar lagu qaaday saddexdaba waa arrin aad u culus, waana mid u eg qodobka shanaad ee NATO,” ayuu yiri. Laakiin wuxuu intaas ku daray in fulinta heshiiska ay u badan tahay inay ku xirnaato hannaan wada-tashi iyo codbixin. Sarkaalku wuxuu sheegay in iskaashiga ugu horreeya uusan qasab ahaan noqon doonin ciidamo si wadajir ah u dagaallama, balse uu xoogga saari karo isdhaafsiga xogta sirdoonka iyo xogta radar-ka. “Waxaan u arkaa isbahaysigan inuu yahay xudunta dallad ka-hortag oo ka bilaaban karta bariga Mediterranean-ka kuna fidi karta Badda Carabta,” ayuu yiri. Heshiis difaaca Sacuudiga? Diblomaasi Carbeed oo hore uga soo shaqeeyay Turkiga ayaa qaba in heshiiska, marka dhinaca awoodda militariga laga eego, uu dhab ahaan aad uga faa’iido badan yahay Sacuudiga marka loo eego labada dal ee kale. “Ma filayo in qof uu aaminsan yahay in haddii Turkiga la weeraro uu u baahan doono ciidamada Sacuudiga ama xitaa Pakistan,” ayuu yiri. Sidoo kale wuxuu shaki geliyay in Turkey ama Pakistan ay dagaal toos ah ula geli doonaan Iran ama dal kale si ay Sacuudiga u difaacaan. “Haddii Sacuudigu wajaho khatar militari oo la mid ah tii dalalka Khaliijka ka dhalatay duullaankii Ciraaq ee Kuwait, ma Turkiga iyo Pakistan oo keliya ayuu u carari lahaa?” ayuu weydiiyay. “Jawaabtu waa maya. Wuxuu u baahnaan lahaa isbahaysi dalal diyaar u ah dagaal oo Mareykanku hoggaaminayo, sida kii xoreeyay Kuwait.” Aragtidaas waxaa la wadaaga qaar ka mid ah saraakiisha Masar. Sarkaal sare oo Masri ah ayaa sheegay in inkastoo dalalka Khaliijka ay mararka qaar ka caroodaan siyaasadaha Washington, haddana aysan jirin beddel dhab ah oo ay u haystaan Mareykanka marka laga hadlayo ammaankooda istiraatiijiga ah. “Ma noolaan karaan Mareykanka la’aantiis,” ayuu yiri sarkaalku. Wuxuu sheegay in iskaashiga ay la sameeyaan Turkey, Pakistan, Masar ama dalal kale uu noqon karo mid kaabaya nidaamka jira, balse uusan beddeli karin kaalinta Mareykanka ee difaaca Khaliijka. Taasi waxay qeyb ka tahay sababta Qaahira aysan ugu qanacsaneyn inay gasho heshiis sharci ahaan ama siyaasad ahaan ku qasbi kara inay qeyb ka noqoto difaaca Sacuudiga. Sarkaal hore oo Masri ah ayaa si cad u yiri: “Masar kuma biiri doonto isbahaysi militari oo Sacuudigu hoggaaminayo.” Maxay Qaahira rabtaa? Taas macnaheedu ma aha in Masar ay diidan tahay dhammaan iskaashiga amni ee Sacuudiga. Qaahira waxay hore ugu biirtay qaab-dhismeedka iskaashiga dalalka ku teedsan Badda Cas ee uu Sacuudigu hoggaamiyo, maadaama ay u aragto Badda Cas meel si toos ah ugu xiran amniga qaranka Masar. “Farqigu wuxuu yahay in iskaashiga Badda Cas uu ku saabsan yahay xog-wadaag, wada-tashi iyo difaaca Badda Cas, ee uusan ahayn difaaca Sacuudiga,” ayuu yiri sarkaalka hore ee Masar. Sarkaal kale ayaa sheegay in wasiirrada arrimaha dibadda Masar iyo Qatar ay hore uga wada hadleen sida Qaahira uga qeyb qaadan karto nidaam cusub oo amni oo gobolka laga hirgeliyo. Laakiin wuxuu sheegay in Masar aysan taageersaneyn nidaam ballaaran oo amni oo aan Carab ku koobneyn, gaar ahaan mid ay Turkiga iyo Pakistan door weyn ku leeyihiin. “Masar ma taageersana inay qeyb ka noqoto nidaam amni oo aan Carbeed ahayn,” ayuu yiri. Masar sidoo kale waxay qabtaa in haddii Sacuudigu u baahan yahay taageero militari oo dalalka Carabta ah, ay hore u jirto Heshiiska Difaaca Wadajirka Carabta , kaas oo labada dalba xubno ka yihiin. Sidaas darteed, ilo diblomaasiyadeed ayaa ku doodaya in heshiiska Makka uu leeyahay muhiimad siyaasadeed oo ka weyn tan militari. Diblomaasiga Carbeed ayaa sheegay in fariinta Riyadh ay tahay: “Waxaan awoodnaa, waxaana dhiseynaa istiraatiijiyad difaac oo cusub oo ka gudbaysa nidaamkii hore ee jiray.” Danaha Turkiga iyo Pakistan Turkiga iyo Pakistan-na waxay heshiiska ka leeyihiin xisaab siyaasadeed iyo mid istiraatiiji ah. Il Turki ah ayaa tilmaamay xiriirka sii xoogeysanaya ee India la leedahay Israel iyo Greece, isagoo sheegay in Ankara iyo Islamabad ay arkaan isbeddel juqraafi-siyaasadeed oo labada dhinacba saameynaya. “India oo deris la ah Pakistan waxay xiriir buuxa la leedahay Israel, oo ku dhow Turkiga. India iyo Israel labaduba waxay sidoo kale xiriir la leeyihiin Greece,” ayuu yiri. Sida uu sheegay isha, arrimahaas waxay Ankara iyo Islamabad ku riixayaan inay iyaguna dhistaan shabakad iskaashi oo ka tarjumeysa isbeddelada cusub ee gobolka. Ka hor dagaalkii Gaza ee billowday 2023, India waxay ku dhawaaqday mashruuca India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor , oo qorshihiisu ahaa in India iyo Yurub lagu xiro dekedo iyo tareenno mara Imaaraadka, Sacuudiga, Jordan, Israel iyo Greece. Laakiin dagaalladii iyo khilaafaadkii gobolka ka dhacay ayaa beddelay xisaabihii siyaasadeed iyo dhaqaale, iyadoo dalal badan ay bilaabeen inay raadiyaan waddooyin kale oo ay ku xaqiijinayaan danahooda. Masar ayaa iyaduna ku dhex jirta isla shabakaddaas xiriirrada isdiidan. Diblomaasi hore oo Carbeed ayaa sheegay in Qaahira aysan dooneyn heshiis difaac oo Turkey ay qeyb ka tahay xilli ay xiriir istiraatiiji ah la leedahay Greece iyo Cyprus. Sidoo kale waxay dooneysaa inay sii ballaariso xiriirkeeda dhaqaale ee India, taas oo ka dhigeysa mid aan jeclayn inay si cad ugu soo biirto xero uu Pakistan door muuqda ku leeyahay. Waxaa arrinta sii adkeynaya loollanka sii muuqda ee Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka Carabta ee hoggaanka iyo saameynta gobolka. Qaahira waxay ilaa hadda isku dayday inay ka fogaato inay si cad dhinac uga raacdo Riyadh ama Abu Dhabi. Sarkaal hore oo Masri ah ayaa sheegay in Masar ay Sacuudiga ugu baahan tahay arrimo badan oo siyaasadda dibadda ah, gaar ahaan marka laga hadlayo Sudan iyo Soomaaliya, halka Imaaraadku dhinaca kale yahay maal-galiye aad muhiim ugu ah dhaqaalaha Masar. Sidaas darteed Qaahira waxay dooneysaa inay xiriirka labada dhinacba ilaashato. Aragtidaas ayaa sharxaysa sababta Masar, inkastoo ay qeyb muhiim ah ka ahayd dadaalladii diblomaasiyadeed ee gogosha u xaadhay iskaashiga cusub, ay uga maqneyd sawirkii Jimcihii laga qaaday Makka. Marka laga eego dhinaca Qaahira, ku biirista heshiiska cusub ma aha oo keliya go’aan ku saabsan difaac wadajir ah. Waxay sidoo kale ka dhigan tahay doorasho xero siyaasadeed oo gobolka ah — doorasho aysan Masar xilligan diyaar u ahayn inay sameyso. The post Sababta Masar uga baaqatay heshiiska difaac ee Turkiga, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Japan Oo Rajo Cusub U Abuurtay Dadka somalida Ilkaha Waayay  si loogu abuuro ilko cusub
items.description: Cilmi-baaris Japan ah oo ku saabsan koritaanka ilkaha cusub Cilmi-baarayaal ka tirsan Jaamacadda Kyoto ee dalka Japan ayaa billaawday tijaabooyin bini’aadam ah oo ku saabsan daaweyn cusub oo loogu talagalay inay ka caawiso dadka inay ilko cusub u koraan si dabiici ah taas oo laga yaabo inay beddesho habka ilkaha la beddelo mustaqbalka. Daaweyntan oo hore loogu tilmaami jiray khayaali saynis ayaa hadda lagu tijaabinayaa dadka waxaanay ujeeddadeedu tahay in la bixiyo beddel ka mid ah maalgashiga ilkaha (implants) iyo ilkaha macmalka ah. Tijaabooyinkan ayaa muhiim u ah sababtoo ah waxay furaan albaab cusub oo ku saabsan sida ay ilkuhu u koraan, taasoo laga yaabo inay u fududayso dadka farabadan oo ilkaha ku waayay da’da dhaawacyada cudurrada ama xaaladaha hidde-sideed. Bini’aadamku wuxuu leeyahay laba nooc oo ilko ah: ilkaha caanaha (baby teeth) iyo ilkaha joogtada ah (permanent teeth). Si kastaba ha ahaatee cilmi-baarayaashu waxay rumeysan yihiin in daanka bini’aadamka uu ka kooban yahay burooyin ilko oo seexda kuwaas oo laga yaabo inay noqon karaan ilko cusub haddii la kiciyo. Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay diiradda saareen borotiin la yiraahdo USAG-1, kaas oo kaalin ka ciyaara xakamaynta calaamadaha ku lugta leh samaynta ilkaha. Waxay ogaadeen in xakamaynta USAG-1 ay kiciso burooyinka ilkaha oo ay dhiirrigeliso in ilko cusub ay koraan. Tijaabooyin hore oo lagu sameeyay jiirarka ferrets iyo eeyaha ayaa muujiyay natiijooyin dhiirrigelin leh oo ay ku jiraan koritaanka ilko cusub. Tijaabooyinka bini’aadamka ah oo ah kuwa ugu horreeya, ayaa lagu sameynayaa Jaamacadda Kyoto waxaana ka qayb galaya rag waaweyn oo caafimaad qaba oo da’doodu u dhaxayso 30 ilaa 64 sano . Diiradda ayaa la saaray ilkaha dambe si loo yareeyo welwelka ku saabsan muuqaalka, waxaana la siinayaa qiyaas loogu talagalay inay xakameyso USAG-1. Hadii tijaabooyinka ay sii wataan inay muujiyaan natiijooyin wanaagsan cilmi-baarayaashu waxay rajeynayaan in daaweynta la sii ballaariyo dadka waaweyn ee ilkaha ku waayay. The post Japan Oo Rajo Cusub U Abuurtay Dadka somalida Ilkaha Waayay si loogu abuuro ilko cusub first appeared on Radio Dalsan .

items.title: Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur elected speaker of Somali parliament
items.description: Mogadishu, Somalia- The Somali parliament on Monday elected Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, a lawmaker who completed his higher education in Türkiye, as its new speaker. Nur, who was the ports and transport minister, received 142 votes, defeating Abdulkadir Omar Maolim, who got 30. The lower house of parliament has 275 members. He took the oath of office after the vote. Nur, an influential politician in the country for nearly a decade, studied international relations at Ankara University’s Faculty of Political Sciences from 2012 to 2016, where he completed his bachelor’s degree. He also worked at Somalia’s embassy in the Turkish capital. Constitutionally, the speaker is considered the second-most powerful leader in the Horn of Africa country, after the president. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud congratulated the new speaker, urging him to lead the house in accordance with the Constitution. He reassured the speaker of his and the executive branch’s full support. Source: AA The post Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur elected speaker of Somali parliament appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: A Parliament in Limbo: Why the Election of a New Speaker May be Less a Crisis Than a Necessary Act of Continuity
items.description: By Mohamed A Yasin Somalia’s political crisis has produced a constitutional paradox that increasingly defies conventional political logic: a Parliament whose mandate expired months ago continues to sit, a presidency whose mandate has also expired remains in office, and negotiations between the Federal Government and the opposition—despite repeated rounds of internationally mediated talks—have yet to produce an agreement on how the country should proceed. In the middle of this uncertainty, one question has become unavoidable: if there is no political agreement and no agreed timetable for a new Parliament, should the existing House of the People simply abandon its chamber and leave the country without a functioning legislature? That is the dilemma facing Somalia. The 11th Parliament’s mandate expired on April 14, 2026. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s mandate subsequently expired on May 15. Yet neither a new Parliament nor a new president has emerged because the country’s political leadership remains locked in negotiations over the electoral and constitutional arrangements that will determine the next phase of the transition. International partners have repeatedly encouraged the government and opposition to reach a compromise. Meeting after meeting has been convened. Statements have been issued. Political delegations have traveled, consulted, and negotiated. But the fundamental disagreement remains unresolved.There is still no political settlement capable of providing Somalia with a universally accepted electoral roadmap. So What Was Parliament Supposed to Do? The question becomes particularly important when viewed against the circumstances surrounding the vacant speakership. Former Speaker Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur (Aden Madoobe) left the position after being elected President of Southwest State. His departure created a vacancy at the top of the House of the People at precisely the moment when Somalia’s constitutional order was already under extraordinary pressure. Rather than leaving the institution without a permanent presiding officer, the 11th Parliament proceeded to elect a new Speaker. Abdulqadir Mohamed Nur Jama, a relatively young but experienced Somali political figure, emerged as the winner. Jama brings considerable experience in Somalia’s political, legal, security, and administrative affairs. He has previously served as Minister of Justice, Minister of Defense, and Minister of Ports and Transport, and has also served as Deputy Commander of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) and as a senior adviser to Speaker Mohamed Mursal Sheikh Abdirahman during the 10th Parliament. His election has immediately generated controversy, particularly among opposition groups who argue that the 11th Parliament’s mandate had already expired and therefore question the legitimacy or necessity of electing a new Speaker. That criticism deserves to be heard. But it also raises a larger question that has not been adequately answered: What is the alternative? Should the House of the People simply close its doors indefinitely? Should MPs abandon their institutional responsibilities while politicians negotiate without a deadline? Should Somalia deliberately create a legislative vacuum while waiting for rival political camps to agree on an electoral formula? Or should existing institutions continue performing essential functions until a political agreement produces legitimate successor institutions? These are not merely procedural questions. They go to the heart of Somalia’s institutional survival. An Expired Mandate Does Not Automatically Mean Institutional Anarchy Somalia’s current predicament is unusual precisely because almost every major political institution is operating in a contested constitutional environment. The President’s mandate has expired. The Parliament’s mandate has expired. The electoral process remains disputed. The constitutional framework itself is contested. And the opposition and government have yet to agree on the mechanism through which political authority should transition. Under such circumstances, there is a legitimate distinction between constitutional legitimacy and institutional continuity. The fact that Somalia has not yet agreed on the next political arrangement does not necessarily mean that every existing state institution should cease functioning overnight. Indeed, doing so could create a far more dangerous situation. A functioning legislature—even one operating under a contested transitional arrangement—may provide a degree of institutional continuity that is preferable to an empty Parliament and an expanding political vacuum. The alternative could be political paralysis without any institutional mechanism capable of managing it. The Opposition’s Criticism Opposition leaders have criticized the decision to elect Jama, arguing that the outgoing Parliament should not be making major institutional decisions after its mandate expired. Their concern is understandable. If Parliament’s mandate has ended, any action it takes inevitably raises questions about constitutional authority. But criticism becomes more compelling when accompanied by a practical alternative. So far, the central political problem remains unresolved: there is no agreed successor institution. The opposition has not yet produced a universally accepted mechanism through which the country can move from the expired 11th Parliament to a legitimate 12th Parliament while negotiations continue. That is the uncomfortable reality.  It is easy to say that Parliament should not elect a Speaker. It is considerably harder to explain what should replace the institution while the government and opposition remain unable to agree. Somalia cannot be governed indefinitely through political objections alone. At some point, every political actor must present a workable pathway through the crisis. Why Jama’s Election Matters Jama’s election therefore carries significance beyond the question of who occupies the Speaker’s chair. He inherits a Parliament operating under extraordinary political circumstances. At the same time, he enters the office at a moment when Somalia desperately needs institutional reform, modernization, and greater public confidence in its legislative institutions. Jama is young, educated, and has accumulated considerable experience in Somali political and security affairs. Those qualities could prove valuable if he chooses to use the speakership not simply as a ceremonial position, but as an opportunity to modernize the House of the People. Somalia’s Parliament has long faced criticism over weak legislative oversight, limited transparency, inadequate research capacity, poor public engagement, and the perception that MPs frequently follow political instructions rather than independently scrutinizing government policy. The new Speaker has an opportunity to challenge that culture. He could strengthen parliamentary committees. He could improve legislative research and drafting. He could expand public access to parliamentary proceedings.He could modernize parliamentary administration and digital systems. He could strengthen financial and administrative accountability. And, perhaps most importantly, he could seek to restore the idea that Parliament exists not merely to endorse political decisions but to scrutinize the executive and represent the Somali people. But How Long Can He Serve? This is perhaps the biggest uncertainty surrounding Jama’s election. Nobody can say with confidence how long the 11th Parliament will remain in place. If the government and opposition reach an agreement tomorrow, the political landscape could change rapidly. If negotiations continue for months, however, the question of institutional continuity will become even more pressing. The Speaker therefore enters an office whose duration is uncertain, but whose responsibilities are immediate. That reality should encourage restraint. The new Speaker should not interpret his election as a mandate to perpetuate the 11th Parliament indefinitely. Nor should the government use the existence of a functioning legislature as an excuse to postpone an eventual political settlement. Instead, the speakership should be understood as part of a broader effort to keep the state functioning while Somali political leaders negotiate a legitimate path forward. Somalia Cannot Afford Another Institutional Vacuum The most dangerous outcome of the current crisis would not necessarily be the election of a controversial Speaker. It would be the collapse of institutional authority altogether. Somalia has spent decades trying to rebuild state institutions after the collapse of the central government in 1991. The country has paid an enormous price for political fragmentation, institutional weakness, and competing claims to legitimacy. Today, Al-Shabaab continues to exploit governance gaps. Federal and state authorities remain politically divided. International partners continue to play a major role in Somalia’s security and institutional development. Against that backdrop, deliberately allowing Parliament to become completely dysfunctional would be difficult to justify without a clear alternative. Political leaders must therefore distinguish between challenging the legality of an institution and destroying its functionality without providing a replacement. The first is legitimate political debate. The second risks creating precisely the vacuum that Somalia’s enemies have historically exploited. A Difficult Moment Demands More Than Criticism Somalia’s opposition has every right to challenge the election of a new Speaker. But the country needs more than criticism. It needs solutions. If opposition leaders believe the 11th Parliament should no longer exercise legislative authority, they should explain precisely what mechanism should replace it. If they believe a caretaker arrangement is necessary, they should present a detailed proposal. If they believe an immediate election is possible, they should explain how it can be organized, financed, and secured. And if they believe the government and opposition should continue negotiations, they must also address how state institutions will function while those negotiations continue. Somalia cannot remain suspended indefinitely between an expired political order and an unborn one. The Bigger Test The election of Jama may ultimately prove to be either a footnote or an important moment in Somalia’s institutional history. Much will depend on what he does with the office. If he uses it to modernize Parliament, strengthen oversight, improve legislative professionalism, and defend institutional independence, his tenure could leave a meaningful legacy regardless of how long it lasts. If, however, the speakership becomes another instrument of political competition, the opportunity will have been lost. For now, Somalia remains caught between an expired mandate and an unresolved future. The government’s mandate has expired. Parliament’s mandate has expired. Until the country’s political leaders agree on a legitimate successor to the existing institutions, some form of institutional continuity remains necessary. The real challenge, therefore, is not whether Somalia should have a functioning Parliament while negotiations continue. That is the question that deserves an answer.
