items.title: After Twenty Years: Renewing Somalia’s Political Settlement
items.description: By Mohamed Abdirizak , the former minister of foreign affairs of Somalia Why the next phase of state-building requires a renewed political consensus A diplomat recently asked me a question that has remained with me ever since. “Will Somalia ever be a united country again?” It was not the question itself that stayed with me. Diplomats ask difficult questions for a living. What struck me was that an experienced observer of Somalia’s long journey would now ask such a fundamental question about the country’s future. Twenty years ago, the question was very different. The international community and Somali leaders were asking whether the Somali state could be rebuilt after more than a decade of collapse. Could Somalis establish national institutions? Could they reconcile former adversaries? Could they agree on a constitutional framework? Could they defeat violent extremism and restore the authority of the state? Those questions produced the political settlement that emerged in 2004. The issue is no longer whether the Somali state can be rebuilt. It is whether the political settlement that made reconstruction possible can continue to sustain a country that has changed profoundly over the last two decades. This is not an argument that the post-2004 settlement has failed. On the contrary, it achieved what many believed impossible. It restored Somalia’s international legitimacy, re-established national institutions, created a framework for federal governance, and gave the country an opportunity to emerge from one of the longest periods of state collapse in modern history. No political settlement is permanent. They are designed for the circumstances in which they are negotiated. As countries change, political settlements must change with them. I believe Somalia has reached that moment. A Different Somalia The Somalia of 2026 is not the Somalia of 2004. The country is younger, more urban, more connected to the outside world, and more strategically important than at any time since the collapse of the state in 1991. According to current demographic estimates, Somalia’s median age is approximately 16.6 years. Most Somalis have no memory of civil war or of the painstaking negotiations that shaped the post-transition political order. They inherited its institutions but not the circumstances that produced them. The regional environment has also changed dramatically. The Red Sea has become one of the world’s most strategically contested waterways. Competition among regional and global powers has intensified. Security challenges in the Horn of Africa are increasingly intertwined with developments in the Gulf, the Suez Canal, and the wider Middle East. At the same time, international priorities are shifting. The willingness of external partners to provide open-ended political, financial and security support can no longer be taken for granted. Yet much of Somalia’s political debate remains anchored in the assumptions of twenty years ago. This disconnect between the Somalia of today and the political settlement of 2004 deserves far greater attention than it has received. The Achievement of 2004 It is important to begin by acknowledging what the post-2004 political settlement accomplished. Those of us who were involved in Somalia’s state-building efforts understood that there was no perfect solution. Federalism, power-sharing arrangements, and transitional institutions were not adopted because everyone agreed on every detail. They were adopted because they represented the most practical means of rebuilding trust after years of conflict and restoring a functioning Somali state. The settlement that emerged from the peace process was, above all, a political compromise. It accommodated competing interests, created space for reconciliation, and gradually rebuilt national institutions. Without that compromise, Somalia would not have returned to international diplomacy, developed permanent federal institutions, or begun the long process of constitutional reconstruction. Its achievements deserve recognition. But it is equally important to recognize its limitations. The settlement was designed to end a period of state collapse. It was not intended to become the final blueprint for governing Somalia indefinitely. Peace agreements create opportunities. They do not eliminate the need for political renewal. Twenty years later, many of the country’s most fundamental constitutional and political questions remain unresolved. The Federal Compact Under Pressure The strength of any federal system ultimately depends less on constitutional text than on political confidence. Federal governments and constituent states will disagree. That is the nature of every federation. What matters is whether those disagreements are resolved through institutions that all sides regard as legitimate. Recent political developments suggest that this confidence has weakened. Political disputes surrounding leadership transitions in Southwest State and Galmudug, the commencement of the Hirshabelle electoral process, continuing disagreements with Puntland and Jubaland, and broader disputes over constitutional amendments and electoral reforms are often discussed as separate issues. In reality, they are symptoms of a larger challenge. For the first time since the federal system was established, several pillars of Somalia’s political settlement appear to be under strain simultaneously. The constitutional review remains contested. Relations between the Federal Government and some Federal Member States have deteriorated. There is no national consensus on the electoral framework. Trust among key political stakeholders has declined.  Individually, each of these problems is manageable.Taken together, they point to something more significant: a gradual weakening of the political compact that has held Somalia together since 2004. That should concern all Somalis. Constitutional Politics Cannot Replace Constitutional Consensus Perhaps no issue better illustrates Somalia’s current predicament than the unfinished constitution. The constitutional review process was intended to complete Somalia’s transition from conflict management to constitutional governance. Instead, constitutional questions have increasingly become the principal arena of political contestation. Disagreements over the division of powers, electoral arrangements, the relationship between the Federal Government and the Federal Member States, and the procedures for constitutional amendment continue to generate political uncertainty. Constitutions are meant to provide the rules within which politics takes place. They should not themselves become the principal object of political conflict. No constitutional order can command lasting legitimacy if significant political actors believe that fundamental rules are being determined without broad national consensus. For Somalia, completing the constitution is no longer simply a legal exercise. It is an essential step toward rebuilding political trust. A Changing Strategic Environment While Somalia has struggled to resolve its internal political questions, its strategic importance has increased considerably. The Horn of Africa has become central to global maritime security. Instability in the Red Sea has elevated Somalia’s strategic importance and intensified competition among regional and international powers. Somalia’s long coastline and location at the gateway to the Red Sea present significant opportunities—but also significant responsibilities. Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Türkiye, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, the United States, the European Union and others all have legitimate interests in Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa. That should not surprise anyone. Every nation pursues its own strategic interests. The challenge for Somalia is not how to avoid international competition. It is how to ensure that external partnerships reinforce Somali sovereignty rather than substitute for Somali political consensus. Strong states manage geopolitical competition. Weak states become arenas in which others compete.Somalia cannot afford the latter. International Patience Is Not Unlimited For more than three decades, Somalia has benefited from extraordinary international support. The United Nations, the African Union, bilateral partners and international financial institutions have invested enormous political, financial and diplomatic resources in supporting Somalia’s recovery. Many Somalis understandably came to assume that this level of engagement would continue indefinitely.Recent developments suggest otherwise. The decision by the United States to oppose further United Nations logistical and operational support for the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) beyond the current mandate ending on 31 December 2026 is significant not simply because of its financial implications. It signals a broader reassessment of long-standing international approaches to Somalia’s security and state-building. Whether driven by changing global priorities, competing crises or frustration with Somalia’s prolonged political deadlock, the message is difficult to ignore. International partnerships will remain important. But no external partner can indefinitely substitute for Somali political agreement. Ultimately, the future of the Somali state will be determined not in foreign capitals, but by the ability of Somalis themselves to reach durable political consensus. Leadership in a More Competitive World Throughout my career in public service, I have consistently believed that Somalia’s unity is both a historical responsibility and a strategic necessity. That conviction has not changed. Neither has another lesson I have learned through years of diplomacy and public service. International partners can support peace. They can finance development. They can assist security institutions. They cannot create political legitimacy. Only Somalis can do that. The coming years will require a different kind of leadership—leadership capable of engaging confidently with multiple international partners while remaining firmly anchored in a national vision that transcends personalities, electoral cycles and political rivalries. The true measure of leadership is not the number of international partnerships a country attracts. It is whether those partnerships strengthen national institutions and advance the long-term interests of the state. The Generation Waiting for Tomorrow Perhaps the greatest challenge facing Somalia receives the least attention. Somalia is one of the youngest countries in the world. The median age is just over sixteen years. Most young Somalis have no personal memory of state collapse, the Arta Conference, the Mbagathi peace process, or the difficult negotiations that produced the federal system. They have inherited the institutions that emerged from those efforts, but they did not participate in creating them. Their aspirations are understandably different. They are concerned with education, employment, entrepreneurship, technology, and the opportunities that will allow them to build productive lives. They want accountable institutions, economic opportunity, and a country that competes successfully in the region and the wider world. Yet much of Somalia’s political discourse remains consumed by the unfinished business of yesterday. The generation that rebuilt the Somali state after collapse was understandably preoccupied with restoring peace and preventing renewed conflict. That was its historic responsibility. The responsibility of this generation is different. It must transform a successful peace settlement into a durable constitutional democracy. No political settlement can remain legitimate indefinitely if it does not evolve with the society it serves. Institutions that once inspired confidence can gradually lose public support if they fail to respond to changing realities. Political renewal is therefore not a rejection of the past. It is the means by which the achievements of the past are preserved. Renewing Somalia’s Political Settlement If Somalia’s greatest challenge is no longer rebuilding the state but strengthening it, then our national conversation must also change. For much of the last two decades, political debate has revolved around the mechanics of governance: power-sharing formulas, constitutional provisions, electoral systems, institutional mandates, and the allocation of authority between different levels of government. These debates are important. But they are not the destination. They are the instruments through which we pursue a larger objective. That objective is to build a Somali state that enjoys the confidence of its citizens, commands the respect of its neighbors, protects its sovereignty, and creates opportunities for future generations.That requires a renewed political settlement. By renewal, I do not mean abandoning the achievements of 2004 or beginning another prolonged transitional process. Somalia has already spent too many years in transition. Nor do I suggest that every institution created over the past two decades should be reconsidered. The opposite is true. The achievements of the post-2004 settlement should be preserved. But they must now be strengthened by a broader national consensus capable of addressing the constitutional, political, and strategic realities of today. A renewed political settlement should pursue several objectives. It should restore trust between the Federal Government and the Federal Member States.  It should complete the Provisional Constitution through broad national consensus.  It should establish an electoral framework accepted across the political spectrum. Equally important, it must strengthen institutions rather than personalities.  It should also reaffirm federalism while clarifying constitutional responsibilities of federal and state institutions. Finally, it must prepare Somalia for a generation whose aspirations extend well beyond conflict management. And it should enable Somalia to engage confidently with regional and international partners while preserving its strategic independence and national sovereignty. None of these objectives is beyond Somalia’s reach. Indeed, they are more achievable today than they were twenty years ago. Somalia today has functioning national institutions, experienced political leaders, an increasingly capable professional class, and international partners that continue to support Somali-led solutions. The problem is no longer a lack of capacity. It is the absence of sustained political consensus. A Moment That Requires Leadership Every generation inherits its own national task. Nations experience periods of reconstruction, periods of consolidation, and moments when existing political arrangements must adapt to changing circumstances. Somalia has arrived at such a moment. The question before us is not whether the post-2004 settlement was successful. History has already answered that. Without it, Somalia would not have re-established national institutions, regained international recognition, or begun rebuilding after state collapse. The more important question is whether we now possess the wisdom to build upon those achievements rather than assume they can indefinitely sustain themselves. Political settlements survive because people continue to believe in them. When that confidence weakens, institutions weaken with it. Renewing political consensus is therefore not optional. It is essential. Having worked on Somalia’s peace process, constitutional development, democratization, and diplomacy over many years, I have learned one lesson above all others: no international partner, however committed, can substitute for Somali political leadership. Conclusion This brings me back to the diplomat’s question. “Will Somalia ever be a united country again?” My answer is yes. But unity cannot rest on sentiment alone. It must be sustained by institutions that command confidence, constitutional arrangements that enjoy broad legitimacy, and political leadership capable of placing the national interest above immediate political advantage. The generation that gathered in 2004 accomplished something remarkable. It rescued the Somali state from collapse and created the political foundations upon which today’s Somalia stands. Our responsibility is equally historic.Our task is to ensure that those foundations are strong enough to support the next chapter of Somalia’s state-building. When future generations look back on this period, they may identify three defining moments.The first established the Somali Republic in 1960. The second rebuilt the Somali state after collapse through the political settlement that emerged in 2004. The third has yet to be written. Whether it becomes the moment when Somalia renewed its political compact and completed its democratic transition—or the moment when political division allowed the gains of the past two decades to erode—depends on the choices we make today. Nations experience periods of reconstruction, periods of consolidation, and moments when existing political arrangements must adapt to changing circumstances. Somalia has arrived at such a moment. The question before us is not whether the post-2004 settlement was successful. History has already answered that. Without it, Somalia would not have re-established national institutions, regained international recognition, or begun rebuilding after state collapse. The more important question is whether we now possess the wisdom to build upon those achievements rather than assume they can indefinitely sustain themselves. Political settlements survive because people continue to believe in them. When that confidence weakens, institutions weaken with it. Renewing political consensus is therefore not optional. It is essential. Having worked on Somalia’s peace process, constitutional development, democratization, and diplomacy over many years, I have learned one lesson above all others: no international partner, however committed, can substitute for Somali political leadership. Conclusion This brings me back to the diplomat’s question. “Will Somalia ever be a united country again?” My answer is yes. But unity cannot rest on sentiment alone. It must be sustained by institutions that command confidence, constitutional arrangements that enjoy broad legitimacy, and political leadership capable of placing the national interest above immediate political advantage. The generation that gathered in 2004 accomplished something remarkable. It rescued the Somali state from collapse and created the political foundations upon which today’s Somalia stands. Our responsibility is equally historic.Our task is to ensure that those foundations are strong enough to support the next chapter of Somalia’s state-building. When future generations look back on this period, they may identify three defining moments.The first established the Somali Republic in 1960. The second rebuilt the Somali state after collapse through the political settlement that emerged in 2004. The third has yet to be written. Whether it becomes the moment when Somalia renewed its political compact and completed its democratic transition—or the moment when political division allowed the gains of the past two decades to erode—depends on the choices we make today. items.title: Golaha Wasiirrada XFS oo magacaabay Ergeyga Soomaaliya ee OIC iyo laba danjire oo cusub
items.description: Muqdisho, Soomaaliya – Golaha Wasiirrada Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa kulankoodii maanta ku ansixiyey soo-jeedinta Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibedda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ee la xiriirta magacaabista Ergeyga Soomaaliya ee Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka (OIC) iyo dalacsiinta Danjirayaal cusub. Go’aanka Golaha ayaa lagu dalacsiiyey Mudane Maxamed Cadde Mukhtaar iyo Mudane Axmed Xaaji Maxamed Caynte darajada Safiirnimo, iyadoo loo aqoonsaday Danjirayaal cusub oo matali doona Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Sidoo kale, Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa Mudane Maxamed Cabdinuur u magacaabay Ergeyga Soomaaliya u qaabilsan Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka (OIC), si uu u xoojiyo xiriirka iyo iskaashiga u dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo ururka. Magacaabista iyo dalacsiintan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ee lagu xoojinayo diblomaasiyadda dalka, korna loogu qaadayo matalaadda Soomaaliya ee heer gobol iyo heer caalami.

items.title: Soomaaliya oo si rasmi ah ugu biirtay Heshiiska Ganacsiga Xorta ah ee Afrika (AfCFTA)
items.description: Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa saxiixay ansixinta Heshiiska Ganacsiga Xorta ah ee Qaaradda Afrika (AfCFTA), kaddib markii uu hore u meel mariyey Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya. Tallaabadan ayaa dhammaystireysa ku biirista Soomaaliya ee heshiiska AfCFTA, iyadoo dalka uu hadda gudbin doono waraaqaha rasmiga ah ee ansixinta Guddiga Midowga Afrika. Wasaaradda Ganacsiga iyo Warshadaha ayaa sheegtay in ku biirista heshiiskan ay ganacsatada, maalgashadayaasha, warshadeeyayaasha, iskaashatooyinka iyo dhoofiyeyaasha Soomaaliyeed u fureyso suuq ay ku nool yihiin in ka badan 1.4 bilyan oo qof, taasoo abuureysa fursado cusub oo dhinacyada dhoofinta, maalgashiga, warshadaynta, kobaca dhaqaalaha iyo shaqo abuurka ah. Wasiirka Ganacsiga iyo Warshadaha, Jamaal Maxamed Xasan, ayaa sheegay in maanta ay tahay maalin taariikhi ah oo Soomaaliya u horseedaysa inay si buuxda uga faa’iidaysato suuqa ugu weyn ee ganacsiga xorta ah ee dunida, isla markaana sare u qaaddo tartanka iyo hal-abuurka ganacsiga gaarka loo leeyahay. Wasaaradda Ganacsiga ayaa sidoo kale sheegtay inay hoggaamin doonto hirgelinta heshiiska, iyadoo diyaarin doonta jadwalka canshuuraha, qalabka ganacsiga iyo barnaamijyo wacyigelin ah si ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed, gaar ahaan shirkadaha yaryar iyo kuwa dhexdhexaadka ah, ay uga faa’iidaystaan fursadaha uu heshiisku bixiyo. Heshiiska AfCFTA ayaa ah kan ugu weyn dunida ee ganacsiga xorta ah marka loo eego tirada dalalka ka qaybgalaya, waxaana ujeeddadiisu tahay kor u qaadidda ganacsiga gudaha Afrika, xoojinta silsiladaha wax-soo-saarka, dardargelinta warshadaynta iyo koboc dhaqaale oo waara oo qaaradda oo dhan ka hirgala.

items.title: President Hassan Sheikh Meets AFRICOM Commander for Security Talks
items.description: Mogadishu— President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud held talks with the Commander of the United States Africa Command, General Dagvin R. M. Anderson, focusing on regional security, counterterrorism efforts and strengthened defence cooperation between Somalia and the United States. The meeting reviewed the overall security situation in Somalia and the wider region, with particular emphasis on accelerating military operations against terrorist groups, enhancing coordination between the two countries and strengthening the capabilities of the Somali National Armed Forces. The two officials also discussed continued United States support for Somalia’s efforts to consolidate peace, improve national security and promote long-term stability across the region. President Hassan Sheikh expressed his appreciation to the United States Government for its sustained support and longstanding partnership with Somalia. He said cooperation between the two countries had played an important role in strengthening Somalia’s security institutions and improving the operational capabilities of the national armed forces. The President further noted that the strategic partnership between Somalia and the United States remained essential to advancing security, stability and sustainable development in Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa. General Anderson, for his part, reaffirmed the United States Government’s commitment to supporting Somalia in its fight against terrorism. He also underlined Washington’s continued support for military capacity-building, security-sector development and stronger strategic cooperation between the two countries. Both sides reiterated their commitment to maintaining close coordination and expanding security and defence cooperation in support of a more peaceful, secure and stable Somalia. items.title: Northeast Lawmakers Defect to Somaliland, Signal More Political Realignments Ahead
items.description: Hargeisa (WDN) — Five lawmakers from the North Eastern administration have arrived in Hargeisa, where they were formally welcomed by Somaliland officials after announcing their defection from the administration they previously represented. The lawmakers were initially received in the town of Gabiley before traveling to Hargeisa, where they publicly explained their decision to leave the administration in which they had served as members of the regional legislature. Speaking to local media, several of the lawmakers accused Somalia’s Federal Government of failing to genuinely support or recognize the interests of their communities. They argued that their decision followed what they described as growing dissatisfaction with Mogadishu’s policies toward their region. “We have come to realize that the greatest challenge facing our people is the Federal Government of Somalia,” one of the defecting lawmakers said during the reception. The defections have drawn considerable political attention, as they come amid heightened tensions over Somalia’s constitutional future, federal relations, and competing political visions between Mogadishu and Somaliland. Adding to the political significance of the event, Fahiima Quuje, who participated in welcoming the lawmakers, suggested that the latest defections are unlikely to be the last. “This will not be the final reception,” she said, expressing confidence that more political figures would follow the same path in the coming months. She used the Somali proverb “Faanoole fari kama qodna,” implying that actions—not rhetoric—would ultimately demonstrate the momentum behind the movement. If additional defections materialize, they could signal a broader political realignment among leaders from northern regions, potentially strengthening Somaliland’s claim that its political project continues to attract support from figures previously aligned with other administrations. Whether the latest move proves to be an isolated incident or the beginning of a wider shift remains to be seen. However, the public statements made during the reception suggest that Somaliland’s leaders expect more politicians to cross over in the near future, a development that could further reshape the political landscape in northern Somalia. items.title: Puntland oo si rasmi ah u furtay dastuurkeeda iyo qodobo xasaasi ah oo wax laga beddelayo
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Baarlamaanka Puntland ayaa si rasmi ah u guda galay dib-u-eegista iyo wax-ka-beddelka dastuurka maamulka, iyadoo qodobo muhiim ah oo la xiriira hannaanka doorashooyinka, nidaamka siyaasadda, arrimaha bulshada iyo garsoorka la horgeeyay Golaha Wakiillada si wax looga beddelo. Sida ay ogaatay Caasimada Online, qodobada dib-u-eegista lagu sameynayo waxaa ka mid ah qodobada 37, 41, 44, 47, 74, 81, 90, 113 iyo 126 ee dastuurka. Wax-ka-beddelladan ayaa lagu doonayaa in dib loogu habeeyo qaab-dhismeedka maamulka iyo hannaanka doorashooyinka. Xukuumadda Puntland ayaa soo jeedisay in doorashada xubnaha goleyaasha deegaanka iyo baarlamaanka lagu qabto hannaan qof iyo cod ah, halka Madaxweynaha, Madaxweyne ku-xigeenka iyo Guddoomiyaha baarlamaanka ay soo dooran doonaan xubnaha baarlamaanka ee ay shacabka si toos ah u soo doortaan. Haddii isbeddelladan la ansixiyo, waxaa meesha ka bixi doona qodobkii hore ee oggolaanayay in shacabka Puntland ay si toos ah u doortaan Madaxweynaha. Taas beddelkeeda, Puntland waxay u wareegi doontaa nidaam baarlamaani ah, iyadoo 66-da xildhibaan ee baarlamaanka ay yeelan doonaan awoodda ay ku soo dooranayaan madaxda sare ee maamulka. Wararka ayaa sidoo kale sheegaya in kalfadhiyada soo socda ee Baarlamaanka lagu gorfeyn doono qodobka 79-aad ee dastuurka, kaas oo ka mid ah qodobada ugu xasaasisan. Qodobkan ayaa dhigaya in Madaxweynaha Puntland uusan xilka hayn karin wax ka badan laba muddo-xileed oo isku xiga. Doodaha la xiriira qodobka 79-aad ayaa si weyn isha loogu hayaa, maadaama uu si toos ah u taabanayo mustaqbalka siyaasadeed ee Madaxweyne Saciid Cabdullaahi Deni. Sida uu qodobku hadda yahay, wuxuu xaddidayaa muddo-xileedka madaxweynaha laba jeer oo keliya, taas oo meesha ka saareysa inuu mar kale isu soo taago xilka haddii aan wax laga beddelin. Dib-u-habeynta dastuurka Puntland ayaa ku soo beegmeysa xilli Soomaaliya ay guud ahaan ka socdaan dooddo ku saabsan hannaanka doorashooyinka iyo qaab-dhismeedka dowladnimada. Isbeddelkan, haddii la meel-mariyo wuxuu ka dhigan yahay in Puntland ay dib ugu laabaneyso nidaamka baarlamaaniga ah, kaas oo Baarlamaanku soo dooranayo Madaxweynaha, halkii ay shacabka si toos ah u soo dooran lahaayeen. Arrintan ayaa la filayaa inay dhaliso dood siyaasadeed oo ballaaran gudaha maamulka Puntland, maadaama ay saameyn ku yeelaneyso hannaanka awood-qeybsiga iyo doorashooyinka mustaqbalka. Sidoo kale waxay Puntland ka dhigeysaa maamul qaadanaya nidaam u dhow kan Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya oo Madaxweynaha ay soo doortaan xubnaha baarlamaanka halkii ay shacabka si toos ah u dooran lahaayeen. items.title: Calm Returns to Galkayo as Puntland Tightens Security
items.description: Galkayo (WDN) – The security situation in the divided city of Galkayo appears to have stabilized, with both the Puntland and Galmudug sides remaining calm following days of heightened political and military tensions. According to information obtained by WardheerNews, security forces from both administrations have maintained restraint while senior security officials continue efforts to prevent any deterioration in the situation. On the Puntland side, authorities have significantly reinforced their security presence throughout the city. Security personnel have reportedly been deployed at key intersections and strategic locations, with checkpoints closely monitoring vehicle movements. Sources say the operation is intended to prevent military equipment or armed reinforcements from entering Galkayo through neighboring Galmudug-controlled territory. Officials familiar with the developments told WardheerNews that security leaders from Puntland and Galmudug have held discussions aimed at preserving peace in the city, which has long served as a symbol of cooperation despite being jointly administered by the two regional states. The talks reportedly focused on maintaining public order, preventing misunderstandings between security forces, and ensuring that political tensions do not escalate into armed confrontation. Separate reports obtained by WardheerNews indicate that on Wednesday evening a number of personnel previously aligned with the Puntland Security Force (PSF), who had been stationed near Galkayo Airport, crossed over and formally joined Puntland’s official security forces. According to local sources, 83 officers and enlisted personnel are said to have defected from the PSF during the latest development. The reported defections come only weeks after Puntland authorities seized eight armed combat vehicles reportedly operated by the PSF near Bosaso. During that earlier operation, Puntland officials also announced that 84 officers and soldiers had surrendered and joined government security forces. Although the figures have not been independently verified, the developments appear to suggest a continuing erosion of support within sections of the once-powerful force. Questions Over the Future of the PSF Political observers say the latest defections have intensified speculation over the future of the Puntland Security Force. items.title: Former President Sharif Warns Somalia Faces “Afghanistan Moment” as Opposition Sounds Alarm
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN)_ The Future Forum of Somalia has issued one of its strongest warnings yet over the country’s deepening political crisis, declaring that Somalia has entered a period of “national emergency” and urging immediate action to prevent what it described as the collapse of constitutional governance. Speaking at a press conference in Mogadishu, leaders of the opposition coalition argued that the country’s political deadlock has reached a critical point after more than two months of internationally mediated negotiations failed to produce an agreement between President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration and opposition groups. The coalition accused the Federal Government of prolonging the crisis by refusing to compromise on key constitutional and electoral issues, warning that Somalia cannot continue indefinitely under institutions whose mandates are widely disputed. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, addressing reporters, said the country was approaching a dangerous crossroads. “The situation facing Somalia today is deeply unfortunate,” Sharif said. “When the mandate of a government expires without an agreed electoral framework or political consensus on the transfer of power, the entire state enters dangerous territory.” He urged Somali leaders to learn from the country’s past political crises instead of repeating them, warning that the absence of an inclusive political settlement could have profound consequences for national stability. Sharif delivered perhaps the most striking comparison of the evening when he argued that Somalia’s political trajectory bears worrying similarities to Afghanistan before the collapse of its internationally backed government. He said two factors had ultimately destroyed Afghanistan: political disunity and corruption. According to Sharif, Somalia today is struggling with both. “Afghanistan collapsed because of the absence of political consensus and because corruption hollowed out state institutions,” he said. “Unfortunately, Somalia now faces those same dangers—and in some respects the corruption challenge is even greater.” Sharif also questioned whether the enormous international investment made in rebuilding Somalia had produced institutions resilient enough to withstand prolonged political confrontation. His remarks reflected growing concern among opposition leaders that continued political paralysis could weaken state institutions at a time when Somalia is preparing for the withdrawal of the African Union Stabilization Mission (AUSSOM). Opposition Calls for “National Salvation” Throughout the press conference, Future Forum leaders repeatedly described the current moment as one requiring what they called “national salvation.” They argued that the crisis has moved beyond an ordinary political disagreement between government and opposition and now threatens the legitimacy and continuity of the Somali state itself. The coalition urged Somalis from all political backgrounds to support an inclusive political solution capable of restoring constitutional legitimacy before the situation deteriorates further. The statement follows the opposition’s earlier proposal calling for a transitional national mechanism after negotiations with the government reportedly reached an impasse. Future Forum leaders insist that proposal is intended to preserve, rather than replace, Somalia’s state institutions until an agreed constitutional and electoral settlement can be reached. Former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Kheyre also delivered a sharp warning, arguing that Somalia’s unresolved political crisis could damage the country’s relationships with international partners. Kheyre said prolonged uncertainty risks undermining international confidence in Somalia’s institutions at a time when external security assistance remains essential. He pointed in particular to support provided to Somali security forces and the African Union mission, arguing that political instability inevitably raises concerns among donor governments about the country’s future direction. “The political uncertainty facing Somalia is no longer simply an internal matter,” Kheyre said. “It is beginning to affect our relationships with international partners.” His remarks reflected broader opposition concerns that unresolved constitutional disputes could complicate future international political, financial, and security support. The opposition continues to accuse President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration of pursuing constitutional amendments and electoral reforms without securing broad national consensus. The Federal Government, however, maintains that its constitutional and political reforms are necessary to modernize Somalia’s governance system and establish a permanent democratic electoral framework. Those competing visions have become the central fault line in Somali politics. With internationally mediated talks now appearing to have stalled, pressure is mounting on both sides to return to meaningful negotiations before the crisis deepens further. Dialogue Remains the Only Viable Path Despite the increasingly confrontational rhetoric, many political observers continue to argue that sustained dialogue remains the only realistic avenue for resolving Somalia’s constitutional impasse. A negotiated settlement would offer the best opportunity to restore confidence among political stakeholders, establish an agreed electoral roadmap, preserve institutional legitimacy, and ensure that security challenges—including the transition following AUSSOM’s planned withdrawal—are not overshadowed by internal political divisions. Without such an agreement, analysts warn, Somalia risks allowing political polarization to weaken state institutions at a moment when national unity is arguably more important than at any time in recent years. For now, the gap between the Federal Government and the opposition remains wide. Yet both sides continue to acknowledge that a political solution, rather than prolonged confrontation, will ultimately determine whether Somalia can navigate its constitutional crisis while preserving the gains made in rebuilding the state over the past two decades. items.title: Somalia sent a team with zero or limited military knowledge & experience to the Kampala summit
items.description: Somalia sent a team with zero or limited military knowledge & experience to the Kampala summit of African troop contributing countries – one of most crucial in recent years. New CDF born in 1995, never saw war. Spent most of his time behind an army Logistics desk. The three women – all family members of Somali president – equally have zero defence, military expertise. Jihan Abdullahi Hassan Jihan Hassan Sheikh Mohamud (daughter of HSM) Fadumo Aweis Mohammed That’s how Somalia takes Africa serious.     Rashid Abdi

items.title: Kadib baaqii mucaaradka DF, Uganda oo soo saartay war cusub
items.description: Kampala (Caasimada Online) – Taliyaha Guud ee Ciidamada Difaaca Uganda, Jeneraal Muhoozi Kainerugaba ayaa ku baaqay in ciidamada Howl-galka Midowga Afrika ee Soomaaliya (AUSSOM) ay sii wadaan joogitaankooda dalka. Jeneraal Muhoozi ayaa hadalkan ka jeediyay shir gaar ah oo magaalada Kampala ay ku yeesheen taliyeyaasha ciidamada dalalka ciidamada ka leh howl-galka AUSSOM. Wuxuu sheegay in sugidda amniga Soomaaliya ay tahay mas’uuliyad ay tahay in dalalka Afrika ay si wadajir ah u qaadaan. Taliyaha Ciidamada Uganda ayaa ku baaqay in la helo xal looga gudbo hoos u dhaca ku yimid taageeradii dhaqaale ee howl-galka ka heli jiray saaxiibbada caalamiga ah. Sidoo kale wuxuu ka digay in dhaqaale la’aanta hadda jirta ay si toos ah u saameyn karto howl-galka nabad-ilaalinta ee Soomaaliya, kaas oo soo maray marxalado kala duwan tan iyo markii la bilaabay sannadkii 2007, isagoo xusay in joogtaynta howl-galka ay muhiim u tahay xasiloonida Soomaaliya iyo guud ahaan amniga gobolka. Shirkan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli Xafiiska Qaramada Midoobay ee Taageerada Soomaaliya (UNSOS) uu joojiyay taageeradii dhaqaale ee uu siin jiray howl-galka AUSSOM, iyadoo howl-galka laftiisa lagu wado inuu dhammaado 31-ka December 2026 haddii aan laga gaarin go’aan cusub oo ku saabsan maalgelintiisa iyo mustaqbalkiisa. Dalalka ciidamada ka jooga Soomaaliya ayaa la filayaa inay shirka Kampala ku falanqeeyaan sidii loo heli lahaa ilo cusub oo dhaqaale, loona xaqiijin lahaa sii socoshada howl-galka, iyadoo sidoo kale diiradda la saarayo qorshaha kala guurka amniga iyo sidii ciidamada Soomaaliyeed ay si buuxda ula wareegi lahaayeen mas’uuliyadda amniga dalka. Maalinta berri ayaa la filayaa in Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, iyo madaxda dalalka ciidamada ka joogaan Soomaaliya ay kulan gaar ah ku yeeshaan magaalada Kampala. Kulankaas ayaa la filayaa in diiradda lagu saaro xaaladda amni ee Soomaaliya, caqabadaha dhaqaale ee AUSSOM iyo mustaqbalka howl-galka. Kulankan ayaa loo arkaa mid muhiim u ah jihada uu qaadan doono howl-galka AUSSOM, maadaama go’aannada ka soo baxa ay saameyn ku yeelan karaan qorshaha kala guurka amniga, taageerada caalamiga ah iyo dadaallada lagu xoojinayo awoodda Ciidamada Ammaanka Soomaaliyeed si ay ula wareegaan mas’uuliyadda amniga dalka. Si kastaba, baaqa Uganda ayaa imanaya xilli qaar kamid ah mucaaradka ay si toos ah warqad ugu direen dalalka ay ciidamadoodu qeybta ka yihiin howl-galka AUSSOM iyo taageerayaasha howl-galkaas, kaasi oo ku muujiyeen walaaca amniga Soomaaliya Warqadda oo uu direy Golaha Mustaqbalka Soomaaliyeed ayaa dalalka ay ciidamadoodu qeybta ka yihiin howl-galka AUSSOM loogu soo jeediyay in loo baahan yahay dhismaha gole KMG ah, si loo badbaadiyo sharciyadda iyo kalsoonida. Golaha ayaa dalalka Afrikaanka ah ee ciidamada ku taageera howl-galka AUSSOM ka codsaday inay sii wadaan taageeradooda inta laga helayo xal siyaasadeed oo laga gaaro khilaafka ka taagan hannaanka doorashooyinka. Sidoo kale, waxay madaxda dalalka ay ciidamadu ka joogaan Soomaaliya ka codsadeen inay taageeraan dadaal kasta oo horseedaya heshiis siyaasadeed oo loo dhan yahay, iyagoo sheegay in heshiiskaas uu yahay shuruudda ugu muhiimsan ee guusha howlgal kasta oo amni iyo xasilin ah oo ka socda gudaha Soomaaliya. items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) — Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa maanta guddoomiyey kulanka Golaha Wasiirrada Xukuumadda Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, xilli ay magaalada Muqdisho ka maqan yihiin Ra’iisul wasaare Xamza iyo ku xigeenkiisa Saalax Axmed Jaamac. Kulanka oo ahaa mid xasaasi ah ayaa waxaa looga hadlay arrimaha amniga, doorashooyinka madaxa-bannaan ee dalka ka socda iyo dimuqraadiyadda. Sidoo kale, waxaa kulanka Golaha lagu soo bandhigay warbixinno muujinayaa howlgalladii ugu dambeeyay ee ciidamada qalabka sida ay sameeyeen iyo guulaha la xaqiijiyay, kuwaas oo jab weyn soo gaarsiiyey Khawaarijta. Intaas kadib Golaha Wasiirrada Soomaaliya ayaa ansixiyey Hindise-Sharciyeedka Diiwaangalinta iyo Rukhsad-siinta Ganacsiyada iyo Heshiis is-afgarad oo u dhexeeya Agaasinka Guud ee Arrimaha Diinta ee Madaxtooyada Turkiga iyo Wasaaradda Awqaafta iyo Arrimaha Islaamka ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa dhanka kale adkeeyey in Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay sii laba jibbaari doonto dadaallada lagu xaqiijinayo amniga, xasilloonida, kobaca dhaqaalaha iyo hirgelinta qorshayaasha horumarineed ee dalka, Waxaa kale oo ay shacabka Soomaaliyeed ugu baaqeen inay sii xoojiyaan wada shaqeynta ay la leeyihiin hay’adaha dowladda, si loo gaaro Soomaaliya nabdoon, midaysan oo horumar leh. Xukuumadda Soomaaliya ayaa haatan ku howlan qorshayaal lagu dardargelinayo howlaha doorashooyinka dalka, iyada oo maanta Galmudug looga dareeray doorashooyinka isku sidaan ee golaha wakiilada iyo kuwa deegaanka oo lagu soo dooranayo hanaan qof iyo cod ah. Kulanka oo ahaa mid xasaasi ah ayaa waxaa looga hadlay arrimaha amniga, doorashooyinka madaxa-bannaan ee dalka ka socda iyo dimuqraadiyadda. Sidoo kale, waxaa kulanka Golaha lagu soo bandhigay warbixinno muujinayaa howlgalladii ugu dambeeyay ee ciidamada qalabka sida ay sameeyeen iyo guulaha la xaqiijiyay, kuwaas oo jab weyn soo gaarsiiyey Khawaarijta. Intaas kadib Golaha Wasiirrada Soomaaliya ayaa ansixiyey Hindise-Sharciyeedka Diiwaangalinta iyo Rukhsad-siinta Ganacsiyada iyo Heshiis is-afgarad oo u dhexeeya Agaasinka Guud ee Arrimaha Diinta ee Madaxtooyada Turkiga iyo Wasaaradda Awqaafta iyo Arrimaha Islaamka ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa dhanka kale adkeeyey in Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay sii laba jibbaari doonto dadaallada lagu xaqiijinayo amniga, xasilloonida, kobaca dhaqaalaha iyo hirgelinta qorshayaasha horumarineed ee dalka, Waxaa kale oo ay shacabka Soomaaliyeed ugu baaqeen inay sii xoojiyaan wada shaqeynta ay la leeyihiin hay’adaha dowladda, si loo gaaro Soomaaliya nabdoon, midaysan oo horumar leh. Xukuumadda Soomaaliya ayaa haatan ku howlan qorshayaal lagu dardargelinayo howlaha doorashooyinka dalka, iyada oo maanta Galmudug looga dareeray doorashooyinka isku sidaan ee golaha wakiilada iyo kuwa deegaanka oo lagu soo dooranayo hanaan qof iyo cod ah. items.description: Muqdisho, Soomaaliya – Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa maanta guddoomiyey shirka Golaha Wasiirrada Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, kaas oo diiradda lagu saaray arrimaha amniga, doorashooyinka madaxa-bannaan ee dalka iyo horumarinta dimuqraadiyadda. Intii uu socday kulanka, Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa lagu soo bandhigay warbixin ku saabsan howlgalladii ugu dambeeyay ee Ciidamada Qalabka Sida Soomaaliyeed ay ka fuliyeen deegaanno kala duwan. Warbixinta ayaa lagu sheegay in howlgaladaasi lagu gaarsiiyey kooxda Al-Shabaab jab xooggan, islamarkaana lagu xaqiijiyey guulo dhanka amniga ah. Sidoo kale, Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa ansixiyey Hindise-Sharciyeedka Diiwaangelinta iyo Rukhsad-siinta Ganacsiyada, kaas oo lagu xoojinayo nidaamka diiwaangelinta iyo sharciyeynta ganacsiyada dalka. Dhanka kale, Golaha ayaa meelmariyey Heshiis Is-afgarad (MoU) oo u dhexeeya Agaasinka Guud ee Arrimaha Diinta ee Madaxtooyada Turkiga iyo Wasaaradda Awqaafta iyo Arrimaha Islaamka ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, kaas oo lagu xoojinayo iskaashiga labada dhinac ee arrimaha diinta iyo wacyigelinta bulshada.

items.title: Red Sea Security, Berbera Access: Geopolitical realities propelling Somaliland recognition
items.description: Red Sea Security, Berbera Access: Geopolitical realities propelling Somaliland recognition A ship docked at Berbera, a port located in Somaliland. (Photo: Social Media) Addis Abeba — For more than three decades, Somaliland has presented one of the most striking anomalies in contemporary international politics. It satisfies all classical criteria of statehood under the Montevideo Convention . It possesses clearly demarcated borders inherited from the former British Somaliland Protectorate, a permanent population, functioning democratic institutions, effective territorial governance, and the capacity to enter into international relations. Nevertheless, despite this undisputed record of functional sovereignty, Somaliland has historically remained excluded from formal diplomatic recognition by the United Nations and the majority of sovereign state ​For years, Somaliland’s status was treated primarily as a narrow question of regional diplomacy and international law, heavily filtered through the African Union’s deep-seated anxieties regarding border alterations. Today, however, that status is inextricably linked to a much larger global crisis: securing the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait amid proxy warfare, asymmetric maritime insecurity, and intensifying competition among global powers. ​The fundamental question facing policymakers in Washington, Brussels, Addis Abeba, and across African capitals is no longer whether Somaliland’s political aspirations should be recognized in theory. The defining question of our current geopolitical era is whether the international community can afford to continue ignoring a stable, democratic actor positioned directly at the crossroads of global commerce. Securing Bab al-Mandeb in era of maritime insecurity Few maritime passages carry greater geopolitical weight than the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. This narrow choke point, connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean, acts as the maritime jugular linking East Asian manufacturing hubs and Persian Gulf energy exporters to European markets via the Suez Canal route. Measuring barely twenty-nine kilometers at its narrowest expanse, the strait is as vital as it is vulnerable. ​The systemic fragility of this corridor became starkly visible following the escalation of attacks on commercial vessels by Yemen’s Houthi movement. As detailed in ongoing trade security assessments by UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) , sustained disruptions to Red Sea transit routes forced major international container lines to abandon the Suez route entirely in favor of rerouting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope. ​This massive global diversion adds thousands of nautical miles to Asia–Europe transit voyages. It extends delivery timelines by weeks, drives up maritime insurance premiums to unprecedented levels, increases global fuel consumption, and heavily inflates freight rates. What began as a localized spillover from Middle Eastern conflicts has crystallized into a structural vulnerability for global trade. The ongoing crisis has underscored a fundamental axiom of twenty-first-century geopolitics: maritime security is absolutely inseparable from global economic stability. ​The Red Sea crisis cannot be understood in isolation. It reflects a much broader and more dangerous contest over regional hegemony, asymmetric proxy warfare, and control over critical maritime passages. Iran’s supply of advanced anti-ship ballistic missiles , uncrewed aerial vehicles, and uncrewed surface vessels to Houthi forces fundamentally expanded Tehran’s capacity to project power well beyond the Persian Gulf. By establishing a dense threat matrix at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, Tehran and its proxies demonstrated how non-state networks can effectively disrupt international shipping lanes and directly challenge traditional carrier strike groups. Intelligence reports have further documented the emergence of a cross-gulf smuggling pipeline, where advanced weaponry and drone components are trafficked from Houthi-controlled Yemen across the Gulf of Aden to Al-Shabaab insurgents in south-central Somalia. ​In response to this disruption, naval coalitions led by the United States, alongside complementary missions deployed by the European Union, launched extensive defense and interception operations . While guided-missile destroyers and carrier-based aircraft have successfully dealt with hundreds of incoming threats, military planners are increasingly realizing that defensive naval patrols and occasional air strikes only tackle the symptoms of maritime insecurity, not the underlying issues. Control of strategic waterways is no longer simply a regional concern—it has become a direct test of the resilience of the international rules-based maritime order.” ​Naval ships in open waters face challenges like limited visibility, supply issues, and tired crews. Keeping aircraft carriers deployed all the time and using expensive air defense weapons against cheap, mass-produced drones isn’t practical or affordable in the long run. To achieve lasting maritime security, we need dependable land-based partnerships, logistics support, and ongoing monitoring of the coastlines near Yemen. Washington’s strategic imperative ​Inside Washington policy circles, the crisis in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait has triggered a profound re-evaluation of American force posture and strategic partnerships in the Horn of Africa. For decades, the United States has relied almost exclusively on Camp Lemonnier in neighboring Djibouti as its principal operational hub in the region. However, this single-point-of-failure reliance has introduced growing tactical and strategic risks. ​American forces in Djibouti now operate under the direct gaze of China’s first overseas naval base , located just miles away. In a scenario marked by escalating great-power competition, concentrating American military resupply, intelligence collection, and counter-terrorism assets in a congested, heavily spied-upon enclave creates unacceptable operational vulnerabilities. ​This strategic paradox explains why military leadership at U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) and defense strategists have increasingly turned their focus toward Somaliland’s deep-water Port of Berbera and its accompanying four-kilometer military-grade airfield. Berbera offers the United States an unrivaled, low-risk alternative for forward logistics, maritime domain awareness, and rapid response operations directed against Houthi threat nodes across the Gulf of Aden. ​Moreover, Washington’s calculation extends beyond immediate naval defense to encompass global supply-chain security and critical mineral resilience. Somaliland sits atop significant, unexploited reserves of rare earth elements, coltan, and lithium—resources that are indispensable to modern defense manufacturing and green technology. As the United States seeks to diversify its supply chains away from near-monopolistic competitors, establishing formal economic and security agreements with Hargeisa offers a direct pipeline to critical minerals guaranteed by a stable local government capable of securing its own territory. ​Legislative momentum in the U.S. Congress, reflected in proposed bills such as the Republic of Somaliland Independence Act and strategic provisions within National Defense Authorization Acts, underscores a growing bipartisan consensus. Lawmakers recognize that formalizing security cooperation with Somaliland delivers a fully functioning, democratic counter-terrorism and maritime security partner without the immense nation-building costs historically associated with interventions in Mogadishu. By securing basing access, intelligence cooperation, and mineral rights in Somaliland, Washington can simultaneously degrade Houthi-Al-Shabaab smuggling networks and fortify its long-term posture across the Red Sea. When geography meets governance ​This strategic reality highlights why Somaliland’s geography is impossible to ignore. Occupying more than eight hundred and fifty kilometers of coastline along the southern shore of the Gulf of Aden, Somaliland sits directly across from Yemen, offering direct oversight of the maritime approaches to the Bab al-Mandeb. ​At the geographic and economic center of this coastline lies the Port of Berbera. Developed through massive capital investments by global logistics operator DP World , Berbera has been transformed from a modest regional harbor into a state-of-the-art, deep-water container terminal. Accompanied by a modernized four-kilometer airfield and expanding special economic zones, the Berbera Corridor provides high-capacity transport links connecting the Gulf of Aden directly to the rapidly growing East African hinterland ​Beyond physical infrastructure, Somaliland’s primary strategic asset is its enduring political stability. Following the total collapse of the military dictatorship in Mogadishu in 1991, Somaliland did not descend into the decades of factional warfare that plagued the rest of the region. Instead, it pursued internal, clan-based reconciliation through traditional assemblies, locally known as the Shir. This indigenous peacebuilding process laid the groundwork for a constitutional democracy featuring executive, legislative, and judicial branches, alongside a biometric voter registration system that has facilitated multiple competitive elections and peaceful transfers of executive power. ​In stark contrast to neighboring regions in south-central Somalia—which continue to struggle against persistent, lethal insurgencies led by the Al-Shabaab terror network while relying heavily on the presence of foreign peacekeeping missions—Somaliland has secured its territory and coastal waters independently. Its coast guard serves as the primary physical buffer preventing the Gulf of Aden from becoming a completely unchecked transit route for proxy proliferation. Re-Framing Legal Reality: State continuity over secession ​Critics of Somaliland’s diplomatic aspirations frequently frame its pursuit of recognition as a secessionist effort, warning that it risks destabilizing the Horn of Africa or violating deeply held African Union principles regarding the sanctity of inherited colonial boundaries. However, careful legal scholarship and consistent reporting by regional policy platforms like Addis Standard reveal that Somaliland’s claim is firmly rooted in state continuity and international legal precedent. ​On 26 June, 1960, the former British Somaliland Protectorate received full independence from Great Britain. Upon this declaration, the sovereign state of Somaliland was promptly recognized by more than thirty-five sovereign nations, including permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. Days later, on July 1, 1960, Somaliland voluntarily entered a political union with the newly independent former Italian-administered Trust Territory to form the Somali Republic. ​Crucially, legal researchers emphasize that the formal Act of Union designed to legally bind the two territories was never ratified through the required parallel constitutional procedures. When Somaliland officially reasserted its sovereignty in May 1991 following the collapse of the central regime, it did not draw new lines on a map. Rather, it reclaimed the precise, internationally recognized borders of its 1960 independence. ​This legal positioning aligns directly with the foundational principles of the African Union Constitutive Act , specifically the doctrine of uti possidetis juris , which mandates strict respect for borders existing at the time of national independence. The African Union’s own official Fact-Finding Mission in 2005 explicitly noted that Somaliland’s case was historically unique and self-justified, concluding that its recognition would not open a Pandora’s box of unlawful secession across the African continent. Great power realignment, cost of diplomatic inertia ​While Western capitals have historically adhered to a legacy “ One Somalia ” policy centered exclusively on Mogadishu, rival global and regional powers have aggressively adapted to operational realities along the Red Sea basin. The scramble for influence in the Horn of Africa has fundamentally altered the region’s security architecture. ​China established its very first overseas military facility in neighboring Djibouti, positioning heavily armed naval assets directly adjacent to major international shipping lanes while simultaneously embedding itself deeply into the region’s economy through extensive Belt and Road infrastructure investments. ​Turkey, pursuing a robust, forward-leaning African policy, constructed its largest overseas military training facility in Mogadishu. Ankara has secured highly lucrative, long-term management agreements for Somalia’s primary seaport and airport, effectively anchoring its geopolitical influence in the Indian Ocean. ​Egypt has also forcefully entered the arena, signing sweeping formal defense and intelligence agreements with the government in Mogadishu. Cairo has recently deployed military personnel and heavy equipment to Somalia, a maneuver widely understood as a strategy to project power into Ethiopia’s backyard and counterbalance Addis Abeba’s influence amid the deeply entrenched geopolitical standoff over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam GERD). For Washington, engaging Somaliland is no longer a matter of peripheral diplomacy—it is a practical necessity for force protection, supply-chain resilience, and Red Sea deterrence.” ​For Washington and European nations, adhering strictly to diplomatic status quo policies while competitors actively build deep infrastructure and security partnerships on the ground creates severe strategic vulnerabilities. Strategic vacuums along the world’s most critical waterways are rarely left empty; they are inevitably filled by actors prepared to recognize and leverage operational realities. MoU with Ethiopia, Israeli pragmatism ​The strategic landscape of the Horn shifted dramatically at the dawn of 2024 when Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Somaliland President Muse Bihi Abdi signed a historic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) . Under this framework, landlocked Ethiopia—a rapidly growing nation of over one hundred and twenty million people—sought to secure a long-term lease of coastal territory along Somaliland’s Gulf of Aden shore for both commercial and naval access. In exchange, the agreement outlined a pathway for Ethiopia to conduct a formal evaluation leading toward international recognition of Somaliland’s statehood, alongside offering Hargeisa an equity stake in major Ethiopian state-owned enterprises. ​Although this agreement provoked intense diplomatic opposition from Mogadishu and Cairo, the underlying economic and strategic logic remains undeniable. Being landlocked presents an existential, long-term economic bottleneck for Ethiopia, which currently relies almost entirely on Djibouti’s ports for its vast maritime trade. Developing the Berbera Corridor provides Ethiopia with desperately needed port redundancy, significantly lowers transit logistics costs, and deeply integrates regional infrastructure across the Horn of Africa. ​This momentum of operational pragmatism reached another historic milestone in December 2025, when Israel became the first United Nations member state to formally and officially recognize Somaliland . Driven by the urgent need to counter Iranian proxy networks and secure a forward intelligence and logistics node overlooking the Red Sea, Jerusalem bypassed decades of diplomatic gridlock. By subsequently inaugurating a Somaliland embassy in Jerusalem in 2026, Israel demonstrated that the integration of the Horn of Africa into the broader Middle Eastern security architecture is not just a theoretical concept but an active reality. ​These developments signal a definitive shift away from legacy naval postures. Traditional security frameworks relied heavily on concentrated, vulnerable bases in Djibouti and ship-based radar systems with inherent horizon limits. The emerging paradigm—an operational recognition framework—favors diversified coastal nodes, ground-based over-the-horizon radar, direct naval resupply at modernized deep-water ports like Berbera, and formalized defense pacts that anchor maritime security in stable, land-based governance. Conclusion: Aligning global policy with strategic necessity ​The Red Sea is no longer a peripheral maritime passage; it is the primary arena of twenty-first-century global geopolitical competition. The security of this corridor will inevitably dictate the resilience of global trade routes, the stability of energy markets, and the future of naval strategy for decades to come. ​Within this volatile environment, the Republic of Somaliland occupies a geographic and political position that the international community can no longer afford to treat as invisible. It combines an indispensable location along the Gulf of Aden with over three decades of internal stability, democratic continuity, and highly effective territorial governance. ​Formal international engagement with Somaliland—whether through full diplomatic recognition, structured bilateral defense pacts, or deep economic integration—is no longer merely a gesture of democratic solidarity. It is an absolute, unavoidable practical necessity for securing the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. ​International diplomacy must choose between stubbornly preserving outdated assumptions that fail to reflect the realities of the Horn of Africa or adapting to the operational facts on the ground. Strategic necessity and democratic governance have perfectly aligned on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. Securing the global maritime order effectively requires recognizing, empowering, and partnering with the very actors who actively maintain stability along its most critical shores. AS Editor’s Note : Adam Daud Ahmed is a political and security analyst specializing in the Horn of Africa, with a focus on democracy, regional geopolitics, and counterterrorism. He can be reached at aadan7333@hotmail.com

Under this framework, landlocked Ethiopia—a rapidly growing nation of over one hundred and twenty million people—sought to secure a long-term lease of coastal territory along Somaliland’s Gulf of Aden shore for both commercial and naval access. In exchange, the agreement outlined a pathway for Ethiopia to conduct a formal evaluation leading toward international recognition of Somaliland’s statehood, alongside offering Hargeisa an equity stake in major Ethiopian state-owned enterprises. ​Although this agreement provoked intense diplomatic opposition from Mogadishu and Cairo, the underlying economic and strategic logic remains undeniable. Being landlocked presents an existential, long-term economic bottleneck for Ethiopia, which currently relies almost entirely on Djibouti’s ports for its vast maritime trade. Developing the Berbera Corridor provides Ethiopia with desperately needed port redundancy, significantly lowers transit logistics costs, and deeply integrates regional infrastructure across the Horn of Africa. ​This momentum of operational pragmatism reached another historic milestone in December 2025, when Israel became the first United Nations member state to formally and officially recognize Somaliland . Driven by the urgent need to counter Iranian proxy networks and secure a forward intelligence and logistics node overlooking the Red Sea, Jerusalem bypassed decades of diplomatic gridlock. By subsequently inaugurating a Somaliland embassy in Jerusalem in 2026, Israel demonstrated that the integration of the Horn of Africa into the broader Middle Eastern security architecture is not just a theoretical concept but an active reality. ​These developments signal a definitive shift away from legacy naval postures. Traditional security frameworks relied heavily on concentrated, vulnerable bases in Djibouti and ship-based radar systems with inherent horizon limits. The emerging paradigm—an operational recognition framework—favors diversified coastal nodes, ground-based over-the-horizon radar, direct naval resupply at modernized deep-water ports like Berbera, and formalized defense pacts that anchor maritime security in stable, land-based governance. Conclusion: Aligning global policy with strategic necessity ​The Red Sea is no longer a peripheral maritime passage; it is the primary arena of twenty-first-century global geopolitical competition. The security of this corridor will inevitably dictate the resilience of global trade routes, the stability of energy markets, and the future of naval strategy for decades to come. ​Within this volatile environment, the Republic of Somaliland occupies a geographic and political position that the international community can no longer afford to treat as invisible. It combines an indispensable location along the Gulf of Aden with over three decades of internal stability, democratic continuity, and highly effective territorial governance. ​Formal international engagement with Somaliland—whether through full diplomatic recognition, structured bilateral defense pacts, or deep economic integration—is no longer merely a gesture of democratic solidarity. It is an absolute, unavoidable practical necessity for securing the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. ​International diplomacy must choose between stubbornly preserving outdated assumptions that fail to reflect the realities of the Horn of Africa or adapting to the operational facts on the ground. Strategic necessity and democratic governance have perfectly aligned on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. Securing the global maritime order effectively requires recognizing, empowering, and partnering with the very actors who actively maintain stability along its most critical shores. items.title: Baaq ka soo baxay madasha indheer’garadka Somaliland  (SIO)
items.description: BAAQ KA SOO BAXAY MADASHA INDHEER-GARADKA SOMALILAND (SIO) Ku: Xukuumadda Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, Ganacsatada Qaranka, Hay’adaha Samafalka, Qurba-joogta iyo Guud ahaan Shacabka Somaliland Ujeeddo: Kordhinta Adeegyada Sifaynta Kelyaha (Dialysis) iyo Taageerada Bukaannada Kelyaha Madasha Indheer-garadka Somaliland (SIO) waxay si qoto dheer uga damqanaysaa xaaladda ay ku sugan yihiin bukaannada kelyaha ee maalin kasta u baahan adeegga sifaynta dhiigga (Dialysis). Waa xaalad taabanaysa qoysas badan, isla markaana u baahan iskaashi qaran iyo tallaabo degdeg ah. Sidaas awgeed, Madashu waxay ugu baaqaysaa: 1. Xukuumadda Somaliland inay mudnaanta siiso ballaadhinta adeegyada sifaynta kelyaha, lana kordhiyo tirada mishiinnada Dialysis ee dalka, si bukaan kasta u helo adeeg ku filan oo waqtigiisa ku habboon. 2. Ganacsatada iyo shirkadaha waaweyn inay qayb ka noqdaan masuuliyadda bulshada (Corporate Social Responsibility), iyagoo gacan ka geysanaya iibinta iyo maalgelinta mishiinnada Dialysis iyo qalabka kale ee caafimaadka. 3. Hay’adaha samafalka iyo deeq-bixiyeyaasha inay mudnaan siiyaan taageerada adeegyada sifaynta kelyaha, maadaama ay badbaadin karaan nolosha boqollaal qof. 4. Qurba-joogta Somaliland inay ka qayb qaataan ololaha lagu horumarinayo adeegyada caafimaadka, gaar ahaan kuwa la xidhiidha bukaannada kelyaha. 5. Shacabka Somaliland inay muujiyaan isku-duubni, naxariis iyo is-garab-istaag, una gurmadaan walaalahooda la ildaran xanuunkan. Farriinta Madasha Xusuusnow: Maanta waxaad ku naaloon kartaa caafimaad, laakiin berri adiga ama qof aad jeceshahay ayaa u baahan kara isla adeeggaas. Caafimaadku waa nimco Alle bixiyo, xanuunkuna waa imtixaan qof kasta ku iman kara. Sidaa darteed, aynu dhisno bulsho isu naxariisata oo aan cidna ka tegin marka ay dhibaato caafimaad la kulanto. Madasha Indheer-garadka Somaliland (SIO) waxay ku baaqaysaa in arrintan loo arko waajib qaran iyo masuuliyad wadajir ah, si loo badbaadiyo nafaha muwaadiniinta loona xaqiijiyo in qof kasta helo daryeel caafimaad oo sharaf leh. “Badbaadinta hal naf waa badbaadinta bulsho dhan.” Mohamed Ali Guddoomiye Madasha Indheer-garadka Somaliland (SIO) Hargeysa – Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland

items.title: Xildhibaannadii ka goostay maamulka Waqooyi Bari oo gaaray Hargeysa + Video
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Afar kamid ah Xildhibaannadii dhawaan iska casilay Baarlamaanka Waqooyi Bari ayaa maanta gaaray magaalada Hargeysa ee caasimada Somaliland, halkaas oo si weyn loogu soo dhaweeyay. Xildhibaannadan oo shaaca ka qaaday inay tanaasuleen aragtidii Soomaali wayn ayaa ugu dambeyn dib ugu laabtay Somaliland oo soo dhaweyn heerkoodu sarreeyo u sameysay. Mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan maamulka fadhigiisu yahay Hargeysa oo ay ugu horreeyaan Guddoomiyaha Golaha Wakiilada, Yaasiin Faratoon iyo Wasiirka Arrimaha Gudaha Cabdalle Maxamed Carab (Sandheere) ayaa xildhibaannada kusoo dhaweeyay xadka labada gobol ee Maroodi Jeex iyo Gabiley, kadibna waxaa loo galbiyay caasimada Hargeysa. Mid kamid ah Xildhibaannada iska dhiibay Somaliland oo hadal siiyay warbaahinta ayaa sheegay inay soo guryo noqdeen, wuxuuna sidoo kale shaaca ka qaaday inay soo ogaadeen in dhibaatada socoto ay ka timid dhanka magaalada Muqdisho, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Runtii waxaan ogaanay in dhibaatada ugu badan ee dadkeena haysato inay uga timid Xamar, waana fiicneyd inaanu soo ogaano” ayuu yiri mid kamid Xildhibaannada lagu soo dhaweeyay magaalada Hargeysa. Dhankeeda waxaa goobta ka hadashay Fahiima Yuusuf Quuje oo iyadana dhawaan u goosatay Somaliland, taas oo mar kale u gacan haatisay saaxibadeeda weli ku jira maamulka Waqooyi Bari oo ay ugu baaqday inay isaga soo baxaan, dibna ugu soo laabtaan maamulkooda. “Waxaan leeyahay faanoole fari kama qodna teamkan uguma dambeynayaan waa imaan doonaan saaxibo ka badan dadka waa in loogu tegayo meeshoodii iyo gobolkoodii iyo kaxeyn doonta calanka nabadda ee Somaliland,” ayay tiri Fahiima Quuje. Goosashada Xildhibaannadan ayaa kusoo aaday, iyada oo maanta shacabka Waqooyi Bari iyo madaxdooda ay u dabaal-degayaan Sanad-guurada 1aad ee aas aaska maamulkaasi, iyada oo si gaar ah loogu xusayo hirgelintii himiladii shacabka ee ku dhisnayd midnimo, dowladnimo iyo horumar. The post Xildhibaannadii ka goostay maamulka Waqooyi Bari oo gaaray Hargeysa + Video appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Mucaaradka oo fursad ka dhex raadinaya Xasan & Xamza
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Cadaaladda iyo Arrimaha Dastuurka Xasan Macallin ayaa sheegay in qaar kamid ah siyaasiyiinta mucaaradka ay isku dayayaan inay abuuraan khilaaf u dhexeeya Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh iyo Ra’iisul wasaarihiisa, si ay uga dhex faa’iideystaan. Xasan Macallin oo ka qayb-galay kulan xalay ka dhacay hoteelka Jaziira ee magaalada Muqdisho ayaa shaaca ka qaaday in xubnaha mucaaradka ay jeclaan lahaayeen inay is khilaafaan Xasan Sheekh iyo Xamza Cabdi Barre, kadibna khilaafkooda la geeyo dalka dibaddiisa, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Waxaa jeclaan lahayn inay Madaxweyne Xasan iyo Ra’iisul wasaare Xamza is khilaafaan, kadibna dalka dibadiisa aan gayno, dad ayaa sidaas dhahaayey waa la idiinka diiday mucaaradow,” ayuu yiri Wasiir Xasan Macallin. Sidoo kale, wuxuu tilmaamay in laga soo gudbay dhaqankaas, isla markaana Madaxweynaha iyo Ra’iisul wasaaraha ay yihiin saaxibo isku aragti ah oo hal meel ku wada dalka, sidaas daraadeed wuxuu mucaaradka ugu baaqay haddii ay dhaliil jirto inay usoo bandhigaan si wanaagsan oo la fahmi karo. “Xukuumadda midnimadeeda, wadajirkeeda iyo hore u socodkeeda waa la bogaadiyaa waxaa la dhaliilaa meelaha ay dhaliilaha ka leedahay, balse la yaqaano waxa aad dhaliileyso,” ayuu mar kale yiri Wasiirka Cadaaladda. Waxaa kale oo uu kusii daray “Mucaaradnimo wax wanaagsan waayay waa dastuuri, laakiin mucaaradnimada sidaan haloo dhaamo oo yaan mucaaradnimada la gayn dalka dibaddiisa”. Hadalkan ayaa kusoo aadayo xilli xasaasi ah, isla markaana dalka uu wajahayo marxalad adag oo kala guur ah, iyadoo wel la’isku hayo hannaanka guud ee doorashooyinka iyo wax ka beddalka lagu sameeyay dastuurka KMG ah. Si kastaba, siyaasiyiinta mucaaradka ayaa inta badan dowladda ku dhaliila hannaanka ay u maareyneyso arrimaha siyaasadda, waxayna ku doodayaan inuu dhammaaday muddo xileedkii sharciga ahaa ee hay’adaha dowladda. The post Mucaaradka oo fursad ka dhex raadinaya Xasan & Xamza appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: madaxweynaha Koonfur Sudan Oo Beddelay Guddoomiyihii Baanka Dhexe
items.description: Madaxweynaha Koonfur Sudan , Salva Kiir , ayaa xilka ka qaaday guddoomiyihii baanka dhexe ee dalka Johnny Ohisa, isagoo bedelkiisii u magacaabay Addis Ababa Othow oo horey xilkaas u soo qabtay intii u dhaxaysay Juun iyo Noofambar 2025 . Go’aankan ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli uu Madaxweynuhu sameeyay isbadalo ballaaran oo ka dhaca jagooyinka sare ee dowladdiisa, kuwaas oo falanqeeyayaashu sheegayaan inay muujinayaan dadaal lagu xoojinayo awoodda iyadoo jirto hubanti la’aan ku saabsan mustaqbalka hoggaanka dalka. Go’aankan ayaa muhiim u ah sababtoo ah waxa uu ka dhigan yahay isbadal ku yimaada jagooyinka maamulka dhaqaalaha dalka, iyadoo dhaqaalaha Koonfur Sudan uu wajahayo cadaadis sii kordhaya oo ka yimaada hoos u dhaca dakhliga saliidda, yaraanta lacagta caddaanka ee soo noqnoqota, sicir-bararka sare, iyo qiimo-dhaca lacagta. Dakhliga saliidda ayaa si weyn hoos ugu dhacay kadib markii dhawaaq uu soo gaaray tuubada saliidda ee u dhexaysa Koonfur Sudan iyo Suudaan, taasoo keentay in dhaqaalahu uu foosha xumaado . Ohisa, oo ah dhaqaaleyahan soo noqnoqday jagada guddoomiyaha baanka dhexe, ayaa dib loo magacaabay horraantii sanadkan kadib markii uu horey u soo qabtay xilkan laba jeer oo kala duwan. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, xilligan ma uusan caddayn sababta uu xilka looga qaaday . Koonfur Sudan ayaa sii wadata caqabado dhaqaale oo ba’an oo ay ka mid yihiin hoos u dhaca soo gelitaanka lacagaha qalaad, cadaadiska maaliyadeed, iyo sicir-bararka aad u sarreeya. Falanqeeyayaashu waxay sheegayaan in isbadalada joogtada ah ee jagooyinka sare ay kordhin karaan hubanti la’aanta siyaasadeed iyo dhaqaale, taasoo saameyn ku yeelan karta kalsoonida maalgashadayaasha iyo hay’adaha caalamiga ah . The post madaxweynaha Koonfur Sudan Oo Beddelay Guddoomiyihii Baanka Dhexe first appeared on Radio Dalsan .

Go’aankan ayaa muhiim u ah sababtoo ah waxa uu ka dhigan yahay isbadal ku yimaada jagooyinka maamulka dhaqaalaha dalka, iyadoo dhaqaalaha Koonfur Sudan uu wajahayo cadaadis sii kordhaya oo ka yimaada hoos u dhaca dakhliga saliidda, yaraanta lacagta caddaanka ee soo noqnoqota, sicir-bararka sare, iyo qiimo-dhaca lacagta. Dakhliga saliidda ayaa si weyn hoos ugu dhacay kadib markii dhawaaq uu soo gaaray tuubada saliidda ee u dhexaysa Koonfur Sudan iyo Suudaan, taasoo keentay in dhaqaalahu uu foosha xumaado . Ohisa, oo ah dhaqaaleyahan soo noqnoqday jagada guddoomiyaha baanka dhexe, ayaa dib loo magacaabay horraantii sanadkan kadib markii uu horey u soo qabtay xilkan laba jeer oo kala duwan. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, xilligan ma uusan caddayn sababta uu xilka looga qaaday . Koonfur Sudan ayaa sii wadata caqabado dhaqaale oo ba’an oo ay ka mid yihiin hoos u dhaca soo gelitaanka lacagaha qalaad, cadaadiska maaliyadeed, iyo sicir-bararka aad u sarreeya. Falanqeeyayaashu waxay sheegayaan in isbadalada joogtada ah ee jagooyinka sare ay kordhin karaan hubanti la’aanta siyaasadeed iyo dhaqaale, taasoo saameyn ku yeelan karta kalsoonida maalgashadayaasha iyo hay’adaha caalamiga ah . items.title: Maxaa looga hadlay kulan maanta ee golaha wasiirrada Koonfur Galbeed ?
items.description: Baydhabo ( Raxanreeb Online) Hoggaamiyaha dowlad goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa guddoomiyey kulanka golaha Wasiirrada Koonfur Galbeed, kaas oo diiradda lagu saaray adkaynta amniga, dardargelinta mashaariicda horumarineed iyo xaaladaha bani’aadannimo ee ka jira deegaannada Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed. Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa warbixinno ka dhageystay Wasiirka Amniga, kaasi oo faahfaahin ka bixiyey xaaladda guud ee amniga, guulaha laga gaaray sugidda nabadgelyada iyo qorshayaasha lagu sii xoojinayo la dagaallanka kooxaha amniga qalqal geliya, si loo xaqiijiyo nabad waarta iyo xasillooni ay bulshada ku noolaato. Sidoo kale shirka waxaa lagu lafaguray dardargelinta hirgelinta mashaariicda horumarineed ee dowladda, iyadoo xoogga la saaray mashaariicda adeegyada bulshada, kaabeyaasha dhaqaalaha iyo sidii loo hubin lahaa in si hufan loogu fuliyo bulshada deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed. Golaha wasiirrada ayaa si qoto dheer uga hadlay arrimaha bani’aadannimada, gaar ahaan gurmadka loo fidinayo bulshada ay saameeyeen abaaraha, isbeddelka cimilada iyo duruufaha kale ee bani’aadannimo. Golaha ayaa adkeeyey muhiimadda iskaashiga dowladda, hay’adaha samafalka iyo saaxiibada caalamiga ah si loo xoojiyo taageerada loo fidinayo shacabka nugul. Ugu dambeyn Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa faray dhammaan wasaaradaha iyo hay’adaha dowladda inay laba jibbaaraan dadaallada lagu xaqiijinayo amni waara, horumar muuqda iyo adeegyo tayo leh oo si toos ah u taabanaya nolosha bulshada, isagoo xusay in Dowladda ay mudnaan gaar ah siinayso horumarinta adeegyada dadweynaha iyo xoojinta dowladnimada.
